I can totally relate to these two people because
their experiences are similar to mine. Like Yuna, I
started this journaling during my first year of high
school. At that time, I felt lost, stressed, and unsure
about the future, and it wasn’t easy for me to
ⓐconcentrate. When I first tried writing three daily
pages, I didn’t expect to stick to it. But I did, and
it changed my life! ⓑReleasing my feelings onto
paper every morning helped relieve my emotional
tension. I gained more inner peace, which improved
my schoolwork performance. Like David, I asked
many questions, for instance, “Why was I so angry
yesterday?” “Why are things less fun these days?”
Then, I started raising more challenging ones: “What
could make me happier right now?” “What is my
ideal future? Can I reach it? How?”
(A)[Answer / Answering] these questions showed
me what kind of person I was and what my needs,
values, ⓒpassions, and talents were. More
importantly, I came to know what I truly wanted! I
remembered my childhood dreams of being a
writer, songwriter, and radio host. Gradually,
ⓓvague ideas became clear plans. Years later, here
I am, a successful podcaster and vlogger! I’ve also
published a book and a music album. My morning
pages, which I still write every day, (B)[having given
/ have given] me the drive and ideas to achieve
these aims.
Dear ⓔsubscribers, will you try writing your
morning pages, too? You never know (C)[that /
what] creative energy or ideas you have until you
start exploring. Don’t be a perfectionist, though. If
you miss a few days, simply open your notebook
and start again! The ultimate aim is to improve
your mental health and help you lead a happier,
more creative life.

ⓑ: to make something available to the public,typically for the first time, such as aproduct, movie, or piece of music

ⓓ: not clearly or explicitly stated or defined;unclear in meaning or intention

Welcome to my channel Good Habits! This is
Regan, your podcast host. Today, I’m going to talk
about a way of starting the day that many people,
including me, find enormously (A)[useless / useful].
It’s a kind of journaling called “the morning pages.”
ⓐThere is no age which it is too late to forming
this habit. I started eight years ago as a high
school student, and that’s why today’s episode is
especially for my teenage subscribers.
The morning pages are three pages of “free
writing,” ideally done first thing in the morning. The
concept is simple. Get up every morning, pick up a
pen and a notebook, and write whatever crosses
your mind until you have filled three pages.
The technique was originally developed to help
writers and artists (B)[overcome / deteriorate] a loss
of creativity, but anybody can use it to create a
better life.
There is no right or wrong way to write your
morning pages, but there are two rules. First, don’t
judge your writing as good or bad. These pages
are meant to be a “brain cleansing,” so don’t worry
about writing correctly. Second, keep your writing
completely (C)[public / private]. ⓑIt is important of
you write freely and honestly. You’re even advised
not to read your writing yourself for weeks.

(A)

(C)
solution: 정답은 ② 이다. (해설 없음)

다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

Forming a new habit is not easy, especially in the
beginning. Here are five ways to start a habit that
really sticks. First, start small. Don’t try to do too
much, too quickly. A habit is formed through
repetition, so make the change easier to repeat.
Second, make your goal (A)[specific / abstract].
Don’t say, “I’ll meditate regularly.” Say, “I’ll meditate
for five minutes each day.” This works even better if
you combine your new habit with an existing one,
for example, “After brushing my teeth in the
morning, I’ll meditate for five minutes.” When your
fixed habit becomes a cue for action, your new
habit is more likely to stick. Third, make it
(B)[tedious / attractive]. Pair your new change with
what you love. You could listen to your favorite
piece of calming music while meditating. Fourth,
track your progress. Mark a calendar with an X
every time you finish something. Seeing the
progress gives you a sense of achievement and
helps you keep going. Fifth, be (C)[flexible /
uncompromising]. Forming a new habit takes time.
If you find that your progress has stopped for any
reason, just pick up where you left off.
(A)
(B)
(C)
solution: (A) ‘나는 규칙적으로 명상을 할 거야.’ 라고 말하지 말고 ‘나는 매일 5분씩 명상을 할 거야.’로 말하라는 내용이 이어지며 더 구체적으로 새로운 습관을 기존의 습관과 결합하여 ‘아침에 이 를 닦은 후 5분간 명상을 할 거야.’라고 말하면 더 효과적이라 고 말하고 있으므로 목표를 구체적으로 설정하라는 흐름이 자 연스럽다. 따라서 ‘specific(구체적인)’이 알맞다. (B) 명상하는 동안 가장 좋아하는 차분한 음악을 듣는 것과 같 이, 새 습관을 당신이 좋아하는 것과 짝짓는 것이 습관 형성에 좋다고 했으므로, 새 습관을 매력적인 걸로 만들라는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 ‘attractive(매력적인)‘가 알맞다. (C) 새로운 습관을 형성하는 데에는 시간이 걸리므로 어떤 이 유로든 진행이 중단된 경우 중단된 지점에서 다시 시작하라고 했으므로, 융통성을 가져야 한다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 flexible(융통성 있는)이 알맞다. YBM(박준언) 1과

I interviewed. David, a chef and kitchen manager,
who has been writing morning pages for two years,
says: My job tends to be very stressful. When I
started writing morning pages, I just wrote a lot of
complaints about my hard life. Later, I began to ask
questions, like “What would make my life easier
today?” “How can I improve my recipes?” Sometimes,
I (A)[keep / stop] asking questions until I reach a
sort of “click moment.” It feels like a door opening
to great ideas. Nowadays, I feel less stressed, enjoy
my job more, and am more productive.
 Now, let’s listen to Yuna, a high school junior:
 When I started this exercise last year, I simply
wrote random thoughts like this:
 I’m sleepy. A slight headache’s starting.
 I need to finish the math assignment today …

 But soon I found I had deeper and deeper
thoughts. Now, I normally start by writing about
today’s tasks or worries. After that, I write about
my dreams and how to move towards them. I often
come up with great plans and a clear sense of
purpose to start the day. Most importantly, I’m
much happier than before.

solution: (A) David는 자신의 힘든 삶에 대한 불평들을 적었지만 후에 멋진 아이디어들로 문을 여는 “click moment”에 도달할 때까 지 계속 질문을 한다는 흐름이므로 keep이 알맞다. (B) 필자는 매일 아침 모닝페이지에 자신의 감정을 적는 것이 감정적 긴장감을 완화하는데 도움이 되었다고 했으므로 이것 은 내적 평화에 기여했다는 흐름이다. 따라서 ‘얻었다’의 뜻을 가진 gained가 알맞다. Like Yuna, I started this journaling during my first
year of high school. At that time, I felt lost,
stressed, and unsure about the future, and it wasn’t
easy for me to concentrate. When I first tried
writing three daily pages, I didn’t expect to stick to
it. But I did, and it changed my life!
Releasing my feelings onto paper every morning
helped relieve my emotional tension. (A)I gained more
inner peace, which improved my schoolwork
performance. Like David, I asked many questions, for
instance, “Why was I so angry yesterday?” “Why are
things less fun these days?” Then, I started raising more
challenging ones: “What could make me happier right
now?” “What is my ideal future? Can I reach it? How?”
(B)The morning Pages are about writing down your
honest thoughts, but if you keep writing negative
emotions, there is a risk of getting stuck in them.
Answering these questions showed me what kind
of person I was and what my needs, values,
passions, and talents were. More importantly, I
came to know what I truly wanted! (C)I
remembered my childhood dreams of being a
writer, songwriter, and radio host. Gradually, vague
ideas became clear plans. Years later, here I am, a
successful podcaster and vlogger! I’ve also published
a book and a music album. (D)My morning pages,
which I still write every day, have given me the
drive and ideas to achieve these aims.
Dear subscribers, will you try writing your morning
pages, too? You never know what creative energy
or ideas you have until you start exploring. Don’t
be a perfectionist, though. If you miss a few days,
simply open your notebook and start again! (E)The
ultimate aim is to improve your mental health and
help you lead a happier, more creative life.

body:
Forming a new habit is not easy, especially in the
beginning. Here are five ways to start a habit that
really sticks. First, start small. Don’t try to do too
much, too quickly. A habit is formed through
repetition, so make the change easier to repeat.
Second, make your goal specific. Don’t say, “I’ll
meditate regularly.” Say, “I’ll meditate for five
minutes each day.” This works even better if _______
_________________________, for example, “After brushing
my teeth in the morning, I’ll meditate for five
minutes.” When your fixed habit becomes a cue for
action, your new habit is more likely to stick. Third,
make it attractive. Pair your new change with what
you love. You could listen to your favorite piece of
calming music while meditating. Fourth, track your
progress. Mark a calendar with an X every time you
finish something. Seeing the progress gives you a
sense of achievement and helps you keep going.
Fifth, be flexible. Forming a new habit takes time. If
you find that your progress has stopped for any
reason, just pick up where you left off.

Now, let me share the experiences of some people I
interviewed. David, a chef and kitchen manager, who
has been writing morning pages for two years, says:
My job tends to be very stressful. When I started
writing morning pages, I just wrote a lot of
complaints about my hard life. Later, I began to ask
questions, like “What would make my life easier
today?” “How can I improve my recipes?”
Sometimes, I keep asking questions until I reach a
sort of “click moment.” It feels like a door opening
to great ideas. Nowadays, I feel less stressed, enjoy
my job more, and am more productive.

When I started this exercise last year, I simply
wrote random thoughts like this:
I’m sleepy. A slight headache’s starting.
I need to finish the math assignment today …
I don’t know what more to write now.
But soon I found I had deeper and deeper
thoughts. Now, I normally start by writing about
today’s tasks or worries. After that, I write about
my dreams and how to move towards them. I often
come up with great plans and a clear sense of
purpose to start the day. Most importantly, I’m
much happier than before.

body:
Welcome to my channel Good Habits! This is
Regan, your podcast host. Today, I’m going to talk
about a way of starting the day that many people,
including me, find enormously useful. It’s a kind of
journaling called “the morning pages.” There is no
age at which it is too late to form this habit. I
started eight years ago as a high school student,
and that’s why today’s episode is especially for my
teenage subscribers.
The morning pages are three pages of “free
writing,” ideally done first thing in the morning. The
concept is simple. Get up every morning, pick up a
pen and a notebook, and write whatever crosses
your mind until you have filled three pages.
The technique was originally developed to help
writers and artists overcome a loss of creativity, but
anybody can use it to create a better life.
There is no right or wrong way to write your
morning pages, but there are two rules. First, don’t
judge your writing as good or bad. These pages
are meant to be a “brain cleansing,” so don’t worry
about writing correctly. Second, keep your writing
completely private. It is important for you to write
freely and honestly. You’re even advised not to
read your writing yourself for weeks.
Now, let me share the experiences of some people
I interviewed.

다음 글을 아래와 같이 표로 정리할 때, 빈칸 (1)~(3)에 들어갈 알맞은 말을 각각 쓰시오.

I can totally relate to these two people because their experiences are similar to mine. Like Yuna, I started this journaling during my first year of high school. At that time, I felt lost, stressed, and unsure about the future, and it wasn’t easy for me to concentrate. When I first tried writing three daily pages, I didn’t expect to stick to it. But I did, and it changed my life! Releasing my feelings onto paper every morning helped relieve my emotional tension. I gained more inner peace, which improved my schoolwork performance. Like David, I asked many questions, for instance, “Why was I so angry yesterday?” “Why are things less fun these days?” Then, I started raising more challenging ones: “What could make me happier right now?” “What is my ideal future? Can I reach it? How?” Answering these questions showed me what kind of person I was and what my needs, values, passions, and talents were. More importantly, I came to know what I truly wanted! I remembered my childhood dreams of being a writer, songwriter, and radio host. Gradually, vague ideas became clear plans. Years later, here I am, a successful podcaster and vlogger! I’ve also published a book and a music album. My morning pages, which I still write every day, have given me the drive and ideas to achieve these aims. Octopuses’ use of tools can be found in their love
of toys and puzzles, too. They are curious about
new objects, and do not like getting bored. That is
why aquariums try to ⓐcome up with ideas to
keep their octopuses busy. Some aquariums hide
food inside a big doll and let the octopus break up
the toy to get the food. Others offer plastic
building blocks for their octopuses to play with.
Our knowledge about the octopus is still very
limited. Thanks to the efforts of scientists, however,
it is expanding year by year. One of the most
ⓑimpressive new findings about the octopus is that
it seems to have feelings. Of course, it is impossible
for us to know exactly what they feel, but a few of
their changes in skin color seem to be linked to
their feelings. For example, a giant Pacific octopus
that turns red seems to be excited, while it is white
when it is relaxed. An octopus ⓒpresented with a
difficult puzzle often undergoes several rapid
changes in color. The octopus seems to be worried
that it may not solve the problem.
Few scientists today ⓓdeny that octopuses are
intelligent animals. Perhaps it is time that we
stopped thinking of them as alien ⓔcreatures and
acknowledged them as intelligent animals like us.
There is still so much we do not know about the
octopus. Aren’t you curious about what is inside
their mind?

animal consciousness has been actively carried

Another sign of the intelligence of the octopus is

create walls to protect the entrances to their
homes. They use not only stones but anything they
can find to protect (A)[them / themselves]. The

shells with bursts of water, carried them to a new
location, and piled them as a shelter. Traveling with
the shells under their bodies forced them to walk
slowly along the sea floor. This made the octopuses
(B)[more exposed / more exposing] to predators.
But it seems that they were willing to take that risk
for greater future protection. The scientists who
discovered the behavior (C)[argue / arguing] that
this is clear evidence of octopuses using tools.

body:
In 2012, scientists met at the University of
Cambridge to talk about consciousness in humans
and animals. Consciousness means having subjective
experiences or awareness. The scientists found that
animals have emotions and can have consciousness
like humans. For example, African grey parrots have
shown evidence of consciousness that is almost as
advanced as that of humans. Even octopuses have
the brain structures needed for subjective
experiences. Drugs that affect human consciousness
also affect some animals in similar ways. So, the
scientists concluded that consciousness is not just
for humans. Animals can have it too.
Since the Cambridge Declaration, research on
animal consciousness has been actively carried out.
Scientists are still working to find out exactly how
animal consciousness works. Not all animals are
conscious, but those with complex nervous systems
are more likely to be. All things considered, it
would be a wise and safe choice to assume that
animals have feelings and to treat them with
respect and kindness.

윗글의 요지로 알맞은 것은?
choices: Animals possess consciousness and experienceemotions in a way similar to humans.
Animals possess reflexive, instinctive consciousnessand emotions, distinct from those of humans.
There is a need for scientific exploration of thebrain structures that support animal consciousness.
The possession of consciousness and emotionshas a positive impact on the formation of socialrelationships among animals.
Many studies are being conducted on how animalshave developed consciousness and emotions, froman evolutionary perspective.

body:
In 2012, scientists met at the University of
Cambridge to talk about consciousness in humans
and animals. Consciousness means having subjective
experiences or awareness. The scientists found that
animals have emotions and can have consciousness
like humans.
(A) Not all animals are conscious, but those with
complex nervous systems are more likely to be.
All things considered, it would be a wise and
safe choice to assume ⓐ[what / that] animals
have feelings and to treat them with respect
and kindness.
(B) So, the scientists concluded that consciousness is
not just for humans. Animals can have it too.
Since the Cambridge Declaration, research on
animal consciousness has been actively carried
out. Scientists are still working ⓑ[to find out /
find out] exactly how animal consciousness
works.
(C) For example, African grey parrots have shown
evidence of consciousness that is almost as
ⓒ[advancing / advanced] as that of humans.
Even octopuses have the brain structures
needed for subjective experiences. Drugs that
affect human consciousness also affect some
animals in similar ways.

다음 글의 요지를 아래와 같이 쓸 때, 빈칸에 들어 갈 알맞은 말을 지문에서 찾아 한 단어로 각각 쓰 시오. (필요시 변형할 것)

Octopuses’ use of tools can be found in their love of toys and puzzles, too. They are curious about new objects, and do not like getting bored. That is why aquariums try to come up with ideas to keep their octopuses busy. Some aquariums hide food inside a big doll and let the octopus break up the toy to get the food. Others offer plastic building blocks for their octopuses to play with. Our knowledge about the octopus is still very limited. Thanks to the efforts of scientists, however, it is expanding year by year. One of the most impressive new findings about the octopus is that it seems to have feelings. Of course, it is impossible for us to know exactly what they feel, but a few of their changes in skin color seem to be linked to their feelings. For example, a giant Pacific octopus that turns red seems to be excited, while it is white when it is relaxed. An octopus presented with a difficult puzzle often undergoes several rapid changes in color. The octopus seems to be worried that it may not solve the problem. Few scientists today deny that octopuses are intelligent animals. Perhaps it is time that we stopped thinking of them as alien creatures and acknowledged them as intelligent animals like us. There is still so much we do not know about the octopus. Aren’t you curious about what is inside their mind? Octopuses show their ability to (A)___________ ___________ when playing with new items, like toys and puzzles, and to express emotions through the (B)___________ ___________ ___________ ___________, suggesting that they should be considered as (C)___________ ___________ akin to humans and that further research is needed to better understand them. YBM(박준언) 2과
answer: (A) use tools (B) change in skin color (C) intelligent animals

Another sign of the intelligence of the octopus is
its use of tools. In the lab, octopuses use tools to
get food rewards. In the wild, they use stones to
create walls to protect the entrances to their
homes. They use not only stones but anything they
can find to protect (A)[them / themselves]. The
most impressive example of octopuses using tools
came in 2009 in Indonesia. A few octopuses were
found to collect coconut shells. They cleaned the
shells with bursts of water, carried them to a new
location, and piled them as a shelter. Traveling with
the shells under their bodies forced them to walk
slowly along the sea floor. This made the octopuses
(B)[more exposed / more exposing] to predators.
But it seems that they were willing to take that risk
for greater future protection. The scientists who
discovered the behavior (C)[argue / arguing] that
this is clear evidence of octopuses using tools.

English has become a widely used “lingua franca”
due to its extensive usage and ⓐadoption in many
countries, allowing individuals who speak different
native languages to communicate and understand
each other. About 1.75 billion people around the
world use English as a useful means of
communication, due to the high ⓑdemand of
English in critical fields such as science, technology,
business, and entertainment. Moreover, in the digital
era, people are ⓒexposed to a vast amount of
online information and resources in English on a
daily basis. These factors have consistently
contributed to the widespread use and global
influence of the English language. As English ability
grows in different nations, various English varieties
have ⓓemerged worldwide, including Singaporean
English, Korean English, Indian English, and others.
Previously, British English and American English were
considered the standard models. However, it is
important to note that American English was initially
seen as a regional ⓔvariation rather than a
standard form. As a result, we now refer to the
different varieties of English as “Englishes,” not
simply “English.”

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ의 영영풀이로 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: ⓐ: the act of accepting or taking somethinginto use, typically a new idea, method, orpolicy
ⓑ: the desire or need for a product or service,often accompanied by the ability to purchaseit
ⓒ: to make something invisible or inaccessible,often something hidden or not immediatelyapparent
ⓓ: to come into view, existence, or prominenceafter being concealed or not yet known.
ⓔ: a difference or change in something, especiallya difference in form, condition, or amount.
solution: 보기의 ⓒ는 ‘종종 숨겨져 있거나 즉시 드러나지 않는 어떤 것 을 보이지 않거나 접근할 수 없게 만들다’로 ‘conceal(감추다)’ 의 영영풀이며, 본문의 exposed는 ‘노출시키다’의 뜻으로 ‘to make something visible or accessible, often something hidden or not immediately apparent (종종 숨겨져 있거나 즉 시 드러나지 않는 어떤 것을 보이거나 접근 가능하게 만들다)’ 으로 풀이된다.

body:
When a language is adopted in a specific region
or community, it is natural for it to (A)[resist /
undergo] changes or modifications as the local people
utilize the language to more accurately reflect their
daily realities and cultural contexts. Linguistic change
takes place across various aspects of language,
including grammar, pronunciation, vocabulary, and
everyday expressions. The change is particularly
noticeable in vocabulary. English vocabulary has
been modified and new expressions have been
(B)[created / discarded] within the different varieties
of English. In Indian English, the term “prepone”
was coined to mean “to reschedule” as the
opposite of “postpone.” For instance, if a meeting
scheduled for Thursday is moved to Wednesday, it
is considered “preponed.” Hong Kong English
speakers shout “add oil” to show encouragement or
support, a direct translation from a Chinese
expression, which originally meant to inject more
gasoline into an engine. In the Philippines, there are
many houses with “dirty kitchens,” which are not
actually “dirty” kitchens. Instead, they refer to
kitchens outside the home, where most of the
cooking takes place to (C)[facilitate / avoid] trapping
heat and smell inside the house in a hot climate.
This evolution allows language to better match up
with the everyday experiences and cultural contexts
of the communities that utilize it.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
solution: (A) 한 언어가 특정 지역이나 공동체에서 채택되면, 지역 사람 들이 그 언어를 자신의 일상 현실과 문화적 맥락을 반영하도 록 활용한다는 것과, 문법, 발음, 어휘, 표현 등 다양한 측면에 서 언어적 변화가 발생한다는 내용이 뒤에 이어지므로, 그 언 어가 변화와 수정을 ‘겪는’ 것은 자연스러운 것이라는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 undergo(겪다)가 알맞다. (B) 영어 어휘는 수정되어 왔으며, 인도, 홍통, 필리핀에서 각 지역별로 "prepone“, "add oil", "dirty kitchen"과 같은 어휘가 만들어졌다는 내용이 이어지므로, 새로운 표현이 만들어져왔다 는 흐름의 created(만들어지는)가 알맞다. (C) 필리핀의 "dirty kitchen"은 실제로 더러운 부엌이 아니라, 더운 기후에서 열기와 냄새를 없애기 위해 집 밖에 마련된 조 리 공간을 흐름으로 avoid(피하다)가 알맞다.

(B) As words and expressions related to Korean

borrowed from foreign languages include

How would you react if you saw an English sign
reading “Robot Ahead” on the road while driving in
South Africa? You would probably look around the
front of your car for a robot that looks like a
human. You would be confused momentarily, but
laugh when you learned that the term “robot” also
means “traffic light” in South Africa. For visitors
from other countries, the unique usage of this word
might cause confusion and misunderstanding, but it
also (A)[highlights / understates] the diversity of
World Englishes, the different varieties of the
English language used around the world.
Using English expressions that incorporate the
cultures of different countries, we are creating
opportunities to (B)[expand / offset] our understanding
of and respect for other cultures. In this respect,
English speakers around the world need to be open
to other English speakers. Embracing the diversity of
English, we can build a more (C)[inclusive /
exclusive] community of English speakers where
everyone's voice is heard without prejudice or
stereotypes. English does not solely belong to
native speakers, but instead it is a language for
anyone who uses it.
(A)
(B)
(C)
solution: (A) 남아프리카공화국에서 "Robot"이라는 단어는 "교통 신호등 "을 의미하며 이 단어의 독특한 사용법은 혼란을 줄 수 있지만, 전 세계 영어의 다양성을 잘 보여준다는 흐름으로 highlights (강조하다)가 알맞다. (B) 다양한 국가의 문화를 반영한 영어 표현은 다른 문화를 이 해하고 존중할 기회를 ‘넓인다’는 흐름으로 expand(확장하다)가 알맞다. (C) 영어의 다양성을 수용하면, 편견 없이 모두의 목소리가 들 리는 포용적인 공동체를 만들 수 있다는 흐름으로 inclusive(포 용적인)가 알맞다. YBM(박준언) 3과

(B) 언어는 문법, 발음, 표현 등 다양한 측면에서 변하지만, 그 중에서도 어휘에서의 변화는 뒤에 이어지는 예시 ‘prepone, add oil, dirty kitchen'과 같이 영어 어휘들은 수정되고 새로운 표현들이 만들어져 사용되고 있으므로 변화가 특히 ’두드려진 다‘는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 noticeable(뚜렷한)은 알맞다. changes or modifications as the local people utilize
the language to more accurately reflect their daily
realities and cultural contexts. Linguistic change
takes place across various aspects of language,
including grammar, pronunciation, vocabulary, and
everyday expressions. The change is particularly
noticeable in vocabulary. English vocabulary has
been modified and new expressions have been
created within the different varieties of English. In
Indian English, the term “prepone” was coined to
mean “to reschedule” as the opposite of
“postpone.” For instance, if a meeting scheduled for
Thursday (A)[is moved / being moved] to
Wednesday, it is considered “preponed.” Hong Kong
English speakers shout “add oil” to show
encouragement or support, a direct translation from
a Chinese expression, which originally meant to
inject more gasoline into an engine. In the
Philippines, there are many houses with “dirty
kitchens,” which are not actually “dirty” kitchens.
Instead, they refer to kitchens outside the home,
(B)[which / where] most of the cooking takes place
to avoid trapping heat and smell inside the house
in a hot climate. This evolution allows language to
better match up with the everyday experiences and
cultural contexts of the communities that utilize
(C)[it / them].

of the communities that utilize it.

Artists usually sign their works of art to show
authorship. But what about AI art? Who actually
creates the work: the AI or the human using it? A
major concern related to authorship is the copyright
of AI-generated art. More and more companies,
developers, and artists ask for legal (A)[ban on /
protection of] the artworks created by AI programs
that they developed or used. Since current copyright
law applies to humans, not machines, the "author"
should be the (B)[machine / person] that arranged
the creation of an AI-generated artwork. However, it
is not always clear who undertook the arrangements.
It could, for example, be the people who organized
or funded the project, did the coding or "teaching"
of the AI, or input a prompt.
Could an AI machine itself ever be considered an
author with legal rights? It seems (C)[likely /
unlikely], but who knows how this question will be
regarded in the future?

(B)
(C)
solution: (A) AI가 생성한 예술 작품의 저작권 문제가 앞 문장에 언급되어 있고, 뒤에는 현행 저작권법이 기계가 아닌 인간에게 적용된다고 설명하고 있으므로, 점점 더 많은 기업, 개발자, 예술가들이 자신 들이 개발하거나 AI로 만든 예술 작품에 대한 법적 보호를 요청 하고 있다는 흐름으로 protection of(~의 보호)’가 알맞다. (B) 현행 저작권법은 기계가 아닌 인간에게 적용된다고 언급되 어 있으므로, AI 생성 예술의 저작자는 창작 업무를 조처한 사 람이어야 한다는 흐름으로 ‘person(인간)’이 알맞다. (C) 뒤에 but(그러나)으로 미래에 이 질문이 어떻게 받아들여질 지는 아무도 모른다는 내용이 이어지므로, 현재로서는 AI 기계 자체가 법적 권리를 가진 저작자로 간주될 가능성이 적어 보인 다는 대조적인 흐름으로 ‘unlikely(있을 것 같지 않은)’가 알맞다.

AI-generated artworks (B)[had been / have been]

people, it is at best an imitation of human art, not

who insist that AI is more than a tool. They argue
that the results of AI creation are largely beyond
human control and AI should therefore be seen as
existing in its own right.

authorship. But what about AI art? Who actually
creates the work: the AI or the human using it?
(A) A major concern related to authorship is the
copyright of AI-generated art. (B) The concept of
copyright was introduced in response to the
widespread use of the printing press in Europe
during the 15th and 16th centuries. (C) More and
more companies, developers, and artists ⓐ[ask /
asking] for legal protection of the artworks created
by AI programs that they developed or used.
(D) Since current copyright law applies to humans,
not machines, the "author" should be the person
who arranged the creation of an AI-generated
artwork. (E) However, ⓑ[it / that] is not always clear
who undertook the arrangements. It could, for
example, be the people who organized or funded
the project, did the coding or "teaching" of the AI,
or ⓒ[input / to input] a prompt.
Could an AI machine itself ever be considered an
author with legal rights? ⓓIt seems unlikely, but
who knows how this question will be regarded in
the future?

body:
The Reasons for the Viral Spread of Fake News
Fake news on social media spreads significantly
farther and faster than true stories. A study by the
Massachusetts Institute of Technology in the US
(A)[has / was] shown that fake news spreads online
6 times faster than real news on average.
One explanation for this phenomenon is that
people like new and provocative things. When
information is (B)[astonishing / astonished], people
not only feel that it is surprising, but they also want
to share the stimulating news with others. By passing
it to others on social media, they can gain attention
because they are the first to post previously
unknown, but possibly false, information. Also, fake
news goes viral because people in their daily lives
tend to think simply and effortlessly. It is more likely
for them to believe new information without any
proof, instead of critically (C)[examine / examining] it.

다음 글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

These days, everyone accesses the news through
the Internet or social media, and often selectively
takes the information that suits their tastes or
beliefs. However, consistently encountering similar
perspectives without considering alternative views
can lead you to be trapped in an “echo chamber.”
An echo chamber refers to an ⓐ[enclosed / open]
space where sound doesn’t leak out and returns as
an echo. The term “echo chamber” is also used to
describe any situation in which you only hear
opinions you already agree with. This can distort
your understanding of reality, and ⓑ[limit /
improve] your ability to think critically and engage
in meaningful debates. Worse still, an echo chamber
may foster social division, making collaboration on
common issues ⓒ[challenging / easy]. To avoid
falling into this trap, you must actively seek diverse
sources of information and engage with people who
have different views. Always remember to check the
information you receive, and keep an open mind
when discussing new ideas. Even if you really want
something to be true, it doesn’t always mean that
it is true.
ⓐ
ⓑ                 ⓒ

of fake news like Gina is not unusual. Fake news is
a deliberate attempt to manipulate people by
spreading inaccurate information. It is made by
certain groups with the intention of attracting
people’s attention, making profits, or gaining
political benefits. It can confuse people, disturb
society, and even ⓐ[rarely / seriously] harm the
public as well as all individuals involved.
It is very ⓑ[rare / common] for fake news to
spread during states of emergency. For example,
after an earthquake measuring 6.5 struck Ambon,
Indonesia, in September 2019, thousands of
residents did not return to their homes and were
still in shelters for two weeks. (A)이것은 쓰나미가 뒤

The Reasons for the Viral Spread of Fake News
Fake news on social media spreads significantly
farther and faster than true stories. A study by the
Massachusetts Institute of Technology in the US
(A)[has / was] shown that fake news spreads online
6 times faster than real news on average.
One explanation for this phenomenon is that
people like new and provocative things. When
information is (B)[astonishing / astonished], people
not only feel that it is surprising, but they also want
to share the stimulating news with others. By passing
it to others on social media, they can gain attention
because they are the first to post previously
unknown, but possibly false, information. Also, fake
news goes viral because people in their daily lives
tend to think simply and effortlessly. It is more likely
for them to believe new information without any
proof, instead of critically (C)[examine / examining] it.

(B)
(C)
solution: (A) 주어 A study by ~ the US(미국 매사추세츠 공과대학의 한 연구)가 ‘보여주는’ 주체로 동사 show와 능동의 관계를 이 루며 이미 나온 연구 결과가 지금까지도 영향을 미치므로 shown과 함께 현재완료를 이루는 has가 알맞다. (B) 주어 information(정보)이 ‘놀라게 하는’ 주체이므로 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 형태의 형용사 astonishing이 알맞다. (C) 구전치사 instead of(~ 대신에)의 목적어이므로 동명사 examining이 알맞다.

W: Welcome to this Free Lecture Series! Today, first,
I’m going to talk about what a digital footprint is
and why it matters. Then, I’ll offer some tips to
protect your digital footprints. Digital footprints are
all the information online about you. They can be
posted by you or others. They include websites
you visit, messages you send, and information you
upload on the Internet. Digital footprints matter
because they’re relatively permanent and they can
reveal your private life. Also, your digital footprints
can determine your digital reputation, ⓐ[which /
that] is now as important as your offline
reputation. For example, if you upload posts that
ⓑ[include / includes] bad words, people might
think negatively about you. To make matters
worse, your digital footprints can be ⓒ[using /
used] for digital crimes. Therefore, to be a good
digital citizen, (A)you’re expected to manage your
digital footprints carefully. From now on, I’ll talk
about the ways to protect your digital footprints.

Gina was ⓐ[astonished / indifferent] when she saw the
news headline, “The Heundeulbawi in Seoraksan
National Park Has Fallen.” Gina immediately shared the
shocking story with her close friends. Later, during the
morning news on TV, a reporter standing next to the
ⓑ[damaged / undamaged] Heundeulbawi said, “Today’s
Internet stories of the Heundeulbawi being damaged
were fake.” Gina was ⓒ[embarrassed / delighted] by
the fact that she had spread the fake news.
It reminded her of another incident of fake news
that had happened a while ago. (A)유명한 운동선수가
사망했다는 뉴스가 온라인에서 가장 큰 이슈가 되었지
만, 그것은 가짜로 밝혀졌다. It had been made by
content creators who sought people’s attention. They
produced provocative false stories to make money by
raising the number of views of their posts. At that
time, Gina criticized those who had made and spread
fake news because it had hurt the athlete and
confused people. This time, however, Gina herself had
accidentally contributed to the spread of fake news.

Unfortunately, becoming an accidental distributor
of fake news like Gina is not unusual. Fake news is
a deliberate attempt ⓐto manipulate people by
spreading inaccurate information. It is made by
certain groups with the intention of attracting
people’s attention, ⓑmaking profits, or gaining
political benefits. It can confuse people, disturb
society, and even seriously harm the public ⓒas
well as all individuals involved.
It is very common ⓓfake news to spread during
states of emergency. For example, after an
earthquake measuring 6.5 struck Ambon, Indonesia,
in September 2019, thousands of residents did not
ⓔreturn their homes and were still in shelters for
two weeks. This was ⓕbecause fake news stories on
social media that another earthquake followed by a
tsunami was about to strike. One of those
messages said, “It’s up to you if you want to

to sink in the next few days.” Many ⓖdisplaced

These days, everyone accesses the news through
the Internet or social media, and often selectively
takes the information that suits their tastes or
beliefs. However, consistently encountering similar
perspectives without considering alternative views
can lead you to be trapped in an “echo chamber.”
(A) This can distort your understanding of reality, and
limit your ability to think critically and engage
in meaningful debates. Worse still, an echo
chamber may foster social division, ⓐ[making /
made] collaboration on common issues challenging.
(B) An echo chamber refers to an enclosed space
ⓑ[which / where] sound doesn’t leak out and
returns as an echo. The term “echo chamber” is
also used to describe any situation in which
you only hear opinions you already agree with.
(C) To avoid falling into this trap, you must actively
seek diverse sources of information and ⓒ[engage
/ engaging] with people who have different
views. Always remember to check the information
you receive, and keep an open mind when
discussing new ideas. Even if you really want

These days, everyone accesses the news through
the Internet or social media, and often selectively
takes the information that suits their tastes or
beliefs. However, consistently encountering similar
perspectives without considering alternative views
can lead you to be trapped in an “echo chamber.” An
echo chamber refers to an enclosed space where
sound doesn’t leak out and returns as an echo. The
term “echo chamber” is also used to describe any
situation in which you only hear opinions you already agree with. This can distort your
understanding of reality, and limit your ability to
think critically and engage in meaningful debates.
Worse still, an echo chamber may foster social
division, making collaboration on common issues
challenging. To avoid falling into this trap, you must
actively seek diverse sources of information and
engage with people who have different views.
Always remember to check the information you
receive, and keep an open mind when discussing
new ideas. Even if you really want something to be
true, it doesn’t always mean that it is true.

Improving Your Discussion Skills Through Social Media
Echo Chambers: Why Seeking Different Views Matters
How to Find the Right Information for You in the Digital Age
The Advantages and Disadvantages of Interacting with Only Like-Minded People

Ways to Spot and Avoid Fake News
With so much information on the Internet, how
can you make sure that fake news does not
mislead you? First, read beyond the provocative
headlines. They can be so stimulating to get more
clicks that you may click on them accidentally. So
don’t just read the headlines, but read the text
carefully. Second, don’t read the news at face value.
Exercise critical thinking skills to judge the news.
You should question, analyze, and evaluate what
you read. Third, examine your biases. Consider if
your own beliefs could affect your judgment. Ask
yourself if you are only reading articles that suit
your opinion, and look for articles that oppose your
opinion as well. Finally, check the credibility of the
source. You should examine who wrote the news
story and what the intent was behind writing the
news story. You also need to check whether the
news story is from a reliable media source and the
evidence is valid.

Verifying the reliability and reputation of thesource is necessary to spot fake news.

body:
It is very common for fake news to spread during
states of emergency. For example, after an
earthquake measuring 6.5 struck Ambon, Indonesia,
in September 2019, thousands of residents did not
return to their homes and were still in shelters for
two weeks. This was because of fake news stories
on social media that another earthquake followed
by a tsunami was about to strike. One of those
messages said, “It’s up to you if you want to
believe me or not, but apparently Ambon is going
to sink in the next few days.” Many displaced
people were so anxious about aftershocks that the
government had to announce that the information
was fake.

(1) When is fake news easy to spread? → It is easy to spread _______________________________. (2) What made thousands of residents not return to their homes? → It was ______________________________________________ ______________________________________________________. YBM(박준언) 1과
answer: during states of emergency. fake news stories on social media that another earthquake

In the summer of 2022, during the worst drought
in 500 years in Europe, a stone known as a
“hunger stone” was found in a Czech town along
the Elbe River. The stone had a sentence written on
it that read: “If you see me, then cry.”
The hunger stones, found in rivers across central
Europe, typically remain underwater. However, when
droughts occur and water levels retreat, these
stones become ⓐ[visible / invisible]. The stones are
significant because they bear records of the past
severe droughts. Droughts cause ⓑ[reduced /
increased] harvests, food shortages, and hunger,
especially for the poor. The words on the hunger
stones are believed to warn of these hardships and
to urge people to be prepared.
Considering the continuation of climate change,
experts warn that the situation we face is not just a
simple, occasional drought but a ⓒ[mild / severe]
drought that could persist for decades. The United
Nations has predicted that by 2050, 기후 변화에 대
응하기 위해 중대한 조치가 취해지지 않으면 전 세계
인구의 75%가 가뭄의 영향들로 고통받을 수 있다.

solution: ⓐ 기아석은 일반적으로 물속에 잠겨 있다고 했으므로, 가뭄으 로 수위가 낮아지면 돌들이 보이게 된다는 흐름이 되는 visible(보이는)이 알맞다. ⓑ 가뭄은 식량 부족과 굶주림을 초래한다는 내용이 이어지므 로 수확량 감소를 초래한다는 흐름이 되는 reduced(감소된)가 알맞다. ⓒ 우리가 직면한 상황이 단순하고 일시적인 가뭄이 아니라는 내용 뒤에서 but(그러나)에 이어지며 수십 년 동안 지속될 수 있다고 했으므로, 심각한 가뭄이라는 흐름이 되는 severe(심각 한)가 알맞다.

다음 글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

The cart is ridiculously heavy now, and almost
impossible to push. Then, a man in a business suit
comes up behind us. He smiles.
“Looks like you could use some help.” He doesn’t
wait for us to answer before grabbing the cart’s
handle.
“Thank you for helping us,” I tell him.
“Not a problem. We all need to help one
another.” He smiles again, and I return the smile. It
is good to know that difficult times can bring out
the ⓐ[best / worst] in people. I decide that one
favor deserves another.
“Why don’t you take a bag of ice for yourself,” I
suggest.
His smile does not fade. “I have a better idea,” he
says. “Why don’t you take a bag of ice for
yourselves, and I’ll keep the rest.”
For a moment I think he is joking, but then
realize he is serious. “Excuse me?”
He is still smiling, but his eyes ⓑ[scare/ relieve]
me. As long as his hands are firmly locked on the
handle of our cart, there is nothing to prove that
it’s ours and not his.
“Is there a problem here?”
It is Uncle Basil. He has arrived just in time.
“Not at all.”
The man looks at the ice with a ⓒ[bitter/ bright]
face, then leaves.
ⓐ              ⓑ               ⓒ
solution: ⓐ 정장 입은 남자가 무거운 카트를 밀어주는 친절을 보이며 서로 도와야 한다고 한 뒤에 이어지므로 어려운 시기에 사람 들의 장점이 드러난다는 것을 알게 되는 것은 좋은 일이라는 흐름이 되는 best(가장 좋은 점)가 알맞다. ⓑ 남자가 화자의 얼음 봉지들을 빼앗을 생각이라는 것을 깨 달은 후이며, 그가 웃고 있다는 내용 뒤에 but(그러나)에 이어 지므로 그의 눈빛이 화자를 위협한다는 흐름이 되는 scare(위 협하다)가 알맞다. ⓒ 화자의 얼음 봉지들을 탈취하려던 남자의 시도가 Basil 삼 촌의 도착으로 좌절되었으므로, 남자가 씁쓸한 표정으로 얼음 을 보았다는 흐름이 되는 bitter(씁쓸한)가 알맞다. In the summer of 2022, during the worst drought
in 500 years in Europe, a stone (A)[knowing / known]
as a “hunger stone” was found in a Czech town along
the Elbe River. The stone had a sentence written on
it (B)[that / what] read: “If you see me, then cry.”
The hunger stones, found in rivers across central
Europe, typically remain underwater. However, when
droughts occur and water levels retreat, these
stones become visible. The stones are significant
because they bear records of the past severe
droughts. Droughts cause reduced harvests, food
shortages, and hunger, especially for the poor. The
words on the hunger stones are believed to warn
of these hardships and to urge people (C)[being /
to be] prepared.
Considering the continuation of climate change,
experts warn that the situation we face is not just a
simple, occasional drought but a severe drought
that could persist for decades. The United Nations
has predicted that by 2050, 75 percent of the
global population could suffer from the effects of
drought unless significant action is taken to address
climate change.

Our mindset, or way of thinking, affects our ability
to deal with life’s challenges. Psychologists say there
are two main mindsets: “fixed” and “growth.”
For people with a fixed mindset, failure just shows
(A)[what / that] their intelligence, abilities, and
talents are limited. They may think, for example,
“I’ve never been good at writing. I’ll never be a
good writer.” Therefore, they stay in their comfort
zone, where they won’t (B)[challenge / be
challenged]. They tend to reject even constructive
criticism. Also, other people’s success makes them
feel defeated and lose confidence.
Meanwhile, people with a growth mindset accept
life’s challenges. For them, failure is an opportunity.
They may think, for example, “I can still learn and
practice writing skills until I can write a great story.”
They can learn from criticism, ask for advice, and
be inspired by other people’s success. A growth
mindset empowers people (C)[feeling / to feel]
more comfortable about their imperfections and
overcome crises or mistakes more easily.
Experts say that we can develop a growth mindset
through practice. Whenever you feel “It’s impossible.
I’d rather give up,” why don’t you train yourself to say,
“I still want to try. I can learn how to make it possible”?

Our mindset, or way of thinking, affects our ability
to deal with life’s challenges. Psychologists say there
are two main mindsets: “fixed” and “growth.”
For people with a fixed mindset, failure just shows
(A)[what / that] their intelligence, abilities, and
talents are limited. They may think, for example,
“I’ve never been good at writing. I’ll never be a
good writer.” Therefore, they stay in their comfort
zone, where they won’t (B)[challenge / be
challenged]. They tend to reject even constructive
criticism. Also, other people’s success makes them
feel defeated and lose confidence.
Meanwhile, people with a growth mindset accept
life’s challenges. For them, failure is an opportunity.
They may think, for example, “I can still learn and
practice writing skills until I can write a great story.”
They can learn from criticism, ask for advice, and
be inspired by other people’s success. A growth
mindset empowers people (C)[feeling / to feel]
more comfortable about their imperfections and
overcome crises or mistakes more easily.
Experts say that we can develop a growth mindset
through practice. Whenever you feel “It’s impossible.
I’d rather give up,” why don’t you train yourself to say,
“I still want to try. I can learn how to make it possible”?

This week’s topic in the City Wellness Center
Newsletter is resilience, or “the power ⓐto
overcome.” Julia Hone, a famous doctor, tells us
ⓑhow we can deal with difficult times by cultivating
our inner strength.
No life is free from problems. ⓒWhatever life path
we choose, we all experience adversity. This can
take the form of illness, accidents, failure in exams,
family and relationship issues, or other stresses. To
cope, we all need the ability to overcome
difficulties, ⓓthat is known as resilience. Resilience
means springing back, just like a bouncy ball after
hitting the ground. If you are resilient, you can
bounce back and recover quickly from the hard
times ⓔwhat you experience. Furthermore, you
learn and grow from adversity. So, resilience is the
ability to handle, recover from, and ⓕbenefiting
from difficult life events.

body:
Our mindset, or way of thinking, affects our ability
to deal with life’s challenges. Psychologists say there
are two main mindsets: “fixed” and “growth.”
For people with a fixed mindset, failure just shows
(A)[what / that] their intelligence, abilities, and
talents are limited. They may think, for example,
“I’ve never been good at writing. I’ll never be a
good writer.” Therefore, they stay in their comfort
zone, where they won’t (B)[challenge / be
challenged]. They tend to reject even constructive
criticism. Also, other people’s success makes them
feel defeated and lose confidence.
Meanwhile, people with a growth mindset accept
life’s challenges. For them, failure is an opportunity.
They may think, for example, “I can still learn and
practice writing skills until I can write a great story.”
They can learn from criticism, ask for advice, and
be inspired by other people’s success. A growth
mindset empowers people (C)[feeling / to feel]
more comfortable about their imperfections and
overcome crises or mistakes more easily.
Experts say that we can develop a growth mindset
through practice. Whenever you feel “It’s impossible.
I’d rather give up,” why don’t you train yourself to say,
“I still want to try. I can learn how to make it possible”?

윗글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: pros and cons of fixed and growth mindsets
reasons why writing skills are hard to improve
effect of natural talent and hard work on success
importance of the growth mindset and how to develop it

There are countless stories of successful people
who not only survived adversity but used it as a
stepping stone to growth. Fairy tale writer Hans
Andersen said that his childhood poverty, the early
loss of his father, and his experience of being
disrespected were the sources for his most popular
stories. “The hardship was a real blessing that
inspired me to write stories like The Little Match
Girl, The Snow Queen, and The Ugly Duckling.”
Athlete Aimee Mullins also saw her challenges as an
opportunity. She was born with a medical condition
that resulted in losing both legs beneath the knee
to surgery. She competed against athletes without
disabilities in a national competition and
participated in the Paralympics in 1996. Her career
also includes modeling, acting, and public speaking.
She says her physical condition is not a disability
but the very thing that opened the door for her
amazing potential. Both people succeeded not
“despite” adversity but thanks to it. This is the real
bouncing back.

like a muscle. You can build it up through practice,
by developing thoughts, behaviors, and habits that
allow you to recover from painful or stressful
events. Here are three basic strategies to build up
this “resilience muscle.”
Three Basic Strategies to Build Up Your “Resilience
Muscle”
First, accept and respect adversity as a natural part
of life. This doesn’t mean being passive, but
understanding that some changes in life can cause
suffering or stress. Then, instead of feeling singled
out and thinking, “Why me?”, you can face
whatever happens and focus on what you can
change, not what you can’t. Embracing challenges
and unexpected obstacles in your life can help you
confront them as a learning process. (B)역경이 없었
다면 결코 생겨날 수 없었던 그 모든 성공담들에 대해
생각해 보세요!

we are all born with the potential for resilience
avoiding stressful situations is the best way tostay mentally strong

Our mindset, or way of thinking, affects our ability
to deal with life’s challenges. Psychologists say there
are two main mindsets: “fixed” and “growth.”
For people with a fixed mindset, failure just shows
that their intelligence, abilities, and talents are
limited. They may think, for example, “I’ve never
been good at writing. I’ll never be a good writer.”
(A)______________, they stay in their comfort zone,
where they won’t be challenged. They tend to reject
even constructive criticism. Also, other people’s success
makes them feel defeated and lose confidence.
(B)______________, people with a growth mindset
accept life’s challenges. For them, failure is an
opportunity. They may think, for example, “I can still
learn and practice writing skills until I can write a
great story.” They can learn from criticism, ask for
advice, and be inspired by other people’s success. A
growth mindset empowers people to feel more
comfortable about their imperfections and overcome
crises or mistakes more easily.
Experts say that we can develop a growth mindset
through practice. Whenever you feel “It’s impossible.
I’d rather give up,” why don’t you train yourself to say,
“I still want to try. I can learn how to make it possible”?

(B)

The Foldscope has been utilized for various purposes
beyond malaria diagnosis. In Nigeria, it has also
been instrumental in detecting fake antimalarial drugs.
The drugs are responsible for over 100,000 deaths
annually in sub-Saharan Africa, mostly among
children under five. When crushed into powder and
examined under a Foldscope, real drugs appear as
uniform particles, while fake drugs appear as mere
powder. Furthermore, over 400 scientific papers
have been published using Foldscope data, and
around 1,200 projects are currently in progress in
India. In the United States, Foldscope programs in
public libraries have introduced many children to
the wonders of science. If Prakash and Cybulski had
given up on their idea of the Foldscope, these
achievements could not have occurred.
As billions of people lack access to health care
and thousands of preventable deaths occur, science
is playing a crucial role in finding solutions to these
challenges. (A)폴드스코프와 같은 도구들은 과학을 모든
사람에게 접근 가능하게 만들어 주어 점차 중요해 지고 있다.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
solution: (A) 현미경의 발명으로 박테리아나 생명체의 미세한 구조를 발 견할 수 있었다는 과거 사실과는 반대되는 상황을 가정하고 있으며, 주절에 ‘might not have discovered’가 사용되었으므 로, 가정법 과거완료 구문 ‘if+주어+had p.p. ~, 주어+조동사의 과거형+have p.p. …’의 구조를 이뤄야 한다. 따라서 과거완료 인 had not been invented가 적절하다. (B) It was 뒤에 온 명사구 the Foldscope가 동사 presented의 목적어에 해당되며, 뒤에 주어와 동사 Manu Prakash and Jim Cybulski presented가 이어지므로, ‘…한 것은 바로 ~였다‘라는 뜻으로 목적어를 강조하기 위해 쓰인 ’It was ~ that …’ 강조 구문을 이루는 that이 적절하다. (C) 앞의 a paper microscope they invented는 주어 The Foldscope와 콤마(,)로 연결되어 주어를 부연 설명하는 동격어구 이므로, 문장의 동사 자리여야 한다. 따라서 과거동사 achieved 가 적절하다.

solution: (A) 완전한 절 뒤에 접속사 없이 콤마만으로 또 다른 동사(구)를 연결할 수 없으므로 준동사를 써야 한다. 분사구문의 의미상의 주어인 주절의 내용이 ‘~을 초래하는’ 주체이고, 뒤에 목적어 food shortages가 이어지므로 능동 의미 현재분사 causing이 적절하다. (B) remember는 목적어로 동명사 또는 to부정사를 취하지만, ‘(과거에) ~했던 것을 기억하다’라는 의미일 때는 동명사를 쓴 다. 문맥상 ‘책에서 풍차를 본 것을 기억했다’이므로 seeing이 알맞다. (C) 준사역동사 help는 ‘help+목적어+(to)동사원형’의 5형식으 로 쓰이며, 목적어와 목적격보어가 능동 관계일 경우 동사원형 또는 to부정사가 온다. us가 grow의 주체이므로 목적격보어로 grow가 적절하다.

For a microscope to function properly, it must
meet certain minimum requirements. These include
an eyepiece, a tube through which the viewer looks,
and a lens for magnification. The microscope must
also have a component that can hold a specimen
and move from side to side to explore different
areas of the specimen. Furthermore, a mechanism
to bring the specimen into focus, usually
accomplished by moving it closer to or farther from
the lens, is necessary. Finally, a light source is
required to illuminate the specimen.
An ideal microscope would be made with the best
performing materials and mechanisms for each
component. However, such a microscope would
likely be enormously expensive. On the other hand,
a cheap microscope may not be able to deliver
high performance. Prakash and Cybulski
experimented with various designs and materials in
order to find a suitable compromise. While many
manufacturers might have settled for a middle
ground between these two extremes, Prakash and
Cybulski were determined to create a microscope
that was both inexpensive and high-performing,
while remaining accessible to all.

The Foldscope has been utilized for various
purposes beyond malaria diagnosis. In Nigeria, it
has also been instrumental in detecting fake
antimalarial drugs. The drugs are responsible for
over 100,000 deaths annually in sub-Saharan Africa,
mostly among children under five. When crushed
into powder and examined under a Foldscope, real
drugs appear as uniform particles, while fake drugs
appear as mere powder. Furthermore, over 400
scientific papers have been published using
Foldscope data, and around 1,200 projects are
currently in progress in India. In the United States,
Foldscope programs in public libraries have
introduced many children to the wonders of
science. If Prakash and Cybulski had given up on
their idea of the Foldscope, these achievements
could not have occurred.
As billions of people lack access to health care
and thousands of preventable deaths occur, science
is playing a crucial role in finding solutions to these
challenges. Tools like the Foldscope, which make
science accessible to everyone, are becoming
increasingly important.

body:
다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
This week’s topic in the City Wellness Center Newsletter is resilience, or “the power to overcome.” Julia Hone, a famous doctor, tells us how we can deal with difficult times by cultivating our inner strength. No life is free from problems. Whatever life path we choose, we all experience adversity.
(A) You might think “Hey, these are ⓐ exceptional people.” However, we are all born with the potential for resilience. Just like these people, we all can develop the strength to quickly recover from a crisis that could ⓑ otherwise cause lasting damage to our mental health. The good news is that resilience is like a muscle. Here are three basic strategies to build up this “resilience muscle.”
(B) To cope, we all need the ability to overcome difficulties, which is known as resilience. Resilience means springing back, just like a bouncy ball after hitting the ground. If you are resilient, you can bounce back and recover ⓒslowly from the hard times you experience. Furthermore, you learn and grow from adversity. So, resilience is the ability to handle, recover from, and ⓓbenefit from difficult life events.
(C) There are countless stories of successful people who not only survived adversity but used it as a ⓔstepping stone to growth. Fairy tale writer Hans Andersen said that his childhood poverty, the early loss of his father, and his experience of being disrespected were the sources for his most popular stories. Athlete Aimee Mullins also saw her challenges as an opportunity. Both people succeeded not “despite” adversity but thanks to it. This is the real bouncing back.

윗글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 가장 적절하 지 않은 것은?
solution: ③ slowly → quickly 회복탄력성이 있는 사람은 힘든 시기로부터 '빠르게 (quickly)' 회복한다는 내용이 되어야 자연스럽다. ① 안데르센과 멀린스를 가리키는 '특출난, 특별한 (exceptional)' 사람이라는 내용이 적절하다. ② 회복력을 기르지 못하면 정신 건강에 손상을 줄이라는 의미의 부사(otherwise)로 적절하다. ④ 역경으로부터 배우고 성장한다는 흐름이므로 고난으로부터 '이득을 얻다(benefit)'가 적절하다. ⑤ 역경을 성장의 '디딤돌(stepping stone)'로 삼았다는 비유적 표현으로 적절하다.

body:
다음 글을 읽고 추론할 수 있는 내용으로 가장 적절한 것은?
This week’s topic in the City Wellness Center Newsletter is resilience, or “the power to overcome.” Julia Hone, a famous doctor, tells us how we can deal with difficult times by cultivating our inner strength. No life is free from problems. Whatever life path we choose, we all experience adversity. This can take the form of illness, accidents, failure in exams, family and relationship issues, or other stresses. To cope, we all need the ability to overcome difficulties, which is known as resilience. Resilience means springing back, just like a bouncy ball after hitting the ground. If you are resilient, you can bounce back and recover quickly from the hard times you experience. Furthermore, you learn and grow from adversity. So, resilience is the ability to handle, recover from, and benefit from difficult life events.
choices: People who avoid all forms of adversity throughout their lives tend to be the most resilient.
No individual can completely escape experiencing some form of hardship in life.
Julia Hone developed the concept of resilience through her own personal medical research.
Resilience is a skill that only certain professionals, such as doctors, are capable of developing.
Once a person recovers from one hard time, they will never face adversity again.
solution: ② 본문 첫 문장에서 '그 어떤 삶도 문제로부터 자유롭지 않다 (No life is free from problems)'고 했고, 이어서 '어떤 삶의 길을 선택하든 우리 모두 역경을 경험한다'고 했으므로, 그 누구도 삶에서 어떤 형태의 어려움을 겪는 것을 완전히 피할 수는 없다는 것을 추론할 수 있으므로 ②가 가장 알맞다. ① 역경을 모두 피하는 사람이 가장 회복탄력적이라는 것은 본문과 정반대이며, 회복탄력성은 역경을 피하는 것이 아니라 그것으로부터 빠르게 회복하고 배우는 능력이므로 알맞지 않다. ③ Julia Hone은 단지 뉴스레터에서 회복탄력성에 대한 설명을 하였을 뿐, 자신의 의학 연구를 통해 회복탄력성 개념을 만들어냈다는 내용은 추론할 수 없다. ④ 회복탄력성이 의사와 같은 특정 전문가만 기를 수 있는 기술이라는 내용은 추론할 수 없다. ⑤ 오히려 삶은 지속적으로 문제를 겪는 것으로 언급되고 있으며, 한 번 회복하면 다시는 역경을 겪지 않는다는 내용은 추론할 수 없다.

body:
다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
There are countless stories of successful people who not only survived adversity but used it as a stepping stone to growth. Fairy tale writer Hans Andersen said that his childhood poverty, the early loss of his father, and his experience of being disrespected were the sources for his most popular stories. ⓐ “The hardship was a real blessing that inspired me to write stories like The Little Match Girl, The Snow Queen, and The Ugly Duckling.” Athlete Aimee Mullins also saw her challenges as an opportunity. She was born with a medical condition that resulted in losing both legs beneath the knee to surgery.
ⓑ She competed against athletes without disabilities in a national competition and participated in the Paralympics in 1996. Her career also includes modeling, acting, and public speaking. ⓒ She says her physical condition is not a disability but the very thing that opened the door for her amazing potential. Both people succeeded not “despite” adversity but thanks to it. This is the real bouncing back. ⓓ You might think “Hey, these are exceptional people.” ⓔ Just like these people, we all can develop the strength to quickly recover from a crisis that could otherwise cause lasting damage to our mental health. The good news is that resilience is like a muscle. You can build it up through practice, (해석: 고통스럽거나 스 트레스가 많은 사건에서 회복할 수 있도록 생각과 행동, 습관을 발전 시킴으로써) Here are three basic strategies to build up this “resilience muscle.”

윗글의 밑줄 친 해석과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <조건>에 맞게 영 작하시오.
보기 events / stressful / that / to / thoughts / behaviors / you / recover / from / painful / or / by / develop / habits / and / allow
조건 1. <보기>의 단어는 모두 한 번씩 사용할 것(단, 어형 변화 가능)
2. '~함으로써'라는 전치사구 구조와 5형식 'allow' 동사의 문법적 특징을 반드시 반영할것
→
answer: by developing thoughts, behaviors, and habits that allow you to recover from painful or stressful events
solution: ~함으로써'의 의미를 가진 'by + -ing'를 써야 하므로 'develop'에 ing을 붙여 동명사로 만든다. 'allow + 목적어(you) + 목적격보어(to recover)'의 5형식 구조를 쓴다.

The good news is that resilience is like a muscle. You can build it up through practice, (해석: 고통스럽거나 스 트레스가 많은 사건에서 회복할 수 있도록 생각과 행동, 습관을 발전 시킴으로써) Here are three basic strategies to build up this “resilience muscle.”

윗글의 문맥상 다음 중 낱말의 영영풀이로 가장 적절하지 않은 것은?
choices: adversity: a difficult or unpleasant situation; hardship
exceptional: much greater than usual; extraordinary or outstanding
resilience: the ability of a person to adjust or recover quickly from difficulties
potential: a permanent mental or physical disability that limits a person’s success
crisis: a time of intense difficulty, trouble, or danger
solution: ⑤ 성공을 방해하는 영구적인 장애(disability)에 대한 설명이므로 옳지 않다. ① '역경, 고난'이라는 의미로, 삶의 힘들고 불쾌한 상황이나 고초를 의미한다. ② 평범함을 뛰어넘는 '이례적인, 특출난, 우수한'이라는 뜻의 올바른 영영풀이다. ③ 어려운 상황에서 빠르게 적응하거나 '회복하는 능력'을 뜻하므로 완벽한 정의이다. ④ 정신 건강에 상처를 줄 수 있는 극심한 고난이나 위험한 시기를 의미하므로 올바르다.

body:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
This week’s topic in the City Wellness Center Newsletter is resilience, or “the power to overcome.” Julia Hone, a famous doctor, tells us how we can deal with difficult times by cultivating our inner strength. No life is free from problems. Whatever life path we choose, we all experience adversity. This can take the form of illness, accidents, failure in exams, family and relationship issues, or other stresses. To cope, we all need the ability to overcome difficulties, which is known as resilience. Resilience means springing back, just like a bouncy ball after hitting the ground. If you are resilient, you can bounce back and recover quickly from the hard times you experience. Furthermore, you learn and grow from adversity. So, resilience is the ability to handle, recover from, and benefit from difficult life events.
choices: Julia Hone is a schoolteacher who writes for the newsletter each week.
According to the passage, adversity can appear in various forms such as illness or exam failure.
Resilience refers to permanently avoiding any kind of hardship in life.
People who are resilient take a long time to recover from difficult experiences.
Learning and personal growth are said to have no connection with adversity.
solution: ② 역경이 질병, 사고, 시험 실패 등 다양한 형태로 나타날 수 있다고 했으므로 일치한다. ① Julia Hone은 '유명한 의사'로 소개되었지 교사가 아니므로 일치하지 않는다. ③ 회복탄력성은 고난을 완전히 피하는 것이 아니라 그것을 극복하는 능력이므로 일치하지 않는다. ④ 회복탄력적인 사람은 빠르게 회복한다고 했으므로 일치하지 않는다. ⑤ 역경으로부터 배우고 성장한다고 명시했으므로 일치하지 않는다.

body:
다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
First, accept and respect adversity as a natural part of life. This doesn’t mean being passive, but (A) understanding that some changes in life can cause suffering or stress. Then, instead of feeling singled out and thinking, “Why me?”, you can face (B) whatever happens and focus on what you can change, not what you can’t. Embracing challenges and unexpected obstacles in your life can help you confront them as a learning process. Think of all the success stories that could never have happened without ! Second, have “me time,” that is, personal time to look after yourself. Take a break and be in the present moment, neither (C) regretting the past nor worrying about the future. Walk, meditate, write, draw, listen to music, or exercise. If you don’t know where to start, the STOP technique can be a great meditative technique. It works like this. Stop whatever you are doing. Take a few deep breaths. Observe your emotions and thoughts as they are, not judging them as good or bad. Proceed with what you were doing. Or start something different based on what you observed. Now go forward with your life. Third, be connected. Allow yourself to ask for help from people (D) whom you can trust, such as friends, family members, or counselors. Talking about your issues with someone can help you (E) seeing your situation with more clarity and respond to it with more strength. Good communication helps resilience. This is the reason why resilient people tend to create good support networks.

solution: 앞서 제시된 안데르센과 에이미 멀린스의 일화처럼, 위대한 성공은 모두 '역경 덕분에' 탄생했다는 것이 이 글의 핵심 주제이므로 빈칸에는 성공의 필수 자양분이 되었던 'adversity'가 들어가는 것이 올바르다.

choices: It is introduced as a useful meditative tool when you are unsure of how to begin your personal time.

solution: ② 관찰 단계 동안 당신의 감정이 긍정적인지 부정적인지 '신중하게 평가해야 한다'고 진술하고 있다. 이는 본문의 'not judging'은 명상적 지침과 반대되므로 적절하지 않다. ① 어디서부터 시작해야 할지 모를 때 훌륭한 명상 기법이 될 수 있다고 했으므로 일치한다. ③ 하던 일을 즉시 멈추는 것 다음에 깊은 숨을 쉬는 단계가 오므로 절차상 일치한다. ④ 하던 일을 계속하거나 관찰에 기반해 다른 것을 시작하는 것 중 선택할 수 있다고 했으므로 일치한다. ⑤ STOP 기법을 통해 마음을 가다듬고 궁극적으로 삶을 향해 앞으로 나아가도록 돕는 것이 목적이므로 일치한다.

I am not saying that these strategies are easy or remove all stress and suffering. Still, I urge you to practice them whenever you can, particularly when you are under stress. ⓐ Remember that there is no better time to build your “resilience muscle” than the moment (A) [which / when] you are in the middle of adversity and uncertainty.
ⓑ Practicing resilience during tough times (B) [helps / help] you endure and grow stronger. ⓒ However, you can also apply these strategies to everyday small stresses or minor challenges. ⓓ As a result, professional athletes often prefer systematic physical workouts over mental training to relieve everyday anxiety. ⓔ Then you will gradually become more able to deal with big ones. Resilient people tend to be happier and more fulfilled because they are less afraid of failing or challenges. So, building resilience is the key not only to overcoming adversity but also to (C) [live / living] a happy life.

다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A),
(B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

solution: (A) 본문 중간의 'apply these strategies to everyday small stresses... Then you will gradually become more able to deal with big ones'를 통해 (A)에는 '작은, 소소한' 뜻을 가진 'minor'가 들어가야 한다. (B) 마지막 문장에서 회복탄력성은 행복한 삶을 사는 열쇠라고 했으므로 본문에 'happier and more fulfilled'를 반영한 'fulfilled'가 적절하다.

Embracing challenges and unexpected obstacles in your life can help you confront them as a learning process. Think of all the success stories that could never have happened without adversity!
choices: 역경을 피할 수 없다면 최대한 빨리 그 상황에서 벗어나는 것이 최선이다.
역경을 자연스러운 삶의 일부로 받아들이고, 통제 가능한 부 분에 집중하며 배움의 기회로 삼아야 한다.
성공한 사람들은 대부분 타고난 재능 덕분에 역경을 쉽게 극 복할 수 있었다.
스트레스를 유발하는 변화는 가능한 한 겪지 않도록 미리 예 방해야 한다.
'왜 하필 나에게'라는 질문을 던지는 것은 역경을 극복하는 데 가장 효과적인 방법이다.
solution: ② 이 글은 역경을 삶의 자연스러운 일부로 받아들이고, 바꿀 수 없는 것이 아니라 바꿀 수 있는 것에 집중하며, 이를 배움의 과정으로 마주해야 한다는 것을 핵심 메시지로 전달하고 있으므로 ②가 가장 알맞다. ① 역경에서 최대한 빨리 벗어나라는 회피적 태도를 주장하는 글이 아니므로 알맞지 않다. ③ 타고난 재능 덕분에 역경을 쉽게 극복했다는 내용은 본문에 전혀 없으므로 알맞지 않다. ④ 스트레스 유발 변화를 예방하라는 내용이 아니라 오히려 자연스러운 것으로 받아들이라는 내용이므로 알맞지 않다. ⑤ '왜 하필 나에게'라고 생각하는 것은 본문에서 지양해야 할 태도로 제시되었으므로 정반대이며 알맞지 않다.

조건 1. 'This is the reason why(이것이 ~하는 이 유이다)' 구문을 사용할 것
2. 'tend to+동사원형(~하는 경향이 있다)' 구문 을 사용할 것
3. <보기>의 단어를 모두 활용할 것 (형태 변형 가 능, 필요시 단어 추가 가능).
4. 13단어로 쓸 것
5. 대문자 및 마침표에 유의하여 쓸 것
보기 this / reason / resilient / people / tend / create / good / support / network
→ _____ .
answer: This is the reason why resilient people tend to create good support networks.
solution: 주어와 동사인 'This is'를 쓰고, 뒤에 이유를 나타내는 명사 the reason과 이를 수식하는 관계부사 why를 연결한다. why가 이끄는 절 안에서는 주어 resilient people을 쓰고, '~하는 경향이 있다'는 의미의 tend to를 쓴 뒤, 동사원형 create와 그 목적어인 good support networks를 배열하여 문장을 완성한다.

body:
다음 빈칸 ⓐ, ⓑ 에 들어갈 알맞은 말을 쓰시오.
There are countless stories of successful people who ⓐ _____ survived adversity
ⓑ _____ used it as a stepping stone to growth. Fairy tale writer Hans Andersen said that his childhood poverty, the early loss of his father, and his experience of being disrespected were the sources for his most popular stories.
ⓐ _____ (2단어)
ⓑ _____ (2단어)
1회차 실전 모의고사
solution: 주격 관계대명사 who가 이끄는 절 안에서, 앞에 언급된 두 동사구(survived adversity / used it as a stepping stone to growth)를 상관접속사로 연결하는 구조이다. 'A뿐만 아니라 B도'라는 의미를 나타내려면 ⓐ 자리에 not only, ⓑ 자리에 but also 를 써서 'not only A but also B' 구문을 완성해야 알맞다.

body:
다음 글을 읽고 추론할 수 없는 내용으로 가장 적절한 것은?
There are countless stories of successful people who not only survived adversity but used it as a stepping stone to growth. Fairy tale writer Hans Andersen said that his childhood poverty, the early loss of his father, and his experience of being disrespected were the sources for his most popular stories. “The hardship was a real blessing that inspired me to write stories like The Little Match Girl, The Snow Queen, and The Ugly Duckling.” Athlete Aimee Mullins also saw her challenges as an opportunity. She was born with a medical condition that resulted in losing both legs beneath the knee to surgery. She competed against athletes without disabilities in a national competition and participated in the Paralympics in 1996. Her career also includes modeling, acting, and public speaking. She says her physical condition is not a disability but the very thing that opened the door for her amazing potential. Both people succeeded not “despite” adversity but thanks to it. This is the real bouncing back. You might think “Hey, these are exceptional people.” However, we are all born with the potential for resilience. Just like these people, we all can develop the strength to quickly recover from a crisis that could otherwise cause lasting damage to our mental health. The good news is that resilience is like a muscle. You can build it up through practice, by developing thoughts, behaviors, and habits that allow you to recover from painful or stressful events. Here are three basic strategies to build up this “resilience muscle.”
choices: The author implies that adversity, when handled properly, can lead to unexpected opportunities.
Aimee Mullins's success suggests that a physical condition does not have to limit personal achievement.
The passage implies that building resilience requires consistent effort over time, similar to muscle training.
Hans Andersen received formal literary training focused specifically on turning grief into fiction.
The author expects that readers might initially view Andersen and Mullins as unusual exceptions.
solution: ④ Andersen이 슬픔을 소설로 전환하는 데 초점을 맞춘 정식 문학 훈련을 받았다는 내용은 본문에서 전혀 언급되지 않았으므로 추론할 수 없다. ① 역경을 '덕분에' 성공했다는 표현에서 추론할 수 있다. ② 신체적 조건이 장애가 아니라 잠재력의 문이었다는 표현에서 추론할 수 있다. ③ 근육 비유와 연습을 통한 습득이라는 표현에서 추론할 수 있다. ⑤ 'You might think, Hey, these are exceptional people'이라는 표현에서 독자가 처음엔 예외적 인물로 여길 것을 저자가 예상하고 있음을 추론할 수 있다.

밑줄 친 단어의 영영 풀이로 잘못된 것은?
Resilience: The Power to Overcome City Wellness Center Newsletter This week’s topic in the City Wellness Center Newsletter is resilience, or “the power to overcome.” Julia Hone, a famous doctor, tells us how we can deal with difficult times by cultivating our inner strength. No life is free from problems. Whatever life path we choose, we all experience adversity. This can take the form of illness, accidents, failure in exams, family and relationship issues, or other stresses. To cope, we all need the ability to overcome difficulties, which is known as resilience. Resilience means springing back, just like a bouncy ball after hitting the ground. If you are resilient, you can bounce back and recover quickly from the hard times you experience. Furthermore, you learn and grow from adversity. So, resilience is the ability to handle, recover from, and benefit from difficult life events.
choices: resilience : the ability to recover quickly from difficulties
cultivate : to completely avoid or ignore something
adversity : a difficult or unpleasant situation
take the form of : to appear or exist as a particular thing
bounce back : to return quickly to a normal condition after difficulty
solution: ② cultivate (기르다, 함양하다): 지문에서 "cultivating our inner strength(내면의 힘을 기르는 것)"라는 표현으로 사용되었다. 이는 무언가를 발전시키고 장려하며 기르는 것을 의미한다. 선택지처럼 '완전히 피하거나 무시하는 것'은 단어의 실제 의미와 정반대다. ① resilience (회복탄력성): 어려움으로부터 빠르게 회복하는 능력을 정확하게 설명하고 있다. ③ adversity (역경): 어렵거나 불쾌한 상황을 뜻하며, 지문 속 '시련'의 의미와 일치한다. ④ take the form of (~의 형태를 띠다): 특정한 사물이나 현상으로 나타나는 것을 의미한다. ⑤ bounce back (다시 회복하다): 고난 후에 정상적인 상태로 빠르게 돌아가는 동작을 '튀어 오르는 공'에 비유하여 잘 풀이했다.

Our mindset, or way of thinking, affects our ability to deal with life’s challenges. Psychologists say there are two main mindsets: “fixed” and “growth.” For people with a fixed mindset, failure just shows that their intelligence, abilities, and talents are limited. They may think, for example, “I’ve never been good at writing. I’ll never be a good writer.” Therefore, they stay in their comfort zone,
ⓐwhere they won’t be challenged. (A) They tend to reject even constructive criticism. (B) Also, other people’s success makes them feel ⓑdefeated and lose confidence.
(C) For them, failure is an opportunity. (D) They may think, for example, “I can still learn and practice writing skills until I can write a great story.” (E) They can learn from criticism, ask for advice, and ⓒbe inspired by other people’s success. A growth mindset empowers people to feel more comfortable about their imperfections and
ⓓovercomes crises or mistakes more easily. Experts say that we can develop a growth mindset through practice.
ⓔWhenever you feel “It’s impossible. I’d rather give up,” why don’t you train yourself to say, “I still want to try. I can learn how to make it possible”?

윗글의 필자가 <보기>에 있는 학생들에게 할 조언으로 올 바르게 연결된 것만을 있는 대로 고른 것은?
보기 ㉠ 주한: 난 이번 수학 시험을 망쳤어. 난 역시 수 학적 재능이 없나 봐. → 조언: 실패를 능력의 한 계로 보지 말고, 연습을 통해 능력을 키울 기회로 삼아보렴.
㉡ 해솔: 선생님의 비판 덕분에 내 글의 문제점을 알게 되었어. 더 연습해야지. → 조언: 건설적인 비판을 거부하고 너의 편안한 구역에만 머무는 것은 좋지 않아.
㉢ 시후: 친구가 경시대회에서 1등을 하니까 내 자신이 너무 초라하고 낙담하게 돼. → 조언: 타인 의 성공에 패배감을 느끼기보다, 그것을 자극제이 자 영감의 원천으로 삼아봐.
㉣ 은성: 이번 프로젝트가 비록 완벽하진 않지만, 시행착오를 통해 해결 방법을 배울 수 있을 거야.
→ 조언: 불완전함을 받아들이고 불가능을 가능 하게 만드는 훈련을 지속하는 모습이 훌륭하구나.
solution: ㉠ 주한: 시험을 망친 후 재능 탓을 하는 학생에게 성장의 기회로 삼으라는 조언은 올바르다. ㉢ 시후: 타인의 성공에 낙담하는 학생에게 영감의 원천으로 삼으라는 조언은 올바르다. ㉣ 은성: 완벽하지 않아도 배울 수 있다고 생각하는 성장 마인드셋 학생의 태도를 칭찬하는 조언은 올바르다. ㉡ 해솔: 이미 성장 마인드셋을 가지고 있으므로, 부정적인 조언을 할 필요가 없다.

밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 틀린 것끼리 짝 지어진 것은?
solution: ⓑ However → Whatever: 뒤에 명사(life path)가 바로 오고 '어떤 ~를 선택하더라도'라는 의미를 나타내야 하므로, 복합관계부사 however가 아닌 복합관계형용사 Whatever가 적절하다. (However는 뒤에 형용사나 부사가 온다.) ⓓ that → which: 콤마(,) 뒤에서 앞 문장 전체나 특정 구를 부연 설명하는 관계대명사의 계속적 용법에서는 that을 사용할 수 없으므로 which로 고쳐야 한다. ⓐ how: '어떻게 ~할 수 있는지'라는 의미의 의문사절 (간접의문문)로 명사절 역할을 충실히 하고 있다. ⓒ to overcome: 앞의 명사 ability를 수식하는 형용사적 용법의 부정사로 적절하다. ⓔ from: benefit from(~으로부터 이득을 얻다)은 하나의 구로 쓰이는 자연스러운 전치사 활용이다.

다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
We are all born with the potential for resilience. We all can develop the strength to quickly recover from a crisis
ⓐthat could otherwise cause lasting damage to our mental health. The good news is that resilience is like a muscle. You can build it up through practice, by developing thoughts, behaviors, and habits ⓑthat allow you to recover from painful or stressful events. Here are three basic strategies to build up this "resilience muscle." First, accept and respect adversity as a natural part of life. This ⓒ doesn't mean being passive, but understanding that some changes in life can cause suffering or stress. Then, instead of feeling singled out and thinking, "Why me?", you can face ⓓwhatever happening and focus on what you can change, not what you can't. Embracing challenges and unexpected obstacles in your life can help you confront them as a learning process. Think of all the success stories ⓔthat could never have happened without adversity! Second, have "me time," that is, personal time to look after yourself. Take a break and be in the present moment, neither regretting the past nor worrying about the future. Walk, meditate, write, draw, listen to music, or exercise.

solution: ④ 주어 역할을 하는 복합관계대명사 뒤에 본동사가 와야 하므로, happening은 happens로 고쳐야 한다.

"Three E _____ S _____ for B _____ Your R " First, accept and respect adversity as a natural part of life. Understand that some changes bring stress, but instead of feeling singled out, focus on what can be changed. Embracing challenges and unexpected obstacles in your life can help you confront them as a learning process. Think of all the success stories that could never have happened without adversity! Second, have "me time," that is, personal time to look after yourself. Take a break and be in the present moment, neither regretting the past nor worrying about the future. Walk, meditate, write, draw, listen to music, or exercise. If you don't know where to start, the STOP technique can be a great meditative technique. Third, be connected. Let yourself ask for help from people whom you can trust, such as friends, family members, or counselors.
