Meditation is a practice that affects the brain in several important ways. When people meditate, they focus their attention on something, such as their breath or a word, and try to clear their minds of distractions. This repeated focus trains the brain to become more aware and ⓐless reactive to stress. Studies have shown that meditation increases activity in the prefrontal cortex, the part of the brain, responsible for decision-making, attention, and self-control. At the same time, meditation can ⓑreduce activity in the amygdala, which is associated with fear and stress. As a result, people who meditate regularly often feel calmer and more focused. Meditation also
ⓒ encourages the growth of new neural connections, a process called neuroplasticity. This makes the brain more adaptable and able to
ⓓavoid challenges. In addition, meditation can improve memory, emotional regulation, and even physical health by lowering blood pressure and reducing inflammation. Overall, meditation changes the brain both structurally and functionally. By practicing it consistently, a person can become more mindful, less stressed, and
ⓔimproved at managing emotions. It is not an instant solution, but over time, meditation can help the brain function in a healthier and more balanced way.

I am not saying that these strategies are easy or remove all stress and suffering. Still, I urge you to practice them whenever you can, particularly when you are under stress. First, accept and respect adversity as a natural part of life. (A) This doesn’t mean being passive, but understanding that some changes in life can cause suffering or stress. (B) Then, instead of feeling singled out and thinking, “Why me?”, you can face ⓐwhatever happens and focus on what you can change, not what you can’t. (C) Remember that to avoid all types of stress is the single most important rule for success. (D) Embracing challenges and unexpected obstacles in your life can help you ⓑconfront them as a learning process.
(E) Think of all the success stories that could never have happened without adversity! Second, have “me time,” that is, personal time to look after yourself. Take a break and be in the present moment, neither regretting the past nor worrying about the future. Walk, meditate, write, draw, listen to music, or exercise. If you don’t know

ⓓdifferently based on what you observed. Now go forward with your life. Third, be connected. Our mindset, or way of thinking, affects our ability to deal with life's challenges. Psychologists say there are two main mindsets: "fixed" and "growth." For people with a fixed mindset, failure just shows that their intelligence, abilities, and talents are limited. They may think, for example, "I've never been good at writing. I'll never be a good writer." Therefore, they stay in their comfort zone, where they won't be challenged. They tend to reject even constructive criticism. Also, other people's success makes them feel defeated and lose confidence. Meanwhile, people with a growth mindset accept life's challenges. For them, failure is an opportunity. They may think, for example, "I can still learn and practice writing skills until I can write a great story." They can learn from criticism, ask for advice, and be inspired by other people's success. A growth mindset empowers people to feel more comfortable about their imperfections and overcome crises or mistakes more easily. Experts say that we can develop a growth mindset through practice. Whenever you feel "It's impossible. I'd rather give up," why don't you train yourself to say, "I still want to try. I can learn how to make it possible"? 3회차 실전 모의고사
choices: I know it really hurts when someone criticizes me, but I believe it will help me grow.
I didn't do well this time, but if I figure out what I did wrong, I might improve next time.
When I see other people succeed, I try to use their success as inspiration to keep working.
When I get a low score, I read the teacher's comments carefully so I can fix my mistakes next time.
I'm just not the type of person who can understand math. No matter how hard I try, my math score won't improve.

Then, instead of feeling singled out and thinking, "Why me?", you can face whatever happens and focus on what you can change, not what you can't. Embracing challenges and unexpected obstacles in your life can help you confront them as a learning process. Think of all the success stories that could never have happened without adversity! Second, have "me time," that is, personal time to look after yourself. Take a break and be in the present moment, ㉠(과거를 후회하지도 미래를 걱정하지 도 말고 / the past, the future, nor). Walk, meditate, write, draw, listen to music, or exercise. If you don't know where to start, the STOP technique can be a great meditative technique. It works like this. Stop whatever you are doing. Take a few deep breaths. ⓐObserve your emotions and thoughts as they are, not judging them as good or bad. ㉡(하고 있던 것을 (다시) 계속하세요 / you, what ).
Or start something different based on what you observed. Now go forward with your life. Third, be connected.
(A)Talking about your issues with them can help you see your situation with more clarity and respond to it with more strength. (B)This is the reason why resilient people tend to create good support networks. (C)Good communication helps resilience. (D)Allow yourself to ask for help from people whom you can trust, such as friends, family members, or counselors.

윗글의 내용상 밑줄 친 문장 (A)~(D)의 배열로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 회복탄력성을 기르기 위한 전략인 소통을 제안하는 내용의 (D) 다음에는, 문제에 대해 이야기하는 것이 상황을 명확히 보게 돕는다는 내용의 (A)가 이어져야 한다. 그다음에는 좋은 의사소통이 회복탄력성을 돕는다는 내용의 (C)가 온 후, 이것이 회복탄력성 있는 사람들이 좋은 지원망을 만드는 이유라는 내용의 (B)로 마무리되는 것이 글의 순서로 가장 적절하다. 따라서 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은 ④이다.

I am not saying that the three basic strategies for resilience muscle are easy or remove all stress and suffering.
(A) Practicing resilience during tough times helps you endure and grow stronger. However, you can also apply these strategies to everyday small stresses or minor challenges.
(B) Still, I urge you to practice them whenever you can, particularly when you are under stress. Remember that there is no better time to build your "resilience muscle" than the moment when you are in the middle of adversity and uncertainty.
(C) Then you will gradually become more able to deal with big ones. Resilient people tend to be happier and more fulfilled because they are less afraid of failing or challenges. So, building resilience is the key not only to overcoming adversity but also to living a happy life.

ⓓis

Our mindset, or way of thinking, affects our ability to deal with life's challenges. Psychologists say there are two main mindsets: "fixed" and "growth."
(A) Meanwhile, people with a growth mindset accept life's challenges. For them, failure is an opportunity. They may think, for example, "I can still learn and practice writing skills until I can write a great story." They can learn from criticism, ask for advice, and be inspired by other people's success. A growth mindset empowers people to feel more comfortable about their imperfections and overcome crises or mistakes more easily.
(B) For people with a fixed mindset, failure just shows that their intelligence, abilities, and talents are limited. They may think, for example, "I've never been good at writing. I'll never be a good writer." Therefore, they stay in their comfort zone, where they won't be challenged. They tend to reject even constructive criticism. Also, other people's success makes them feel defeated and lose confidence.
(C) Experts say that we can develop a growth mindset through practice. Whenever you feel "It's impossible. I'd rather give up," why don't you train yourself to say, "I still want to try. I can learn how to make it possible"?

We had to hike about two miles up, to the top of the ridge, (A)[which / where] we checked our climbing gear, picked up a spare rope (B)[who / that] we had in our backpack, and practiced tying knots with the spare. My brother did well. Then it was my turn. I removed my harness. I lifted up my backup carabiner. I clipped it onto the anchor, tested the strength of the connection, and when I pulled on it, it slipped loose. Then the rope (C)[which / by which] connected that carabiner to my harness, my only safety line, came undone and gear from my pack came tumbling down the slope.

(C)[If / Because] the project works well, then other buildings will receive the same treatment—even the City Council building! *river water system: 하천 순환 시스템

• I have two nieces, (B)[that / who] are studying music.
• He returned to his old school, (C)[which / where] he first met his best friend.
solution: (A) ‘그녀가 무엇을 결정하든지’라는 의미이며 whatever가 decides의 목적어 역할을 하므로 whatever가 알맞다. (B) 콤마로 연결된 계속적 용법에서는 관계대명사 that을 쓸 수 없으므로 who가 알맞다. (C) 콤마 뒤에 완전한 절 he first met his best friend가 이어지고 선행사가 장소이므로 관계부사 where가 알맞다. 따라서 ⑤ whatever - who - where가 적절하다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
(A), (B), (C)의 각 괄호 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
The marketplace connects buyers and sellers worldwide. We can list products on the platform as well as (A)[purchase / purchasing] them instantly, which makes the system more efficient. With a few clicks, people can compare prices, place orders, and leave reviews. But the marketplace is not only for shopping. It is also a place (B)[which / where] we can interact with other sellers. Many people use it to share their own experiences. They can also comment on or even (C)[rate / rating] the experiences of others in some cases.
solution: (A) can list ~ as well as purchase ~에서 list와 병렬 구조를 이루므로 동사원형 purchase가 와야 한다. (B) 장소를 나타내는 선행사 a place 뒤에 완전한 절 we can interact with other sellers가 이어지므로 관계부사 where가 적절하다. (C) can also comment on or even rate ~에서 comment on과 병렬 구조를 이루므로 동사원형 rate가 와야 한다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 글에서 틀린 부분을 두 군데 찾아 바르게 고쳐 쓰시오.
The reason how iron turns rusty is related to oxygen and moisture in the environment. When exposed to water and oxygen, the iron undergoes chemical reactions, some of them are responsible for forming rust. This process produces a reddish-brown coating on the surface. Further corrosion can make the rust layer flaky, creating a rough, crumbling surface. (1) _____ → (2) _____ →
answer: (1) how, why (2) some of them, some of which
solution: (1) 'reason' 뒤에는 관계부사 why가 와야 하므로 how는 why로 고쳐야 한다. (2) 'chemical reactions, some of them are responsible for forming rust'는 쉼표만으로 두 개의 독립된 절을 연결하고 있으므로, 대명사 them을 관계대명사 which로 바꾸어 'some of which are responsible for forming rust'로 고쳐야 한다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 글을 읽고, 우리말과 일치하도록 조건에 맞게 쓰시오.
A mountain town depends heavily on its location for safety. 화산으로부터 너무 가깝지도 너무 멀지도 않아 서, it enjoys fertile soil without facing constant danger. Nearby, thick forests shield the town from strong winds. Without this careful placement, farming there would be impossible.
조건 1. 「neither A nor B」 구문을 이용할 것
2. too, near, far, from을 이용할 것 (중복 사용 가능)
3. 9단어로 쓸 것
→
answer: Neither too near nor too far from the volcano
solution: neither A nor B 구문으로 too near와 too far from the volcano를 병렬 연결한 표현이다. 화산에 너무 가깝지도 너무 멀지도 않다는 의미이며, near와 far를 병렬로 사용해 두 경우를 모두 부정한다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장끼리 짝지어진 것은?
ⓐShe attended a workshop whose focus was to improve teamwork skills.
ⓑDo you know something it will keep the file from being deleted?
ⓒDo you know the reason why she resigned from her position?
ⓓWhatever it caused the delay is being investigated now.
ⓔCan you show me the office where is decorated for the party?
ⓕTom has two colleagues with whom he shares an apartment.
solution: 정답은 ① b, d, e이다. b. 'Do you know something it will keep the file from being deleted?'는 관계대명사 없이 대명사 it이 불필요하게 남아있어 틀리다. → 'Do you know something that will keep the file from being deleted?'로 고쳐야 한다. d. 'Whatever it caused the delay is being investigated now.'에서 whatever는 이미 '~하는 것은 무엇이든'의 의미로 주어 역할을 하므로 it을 추가로 쓰면 안 된다. → 'Whatever caused the delay is being investigated now.'로 고쳐야 한다. e. 'Can you show me the office where is decorated for the party?'에서 관계부사 where 뒤에는 완전한 문장이 와야 하는데 주어가 없어 불완전하다. → 'Can you show me the office which is decorated for the party?'로 고쳐야 한다. a, c, f는 각각 소유격 관계대명사 whose, 관계부사 why, '전치사+관계대명사' with whom이 올바르게 사용되었다. YBM(박) 3과 문법 정복 실전
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장끼리 짝지어진 것은?
ⓐThey visited a school whose principal was very kind.
ⓑIs there anything it will prevent the rain from entering?
ⓒDo you understand the reason why he was late for class?
ⓓWhatever it troubled him was solved eventually.
ⓔDo you know the store where is famous for its bread?
ⓕWe met three tourists with whom we shared a taxi.
solution: 정답은 ④ b, d, e이다. b. 'Is there anything it will prevent the rain from entering?'는 관계대명사가 빠지고 대명사 it이 불필요하게 남아있어 틀리다. → 'Is there anything that will prevent the rain from entering?'으로 고쳐야 한다. d. 'Whatever it troubled him was solved eventually.'에서 whatever는 이미 '~하는 것은 무엇이든'의 의미를 포함하므로 it을 함께 쓰면 안 된다. → 'Whatever troubled him was solved eventually.'로 고쳐야 한다. e. 'Do you know the store where is famous for its bread?'에서 관계부사 where 뒤에는 완전한 문장이 와야 하는데 주어가 없어 불완전하다. → 'Do you know the store which is famous for its bread?'로 고쳐야 한다. a, c, f는 각각 소유격 관계대명사 whose, 관계부사 why, '전치사+관계대명사' with whom이 올바르게 사용되었다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장을 고르시오.
choices: Unless the weather improves, the game will be canceled.
Water the plants, or they will wither.
Some tourists preferred the beach, while others chose the mountains.
The coach, as well as the players, are excited about the tournament.
The focus of the training is not speed but accuracy.
solution: ④ are → is as well as로 연결된 문장에서 동사는 앞에 나온 주어인 The coach(단수)에 일치시켜야 하므로 are가 아니라 is를 써야 한다. ① Unless를 이용한 조건 표현으로 어법상 옳다. ② 명령문 뒤에 or가 이어지는 조건 표현으로 어법상 옳다. ③ while을 이용한 대조 표현으로 어법상 옳다. ⑤ not A but B 구조로 주어 The focus가 단수이므로 is가 알맞다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말이 순서대로 짝지어진 것을 고르시오.
• The museum displayed several statues, one of dated back centuries.
• They moved to a village _____ life was much slower.
solution: 정답은 ①이다. 첫 번째 빈칸은 전치사 of 뒤에 사물을 가리키는 관계대명사가 필요하므로 which가 적절하다. 두 번째 빈칸은 장소를 나타내는 선행사 village를 받아 완전한 문장을 이끄는 관계부사 where가 와야 한다. ② them - that: them은 관계사가 아니어서 절을 연결할 수 없다. ③ them - where: 첫 번째 빈칸에 관계사가 필요하므로 부적절하다. ④ which - which: 두 번째 빈칸 뒤에 완전한 문장이 오므로 관계대명사 which는 쓸 수 없다. ⑤ what - where: what은 선행사를 포함하므로 statues라는 선행사가 있는 문장에는 쓸 수 없다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 문장에서 어법상 틀린 부분을 찾아 바르게 고쳐 쓰시오.
The Renaissance was a period which artists were creating masterpieces of great beauty.
→
solution: 선행사 a period가 시간을 나타내고 관계사절 안에서 부사 역할을 하므로 관계대명사 which 대신 관계부사 when을 써야 한다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 문장을 읽고, 관계사를 이용한 한 문장으로 바꿔 쓰시오.
A stadium is a large venue for sports events. Thousands of fans gather there.
→
answer: A stadium is a large venue for sports events where thousands of fans gather.
solution: there가 앞 문장의 장소(a large venue for sports events)를 가리키므로, 관계부사 where로 바꾸어 두 문장을 한 문장으로 만든다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 문장을 읽고, 관계사를 이용한 한 문장으로 바꿔 쓰시오.
A greenhouse is a structure made of glass. Plants are grown there.
→
answer: A greenhouse is a structure made of glass where plants are grown.
solution: 두 번째 문장의 there는 앞 문장의 장소(a structure made of glass)를 가리키므로, 장소를 나타내는 관계부사 where로 바꾸어 한 문장으로 연결한다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 문장을 읽고, 괄호 안에서 어법상 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
Astronomers study the regions of the sky [that / where] cannot be observed without powerful equipment.
solution: 밑줄 뒤 절 'cannot be observed without powerful equipment'에는 주어가 없는 불완전한 절이다. 주어 역할을 하는 관계대명사 that이 와야 하며, 완전한 절을 요구하는 관계부사 where는 올 수 없다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 문장에서 어법상 틀린 부분을 찾아 바르게 고치고, 그 이유를 우리말로 쓰시오.
Not only the students in the class but also their teacher aren't happy about the new rule. (1) 틀린 부분: _____ → (2) 틀린 이유:
answer: (1) aren't → isn't (2) their teacher가 동사 바로 앞에 있는 단수 주어이므로 동사도 단수형인 isn't가 되어야 한다.
solution: not only A but also B'에서는 동사가 가까운 주어에 수일치하므로 their teacher에 맞춰 단수형 isn't가 적절하다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말이 바르게 짝지어진 것을 고르시오.
• The nurse as well as the patients pleased with the new schedule.
• Neither the doctors nor the nurse notified about the change.
solution: • 첫 번째 문장은 A as well as B에서 동사의 수를 A에 일치시킨다. 주어의 중심인 The nurse가 단수이므로 was pleased가 적절하다. • 두 번째 문장은 neither A nor B에서 동사는 가까운 주어 B에 일치시킨다. 동사에 가까운 the nurse가 단수이므로 was notified가 적절하다. 따라서 정답은 ③ was - was이다. YBM(박) 3과 문법 정복 실전
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은 모두 몇 개인가?
(a) The reports that James hurriedly submitted was incomplete.
(b) Nora forgot her umbrella, which caused her to get wet.
(c) Ben used the old ladder where he found in the garage.
(d) This is why he skipped the meeting.
(e) Most of the workers, who ranged in age from 20 to 50, joined the union. (f) However difficult it is, you should stay calm. (g) Do you know the day which we have no classes?
solution: (a) 주어 The reports가 복수이므로 동사는 was가 아니라 were를 써야 한다. 따라서 ‘was incomplete’를 ‘were incomplete’로 고쳐야 한다. (c) 선행사 the old ladder는 사물이고, 관계절에서 found의 목적어가 필요하므로 where가 아니라 that 또는 which를 써야 한다. 따라서 ‘where he found’를 ‘that he found’ 또는 ‘which he found’로 고쳐야 한다. (g) 뒤의 ‘we have no classes’가 완전한 절이므로 관계대명사 which가 아니라 시간을 나타내는 관계부사 when이 적절하다. 따라서 ‘the day which’를 ‘the day when’으로 고쳐야 한다. (b) which는 앞 문장 전체의 내용을 받아 계속적 용법으로 쓰였다. (d) ‘This is why ~’에서 why가 이유를 나타내는 관계부사로 적절하다. (e) who는 선행사 Most of the workers를 보충 설명하는 계속적 용법의 관계대명사로 적절하다. (f) ‘However + 형용사 + 주어 + 동사’ 구조가 올바르게 쓰였다. 따라서 틀린 문장은 (a), (c), (g)로 총 3개이므로 정답은 ④이다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말이 바르게 짝지어진 것은?
• The reason _____ the flight was delayed hasn't been announced yet.
• This is the movie _____ critics have been raving about.
solution: 첫 번째 빈칸은 선행사 reason 뒤에 오는 관계사 자리이다. 뒤의 ‘the flight was delayed’가 완전한 절이므로 이유를 나타내는 관계부사 why가 적절하다. which는 관계절 안에서 주어나 목적어 등의 역할을 해야 하므로 이 자리에는 적절하지 않다. how는 the reason과 함께 쓰지 않는다. 두 번째 빈칸은 선행사 movie를 수식하며, 관계절의 ‘raving about’에서 about의 목적어가 필요하므로 목적격 관계대명사 which가 적절하다. 따라서 정답은 ① why - which이다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말에 맞도록 [보기]에 주어진 단어를 이 용하여 빈칸을 완성하세요. (단어 추가 및 어형 변화 금지)
Studies of urban parks around the world reveal how creative activities can transform public spaces into lively gathering spots. People often stop to observe artists at work rather than simply passing through empty pathways. Faced with the choice between a quiet path and one filled with creative energy, most visitors choose the livelier option. The stroll feels more interesting and pleasant. (A)관광객들이 예술가들이 그림을 그리는 것을 볼 수 있는 공원들은 많은 사람들을 끌어들여 앉아서 구경하 게 한다. Studies of park benches show that seats offering a clear view of artists at work are used far more frequently than those without such a view.
보기 many people / can / see / artists / tourists / where / attract / paint
→Parks _____ to sit and watch.
answer: where tourists can see artists paint, attract many people
solution: 'where'가 이끄는 관계부사절이 선행사 'Parks'를 수식하며, 절 안에는 'can see + 목적어 + 동사원형(지각동사 구문)'이 쓰였다. 주절의 동사 'attract' 뒤에 목적어 'many people'이 온다. 빈칸1에는 관계부사절이, 빈칸2에는 'attract + 목적어'가 들어가야 한다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
(A), (B), (C)의 각 괄호 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
Legend abounds with remarkable stories (A)
[regard / regarding] the invention of the telephone. Popular tales include those of inventors racing to patent similar devices, each claiming credit for the breakthrough. The device was first demonstrated in Boston, the American city (B)[which / where] it was unveiled in the late nineteenth century. The world's most transformative invention, the telephone is also one of the most influential. Is it any wonder when you consider that it is so practical, easy to use, and essential for communication? Add to that, the fact that it connects people across great distances and supports countless industries, plus being constantly improved and upgraded (C)
[mean / means] it remains indispensable today. It continues to shape how we communicate.
solution: (A)에는 뒤에 명사구(the invention of the telephone)가 이어지므로 전치사 역할을 하는 분사형 regarding이 와야 한다. regard는 동사로 쓰이므로 이 문맥에 맞지 않는다. (B)에는 장소를 나타내는 선행사 the American city 뒤에 완전한 절(it was unveiled in the late nineteenth century)이 이어지므로 관계부사 where가 와야 한다. which 뒤에는 불완전한 절이 와야 하므로 적절하지 않다. (C)의 주어는 the fact that ~, plus being ~로 이어지는 하나의 긴 명사구이며 단수로 취급되므로 단수동사 means가 와야 한다. 따라서 정답은 ① regarding - where - means이다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
우리말과 같은 의미가 되도록 빈칸에 알맞은 관계사를 고르시오.
Michael은 우리가 만날 수 있는 카페를 추천했다.
= Michael recommended a cafe _____ we can meet.
solution: 선행사 'a cafe'에 대한 관계부사 'where'가 필요한데, 관계부사는 '전치사 + 관계대명사'를 대신하므로 'in which'가 적절하다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
우리말과 같은 의미가 되도록 빈칸에 알맞은 관계사를 고르시오.
Emily는 아이들이 놀 수 있는 공원을 보여주었다.
= Emily showed us a park _____ children can play.
solution: 선행사 'a park'에 대한 관계부사 'where'가 필요한데, 관계부사는 '전치사 + 관계대명사'를 대신하므로 'in which'가 적절하다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body: 밑줄 친 부분이 문법상 틀린 것을 고르시오.
choices: Not only Tom but also his friends was invited.
Either Kate or her sisters are coming tonight.
Both the book and the pen are on the table.
Neither the teacher nor the students understand the problem.
Either the dogs or the cat needs to be fed.
solution: ① was → were 'not only A but also B'와 같이 상관접속사로 연결된 A와 B가 주어일 때 동사의 수는 'B'에 일치시킨다. 즉, 'was'가 아니라 'were'이 와야한다. 다만, 'both A and B'에는 복수동사를 쓴다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body: 밑줄 친 부분이 문법상 틀린 것을 고르시오.
choices: Both Mike and Sarah have finished their work.
Either the manager or his assistants is responsible.
Neither the coffee nor the tea tastes good today.
Not only the students but also the professor was surprised.
Either my parents or I am going to the meeting.
solution: ② is → are 'either A or B'와 같이 상관접속사로 연결된 A와 B가 주어일 때 동사의 수는 'B'에 일치시킨다. 즉, 'is'가 아니라 'are'이 와야한다. 다만, 'both A and B'에는 복수동사를 쓴다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body: 다음 중 어법상 어색한 것을 고르시오.
choices: This is the library where I study every weekend.
I still remember the time when we first met.
Do you know the reason why she left for?
That's exactly the way he approached the issue.
There's a café nearby where delicious coffee is served.
solution: 관계부사 why는 전치사구인 for the reason을 대신한다. 즉, 문장 끝에 전치사 for가 남아 있으면 관계부사 why를 쓸 수 없다. 따라서 why를 관계대명사 which로 바꾸거나, for를 삭제해야 한다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body: 다음 중 어법상 어색한 문장을 고르시오.
choices: She doesn't understand how to behave appropriately at work.
This is the restaurant where I used to eat when I was young.
See how excited my cat gets whenever she sees me.
She left the office without the manager's approval.
There are several situations what her advice is required.
solution: situations과 같은 추상적인 장소/상황을 나타내는 선행사 뒤에는 관계부사 where를 사용해야 한다. what은 선행사가 없을 때만 쓰므로, 앞에 명사가 있는 이 문장 구조에서는 사용할 수 없다. YBM(박) 3과 문법 정복 실전
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 생략 가능한 것끼리 짝지어진 것을 고르시오.
• There are volunteer opportunities to ⓐwhich have access at the local library..
• Sarah felt thankful for the gift ⓑthat she received from her grandmother.
• They visited a museum ⓒwhich ancient artifacts are located at.
• Many visitors arrived late, ⓓwhich was causing delays in the event.
• She recalls the moment ⓔwhen she won her first competition.
solution: ⓑ이어지는 절에 목적어가 빠진 목적격 관계대명사는 생략이 가능하다. ⓒ이어지는 절에 전치사의 목적어가 빠진 목적격 관계대명사는 생략이 가능하다.ⓔ시간을 나타내는 관계부사 when은 선행사나 관계사를 생략 가능하다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 (A), (B), (C)의 각 네모 안에서 어법상 옳은 표현으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
• She fixed the computer (A)[which / who] she purchased two years ago.
• The month (B)[when / where] I enjoy outdoor activities is April.
• The artist is a creative painter (C)[which / whose] style is unique.
solution: (A)는 선행사 'computer'가 사물이므로 관계대명사 'which'가 옳다. (B)는 선행사 'month'가 시간을 나타내므로 관계부사 'when'이 옳다. (C)는 뒤의 명사 'style'의 소유격이 필요하므로 관계대명사 'whose'가 옳다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 글을 읽고, 물음에 답하시오.
The history of architecture is usually divided into three periods—Ancient, Medieval, and Modern. Ancient Architecture begins with the earliest cultures ⓐof which we have any reliable records, and ⓑextend to the fall of the Roman Empire in the West, A.D. 476. Medieval Architecture, though it looked very different ⓒfrom which earlier builders had imagined, embraces the period, about one thousand years in length, ⓓlying between the fall of Rome and the voyages of Columbus, A.D. 1492. Modern Architecture begins with the close of the medieval period and continues to shape cities today. We do not know exactly when people first began building shelters, but historians report ⓔthat, as early as 4000 B.C., (A)이미 사람들이 예술과 종교를 발전시킨 도시들과 마 을들이 있었다.

밑줄 친 (A)를 아래 조건에 맞게 영작하시오.
조건 1. 관계부사를 사용할 것
2. 아래 단어를 사용할 것 (필요 시 변형 가능)
(there, cities, towns, people, develop, religion)
→
answer: There were cities and towns where people had already developed art and religion.
solution: 장소를 나타내는 선행사 cities and towns를 수식하는 관계부사 where를 사용하여 문장을 완성한다. develop은 과거완료 had developed로 바꾸어 써야 한다. There were cities and towns where people had already developed art and religion.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 중 어법상 맞는 문장의 개수는?
ⓐHe grew up in the village where his grandparents lived.
ⓑThey admired the artist whom paintings were famous.
ⓒThe team lost the game, which disappointed the fans.
ⓓShe has several cousins, two of whom live abroad.
ⓔYou may leave the room whenever you finish the test.
ⓕThe workshop will start next Monday, when it has been postponed twice.
solution: a, c, d, e가 어법상 맞아 총 4개이다. a의 'where his grandparents lived'는 장소를 나타내는 'the village'를 수식하므로 적절하다. b는 '그 예술가의 그림들'이라는 소유 관계이므로 'whom paintings'가 아니라 'whose paintings'가 되어야 한다. c의 'which'는 앞 절 전체를 받아 '그것이 팬들을 실망시켰다'는 의미를 나타내므로 적절하다. d의 'two of whom'은 여러 사촌 중 두 명을 나타내는 비제한적 관계대명사 표현으로 적절하다. e의 'whenever'는 '시험을 끝낼 때마다/끝내면 언제든'이라는 시간의 의미로 적절하다. f는 '다음 월요일에 시작할 것이다'와 '두 번 연기되었다'는 내용을 'when'으로 연결할 수 없으므로 부적절하다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
우리말과 같은 의미가 되도록 빈칸에 알맞은 관계사를 고르시오.
그녀가 그 과제를 완성할 수 있는 여러 방법들이 있다.
= There are several ways _____ she can complete the assignment.
solution: <방법>을 나타내는 선행사에는 관계부사 'how'를 쓰는데, 선행사 'way'와 관계부사 'how'는 둘 중 하나를 반드시 생략하거나 'how' 대신 'that'이나 'in which'를 쓴다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 적절한 것끼리 짝지어진 것은?
When I entered the conference hall, I could really feel the event's energy. There were several booths near the entrance, (A) displayed the company's newest products. There was also a lounge area (B) _____ employees could relax and chat with colleagues.
solution: (A) 콤마 뒤에 주어가 없는 불완전한 절 displayed the company's newest products가 이어지므로 선행사 several booths를 주어로 받는 관계대명사 which가 알맞다. (B) 뒤에 완전한 절 employees could relax and chat with colleagues가 이어지고 선행사 a lounge area가 장소를 나타내므로 관계부사 where가 알맞다. 따라서 ④ which - where가 적절하다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 글을 읽고, 우리말과 일치하도록 조건에 맞게 쓰시오.
A good campsite must be located carefully among the trees. 불로부터 너무 가깝지도 너무 멀지도 않아서, it keeps campers warm without any danger. Nearby, the thick forest blocks the cold night wind. Without this ideal spot, camping would be very uncomfortable.
조건 1. 「neither A nor B」 구문을 이용할 것
2. too, near, far, from을 이용할 것 (중복 사용 가능)
3. 9단어로 쓸 것
→
answer: Neither too near nor too far from the fire
solution: neither A nor B 구문을 이용하여 too near와 too far from the fire를 병렬로 연결한 표현이다. 캠프장이 불에 너무 가깝지도 너무 멀지도 않다는 의미를 나타낸다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 적절한 것끼리 짝지어진 것은?
After I entered the school gym, I could really enjoy the festival. There were many booths on the left side, (A) _____ were run by students and teachers. There was also a reading corner
(B) _____ visitors could borrow books freely.
solution: (A) 콤마 뒤에 주어가 없는 불완전한 절 were run by students and teachers가 이어지므로 선행사 many booths를 주어로 받는 관계대명사 which가 알맞다. (B) 뒤에 완전한 절 visitors could borrow books freely가 이어지고 선행사 a reading corner가 장소를 나타내므로 관계부사 where가 알맞다. 따라서 ① which - where가 적절하다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장끼리 짝지어진 것은?
ⓐHe joined a club whose members love hiking.
ⓑDo you have anything it will stop the leak from spreading?
ⓒDo you know the reason why the birds migrate south?
ⓓWhatever it damaged the fence needs repair.
ⓔDo you remember the park where is known for its lake?
ⓕSarah has four friends with whom she volunteers regularly.
solution: 정답은 ⑤ b, d, e이다. b. 'Do you have anything it will stop the leak from spreading?'는 관계대명사가 없고 대명사 it이 불필요하게 남아있어 틀리다. → 'Do you have anything that will stop the leak from spreading?'로 고쳐야 한다. d. 'Whatever it damaged the fence needs repair.'에서 whatever는 이미 '~하는 것은 무엇이든'의 의미로 주어 역할을 하므로 it을 추가로 쓰면 안 된다. → 'Whatever damaged the fence needs repair.'로 고쳐야 한다. e. 'Do you remember the park where is known for its lake?'에서 관계부사 where 뒤에는 완전한 문장이 와야 하는데 주어가 없어 불완전하다. → 'Do you remember the park which is known for its lake?'로 고쳐야 한다. a, c, f는 각각 소유격 관계대명사 whose, 관계부사 why, '전치사+관계대명사' with whom이 올바르게 사용되었다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 글을 읽고, 우리말과 일치하도록 조건에 맞게 쓰시오.
A fishing village should be built along a stable shoreline. 해안으로부터 너무 가깝지도 너무 멀지도 않아 서, it stays safe from storms while still allowing easy fishing. Nearby, the rocky cliffs protect the docks from strong waves. Without this balanced location, the village would face constant danger.
조건 1. 「neither A nor B」 구문을 이용할 것
2. too, near, far, from을 이용할 것 (중복 사용 가능)
3. 9단어로 쓸 것
→
answer: Neither too near nor too far from the coast
solution: neither A nor B 구문을 활용하여 too near와 too far from the coast를 병렬로 연결한 표현이다. 해안에 너무 가깝지도 너무 멀지도 않다는 의미를 나타내며, near와 far를 대조하여 거리를 표현한다. YBM(박) 3과 문법 정복 실전
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말이 순서대로 짝지어진 것을 고르시오.
• There were five paintings, one of had unusual colors.
• I stayed at a hotel _____ the staff were extremely kind.
solution: 정답은 ②이다. 첫 번째 빈칸은 전치사 of 뒤에 사물을 가리키는 관계대명사가 와야 하므로 which가 적절하다 (them은 전치사 뒤에서 관계사절을 이끌 수 없다). 두 번째 빈칸은 장소를 나타내는 선행사 hotel을 받아 완전한 문장을 이끄는 관계부사 where가 와야 한다. ① them - that: them은 관계사가 아니므로 관계사절을 이룰 수 없다. ③ them - where: 첫 번째 빈칸에 관계사가 필요하므로 them은 부적절하다. ④ which - which: 두 번째 빈칸은 완전한 문장이 이어지므로 관계대명사 which는 쓸 수 없다. ⑤ what - where: what은 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사이므로 선행사 paintings가 있는 문장에는 쓸 수 없다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말이 순서대로 짝지어진 것을 고르시오.
• She showed me ten bracelets, one of was made of silver.
• We ate at a restaurant _____ the chef prepared everything by hand.
solution: 정답은 ⑤이다. 첫 번째 빈칸은 전치사 of 뒤에 사물을 가리키는 관계대명사가 필요하므로 which가 적절하다. 두 번째 빈칸은 장소를 나타내는 선행사 restaurant를 받아 완전한 문장을 이끄는 관계부사 where가 와야 한다. ① them - that: them은 관계사가 아니어서 절을 연결할 수 없다. ② them - where: 첫 번째 빈칸에 관계사가 필요하므로 부적절하다. ③ which - which: 두 번째 빈칸 뒤에 완전한 문장이 오므로 관계대명사 which는 쓸 수 없다. ④ what - where: what은 선행사를 포함하므로 bracelets라는 선행사가 있는 문장에는 쓸 수 없다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중 어법상 틀린 것끼리 짝지어진 것을 고르시오.
• Neither the teacher nor the students ⓐwas prepared for the sudden quiz.
• That she works overtime every day ⓑsurprises her colleagues.
• The manager along with the employees ⓒare attending the company meeting.
• Either practicing regularly or taking private lessons ⓓis necessary to master the piano.
• As soon as the rain ⓔwill stop, we will go out for a walk.
• Can you tell me when the movie ⓕwill start tonight?
solution: ⓐNeither은 동사와 가까운 명사에 수일치를 하므로 the students에 수일치하면 was를 were로 고쳐야 한다. ⓒ 주어 The manager에 수일치하면 are이 아니라 is를 써야 한다. ⓔ 시간을 나타내는 부사절에서는 현재시제가 미래시제를 대신하므로 will stop을 stops로 고쳐야 한다. 따라서 정답은 ②ⓐ, ⓒ, ⓔ이다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 문장에서 어법상 틀린 부분을 찾아 바르게 고치고, 그 이유를 우리말로 쓰시오.
Not only the teacher but also the students doesn't finish the project on time. (1) 틀린 부분: _____ → (2) 틀린 이유:
실전 학습
answer: (1) doesn't → don't (2) the students가 동사 바로 앞에 있는 복수 주어이므로 동 사도 복수형인 don't가 되어야 한다.
solution: not only A but also B'에서는 동사가 가까운 주어에 수일치하므로 the students에 맞춰 복수형 don't가 적절하다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말이 바르게 짝지어진 것을 고르시오.
• The players as well as their coach excited about the victory.
• Neither the coach nor the players blamed for the loss.
solution: • 첫 번째 문장은 A as well as B에서 동사의 수를 A에 일치시킨다. 주어의 중심인 The players가 복수이므로 were excited가 적절하다. • 두 번째 문장은 neither A nor B에서 동사는 가까운 주어 B에 일치시킨다. 동사에 가까운 the players가 복수이므로 were blamed가 적절하다. 따라서 정답은 ⑤ were - were이다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말이 바르게 짝지어진 것을 고르시오.
• The passengers as well as the driver injured in the accident.
• Neither the players nor the coach present at the meeting.
solution: • 첫 번째 문장은 A as well as B에서 동사의 수는 A에 일치시킨다. 주어의 중심은 복수명사 The passengers이므로 were injured가 적절하다. • 두 번째 문장은 neither A nor B에서 동사는 가까운 주어 B에 일치시킨다. 동사에 가까운 the coach가 단수이므로 was present가 적절하다. 따라서 정답은 ④ were - was이다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 것을 고르시오.
choices: Both doctors and nurses have adapted quickly to the new hospital system.
Neither the director nor the actors wants to change the ending of the film.
Tell me whether the results are going to be announced this week.
Who do you think has organized this entire event?
We don't know who we are expected to become in the next decade.
solution: ② 'Neither A nor B' 구문에서 동사는 더 가까운 명사인 B에 일치시켜야 하는데, 'the actors'가 복수이므로 동사는 'wants'가 아니라 'want'가 되어야 한다. ①'Both A and B'는 항상 복수로 취급하므로 'have adapted'는 옳다. ③whether절이 동사 'tell'의 목적어로 쓰인 명사절 구조로 옳다. ④의문사 'Who'가 주어 역할을 하고 'do you think'가 삽입된 간접의문문 구조로 옳다. ⑤who가 이끄는 간접의문문에서 who가 become의 보어 역할을 하므로 옳다. body:
다음 글 (A), (B)의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 바른 것끼리 짝 지은 것은?
(A) Consider your typical café visit. You walk in and order a latte made from milk sourced from local farms and coffee beans ⓐroast in facilities in Colombia. You then find a seat and ⓑscroll through your phone while waiting for your drink to be prepared. Every cup you enjoy connects you to countless workers you will never meet. Those workers harvesting your coffee are not acting purely out of kindness. ⓒNor a large corporation is compelling them to satisfy your cravings. Instead, they provide these goods because they earn a living in return.
(B) It turns out that the recent boom in global connectivity is not due to a single invention, ⓓbut rather for the countless innovations made to communication infrastructure. From a technological and social perspective, these developments have been nothing short of extraordinary. For example, barriers such as illiteracy, distance, and cost have been reduced through affordable devices. Furthermore, technologies designed to connect people have become available to the masses, whether ⓔvia satellite internet or undersea fiber-optic cables, which alone have linked remote regions to the rest of the world. These impressive shifts have not only changed how people communicate,
ⓕbut also determine how societies will build relationships. 실전 학습
solution: 정답은 ④이다. (A)에서 ⓑ는 주어 you가 이끄는 두 동사 find와 scroll이 and로 병렬 연결된 구조로 둘 다 동사원형이 쓰였으므로 어법상 옳다. (B)에서 ⓔ는 whether via A or B 구문에서 전치사 via의 목적어로 두 개의 명사구(satellite internet, undersea fiber-optic cables)가 병렬을 이루므로 어법상 옳다. ⓐ는 sourced와 병렬을 이루어야 하므로 과거분사 roasted가 되어야 하는데 동사원형 roast가 쓰여 틀렸다. ⓒ는 부정어 Nor가 문두에 나와 주어와 조동사가 도치되어야 하므로 'Nor is a large corporation compelling'이 되어야 하는데 도치가 일어나지 않아 틀렸다. ⓓ는 'not due to A, but rather B' 구조에서 due to와 병렬을 이루어야 하는데 전치사 for가 삽입되어 병렬이 깨져 틀렸다. ⓕ는 not only A but also B 구문에서 changed와 시제가 일치해야 하므로 determined가 되어야 하는데 determine으로 쓰여 틀렸다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

다음 문장에서 어법상 틀린 부분을 찾아 바르게 고치고, 그 이유를 우리말로 쓰시오.
Not only the players on the basketball team but also their captain don't wear a helmet during practice. (1) 틀린 부분: _____ → (2) 틀린 이유:

solution: not only A but also B'에서는 동사가 가까운 주어에 수일치하므로 the captain에 맞춰 단수형 doesn't가 적절하다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
Volunteering at an animal shelter can be a rewarding experience for many students. ⓐIf you decide to take on this responsibility, you should try to make a genuine contribution. You are not only helping the animals ⓑand also easing the burden on the shelter staff. You should have time and energy for ⓒboth the animals and the paperwork involved in daily care. Inversely, if you have plenty of free time even after volunteering regularly, you may consider taking on more responsibilities. Therefore, keep track of how much time you can dedicate ⓓas the season changes. ⓔWhile you don't have to spend every free hour at the shelter, you should find ways to make your visits meaningful.
solution: ⓑ 'not only A but also B' 구문에서는 'but'을 써야 하는데 'and'를 사용했으므로 어법상 틀리다. ⓐ 'If'는 조건을 나타내는 접속사로 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓒ 'both A and B'는 'A와 B 둘 다'라는 뜻의 상관접속사로 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓓ 'as'는 '~함에 따라'라는 뜻의 접속사로 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓔ 'While'은 '비록 ~이지만'이라는 양보의 의미를 나타내는 접속사로 올바르게 쓰였다.

body:
다음 밑줄 친 우리말의 의미를 <조건>에 맞추어 영작하시오.
There are countless stories of successful people 역경에서 살아남았을 뿐만 아니라, 그것을 성장의 초석으로 삼았던. Fairy tale writer Hans Andersen said that his childhood poverty, the early loss of his father, and his experience of being disrespected were the sources for his most popular stories. “The hardship was a real blessing that inspired me to write stories like The Little Match Girl, The Snow Queen, and The Ugly Duckling.” Athlete Aimee Mullins also saw her challenges as an opportunity. She was born with a medical condition that resulted in losing both legs beneath the knee to surgery. She competed against athletes without disabilities in a national competition and participated in the Paralympics in 1996. Her career also includes modeling, acting, and public speaking. She says her physical condition is not a disability but the very thing that opened the door for her amazing potential. Both people succeeded not “despite” adversity but thanks to it. This is the real bouncing back. You might think “Hey, these are exceptional people.” However, we are all born with the potential for resilience. Just like these people, we all can develop the strength to quickly recover from a crisis that could otherwise cause lasting damage to our mental health. The good news is that resilience is like a muscle. You can build it up through practice, by developing thoughts, behaviors, and habits that allow you to recover from painful or stressful events. Here are three basic strategies to build up this “resilience muscle.” 실전 학습
조건 1. 상관접속사 구문을 사용할 것
2. <보기>의 단어를 모두 활용할 것 (필요시 단어 추가 및 형태 변화
3. 14단어로 쓸 것
4. 대문자 및 마침표에 유의하여 쓸 것
5. 관계대명사를 활용할 것 (that은 사용금지)
보기 adversity / growth / use / as / survive / stepping
→
answer: who not only survived adversity but used it as a stepping stone to growth
solution: 선행사 people을 수식하는 주격 관계대명사 who로 절을 시작한다 (that은 조건상 사용 금지). 이어서 'not only A but B(A뿐만 아니라 B도)' 상관접속사 구문을 사용하여, A 자리에 '역경에서 살아남았다(survived adversity)'를 쓴다. B 자리에는 '그것을 성장의 초석으로 삼았다'를 쓰는데, 이때 '그것'은 앞서 언급된 adversity를 가리키는 대명사 it으로 받아 'used it as a stepping stone to growth'로 완성한다. 목적어 it을 빠뜨리면 used가 목적어 없는 불완전한 타동사가 되므로 반드시 포함해야 한다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 밑줄 친 that과 문법적 쓰임이 같은 것은?
Our mindset, or way of thinking, affects our ability to deal with life’s challenges. Psychologists say that there are two main mindsets: “fixed” and “growth.” For people with a fixed mindset, failure just shows that their intelligence, abilities, and talents are limited. They may think, for example, “I’ve never been good at writing. I’ll never be a good writer.” Therefore, they stay in their comfort zone, where they won’t be challenged. They tend to reject even constructive criticism. Also, other people’s success makes them feel defeated and lose confidence.
choices: The book that I borrowed from the library is due tomorrow.
She was so exhausted that she fell asleep on the couch.
I believe that honesty is the most important value in life.
This is the exact reason that made him change his mind.
The moment that we first met is still vivid in my memory.
solution: 밑줄 친 that은 동사 say의 목적어절의 역할로 완전한 절 'there are two main mindsets'을 이끄는 명사절 접속사이다. ③ 동사 believe의 목적어 역할을 하는 완전한 절 'honesty is the most important value in life'을 이끄는 명사절 접속사이므로 밑줄 친 that과 쓰임이 같다. ① 선행사 The book을 수식하며, 뒤에 목적어가 빠진 불완전한 절 'I borrowed from the library'이 이어지는 목적격 관계대명사이므로 쓰임이 다르다. ② 'so ~ that(너무 ~해서 …하다)' 구문의 결과를 나타내는 접속사이므로 쓰임이 다르다. ④ 선행사 reason을 수식하며, 뒤에 주어가 빠진 불완전한 절 'made him change his mind'이 이어지는 주격 관계대명사이므로 쓰임이 다르다. ⑤ 선행사 The moment을 수식하며, 뒤에 완전한 절이 이어지지만 시간을 나타내는 선행사를 받아 '~했던 순간'이라는 의미의 관계부사적 용법으로 that이 when을 대신으로 쓰였으므로, 명사절 접속사와는 쓰임이 다르다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

I am not saying that these strategies are easy or remove all stress and suffering. Still, I urge you
ⓐ to practice them whenever you can, particularly when you are under stress. This week’s topic in the City Wellness Center Newsletter is ⓐresilient, or “the power to

As I approach the back of the store for water bottles, I realize ⓐthat I am too late. The shelves are already empty. I manage my way to the side aisle, trying my luck. Sometimes people place
ⓑunwanted items in the wrong shelves. Lucky! I find a single case of water that someone abandoned there maybe yesterday, when it wasn't such a precious commodity. I reach out, only to find a woman pulling ⓒit away at the last second. She stacks the single case of water on top of her cart like a crown on top of her canned goods. "I'm sorry, but we were here first," she says. And then her daughter steps forward – a girl I recognize from soccer – Hali Hartling. Her mother ⓓpulling their cart away, Hali leans closer to me. "I'm sorry about that. Alyssa." "Didn't I share my water with you at the practice last week?" I point out to her. "Maybe you could return the favor and share a few bottles with me." She looks back to her mother, who's already moving down the aisle, then turns back to me shaking her head. And then she gets a little bit red in the face, and ⓔturning to leave before it becomes a deep flush.

→모두가 과학을 접할 수 있도록 돕는 폴드스코프 같은 도구는 점점 더 중요해지고 있다.
solution: 정답: which, accessible

body:
다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
Microscopes have been an essential tool for science for over 400 years. ⓐIf microscopes are not invented, we might not have discovered bacteria or the microscopic structures of living organisms. In certain areas of the world, however, even basic light microscopes are not accessible due to their cost. ⓑIt was the Foldscope that Manu Prakash and Jim Cybulski presented it as a solution to the problem. The Foldscope, a paper microscope they invented, achieved powerful magnification, and cost less than a dollar in parts. “The idea has been to make science accessible to everybody,” said Prakash.
ⓒWhile researching methods for identifying infectious diseases in Thailand in 2011, Prakash came across an expensive microscope that was meant for malaria testing but was unused. Malaria takes over half a million lives annually, so early diagnosis is crucial in preventing its spread. But then, why was the microscope sitting unused? Prakash found that there were multiple reasons. The microscope was bulky and awkward to transport, required training to operate, and was difficult to maintain. As it was a delicate and expensive instrument, even trained lab workers felt nervous about using it. Prakash began wondering. A cheap, strong microscope could save thousands of lives. ⓓAfter he returned to Stanford University, which he was a professor, he started to reflect on the idea.
ⓔIt was not until he met Jim Cybulski who his idea of an affordable and accessible microscope began to take shape. A graduate student at Stanford, Cybulski was looking for ways to apply his engineering background
(A)to make a difference in the real world. After hearing Prakash’s vision, Cybulski quickly recognized its potential and was eager to contribute. For a microscope (B)to function properly, it must meet certain minimum requirements. These include an eyepiece, a tube through which the viewer looks, and a lens for magnification. The microscope must also have a component that can hold a specimen and move from side to side to explore different areas of the specimen. Furthermore, a mechanism (C)to bring the specimen into focus, usually accomplished by moving it closer to or farther from the lens, is necessary. Finally, a light source is required (D)to illuminate the specimen. 실전 모의고사 1회차 An ideal microscope would be made with the best performing materials and mechanisms for each component. However, such a microscope would likely be enormously expensive. On the other hand, a cheap microscope may not be able to deliver high performance.
Prakash and Cybulski experimented with various designs and materials (E)to find a suitable compromise. While many manufacturers might have settled for a middle ground between these two extremes, Prakash and Cybulski were determined to create a microscope that was both inexpensive and high-performing, while remaining accessible to all.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)~(E) 중, to-v의 쓰임이 나머지와 다른것은?
solution: ③ to bring은 명사를 수식하는 형용사적 용법으로 쓰였다. 나머지는 모두 부사적 용법으로 쓰였다.

body:
다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
The Foldscope provides a magnification of 140 times, making it capable of examining blood cells, bacteria, and single-celled organisms. It is incredibly portable, weighs just 8 grams, fits easily in a pocket, and requires no (A)
[internal / external] power source. Moreover, the Foldscope is built to last, capable of (B) [surviving / reviving] a three-story fall. Its usefulness is further enhanced by its (C) [susceptibility / compatibility] with phone cameras, allowing users to take pictures and record images of the specimen. It is also possible to project a high-resolution image on a wall using the phone light. It is no surprise that over 1.8 million Foldscopes have been distributed in over 160 countries, (가) _____ . The Foldscope has been utilized for various purposes beyond malaria diagnosis.
In Nigeria, it has also been instrumental in detecting fake antimalarial drugs. The drugs are responsible for over 100,000 deaths annually in sub-Saharan Africa, mostly among children under five. When crushed into powder and examined under a Foldscope, real drugs appear as uniform particles, ⓐwhile fake drugs appear as mere powder. Furthermore, over 400 scientific papers have been published using Foldscope data, and around 1,200 projects are currently in progress in India. In the United States, Foldscope programs in public libraries have introduced many children to the wonders of science. If Prakash and Cybulski gave up on their idea of the Foldscope, these achievements could not occur.

body:
다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
We are all born with the potential for resilience, the strength to recover quickly from crises that might otherwise damage our mental health. The good news is that resilience is like a muscle: you can strengthen it through practice by developing thoughts, behaviors, and habits that help you bounce back from painful or stressful events. Here are three basic strategies to build this "resilience muscle." First, accept adversity as a natural part of life. This does not mean being passive, but realizing that some changes bring suffering or stress. Instead of feeling singled out and asking, "Why me?", face what happens and focus on what you can change, not what you cannot. Seeing challenges as opportunities for learning allows adversity to become the starting point of future success. Second, have "me time," personal time to look after yourself and stay in the present, without regretting the past or worrying about the future. You might walk, meditate, write, draw, listen to music, or exercise. Third, stay connected. Ask for help from trusted people such as friends, family members, or counselors. Talking about your problems can give you clearer insight and greater strength. Good communication and strong support networks make people more resilient.
choices: practical strategies for building resilience in everyday life
reasons why people easily break down under stress
differences between emotional and physical resilience
the negative effects of worrying about the future too much
how modern society discourages people from asking for help 실전 모의고사 1회차

다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
For a microscope to function properly, it must meet certain minimum requirements. These include an eyepiece, a tube through which the viewer looks, and a lens for magnification. The microscope must also have a component that can hold a specimen and move from side to side to explore different areas of the specimen. Furthermore, a mechanism to bring the specimen into focus, usually accomplished by moving it closer to or farther from the lens, is necessary. Finally, a light source is required to illuminate the specimen. An ideal microscope would be made with the best performing materials and mechanisms for each component. However, such a microscope would likely be enormously expensive. On the other hand, a cheap microscope may not be able to deliver high performance. Prakash and Cybulski experimented with various designs and materials in order to find a suitable compromise. While many manufacturers might have settled for a middle ground between these two extremes, Prakash and Cybulski were determined to create a microscope that was both inexpensive and high-performing, while remaining accessible to all. After drawing various designs on paper, Prakash and Cybulski realized that paper could be an excellent medium for their microscope. It was cheap, easy to cut and fold with precision, and widely available. They faced many challenges during their attempts to develop the perfect design. Ultimately, they settled on waterproof cardboard paper with a small glass ball lens and named their invention the Foldscope.

body:
다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
For a microscope to function properly, it must meet certain minimum requirements. These include an eyepiece, a tube through which the viewer looks, and a lens for magnification. The microscope must also have a component that can hold a specimen and move from side to side to explore different areas of the specimen. Furthermore, a mechanism to bring the specimen into focus, usually accomplished by moving it closer to or farther from the lens, is necessary. Finally, a light source is required to illuminate the specimen. An ideal microscope would be made with the best performing materials and mechanisms for each component. However, such a microscope would likely be enormously expensive. On the other hand, a cheap microscope may not be able to deliver high performance. Prakash and Cybulski experimented with various designs and materials in order to find a suitable compromise. While many manufacturers might have settled for a middle ground between these two extremes, Prakash and Cybulski were determined to create a microscope that was both inexpensive and high-performing, while remaining accessible to all. After drawing various designs on paper, Prakash and Cybulski realized that paper could be an excellent medium for their microscope. It was cheap, easy to cut and fold with precision, and widely available. They faced many challenges during their attempts to develop the perfect design. Ultimately, they settled on waterproof cardboard paper with a small glass ball lens and named their invention the Foldscope.

윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: Balancing Cost and Performance: The Story Behind the Foldscope
Pricing Struggles Between The Foldscope Inventors and Manufacturers
Prakash and Cybulski: The Most Iconic Inventor Duo of Our Time
Essential Features of a Standard Light Microscope
Foldscope: The Ideal Microscope of All Time
solution: Prakash와 Cybulski가 적절한 균형점을 찾아 종이 현미경을 발명한 과정을 설명하는 내용의 글이다. 따라서 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은 ① ‘비용과 성능의 균형: Foldscope 이면의 이야기’이다.

(E) She says her physical condition is not a disability but the very thing that opened the door for her amazing potential.
solution: Hans Andersen의 역경 극복 사례를 소개하는 내용의 글이다. 주어진 문장은 운동선수 Aimee Mullins 또한 그녀의 시련을 기회로 보았다는 내용이다. 따라서 이 문장 앞에는 Andersen의 사례가 마무리되는 문장이 있어야 하고, 뒤에는 Mullins의 구체적인 시련에 관한 문장이 이어져야 한다. (B) 앞에서 Andersen의 명작 탄생 비화가 마무리되고, (B) 뒤에서 Mullins의 출생 시 신체적 조건이 설명되므로, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은 ② (B)이다.

body:
밑줄 친 단어의 영영 풀이로 적절한 것은?
While researching methods for identifying infectious diseases in Thailand in 2011, Prakash came across an expensive microscope that was meant for malaria testing but was unused. Malaria takes over half a million lives annually, so early diagnosis is crucial in preventing its spread. But then, why was the microscope sitting unused? Prakash found that there were multiple reasons. The microscope was bulky and awkward to transport, required training to operate, and was difficult to maintain. As it was a delicate and expensive instrument, even trained lab workers felt nervous about using it. Prakash began wondering. A cheap, strong microscope could save thousands of lives. After he returned to Stanford University, where he was a professor, he started to reflect on the idea. It was not until he met Jim Cybulski that his idea of an affordable and accessible microscope began to take shape. A graduate student at Stanford, Cybulski was looking for ways to apply his engineering background to make a difference in the real world. After hearing Prakash’s vision, Cybulski quickly recognized its potential and was eager to contribute.
choices: infectious : something that cannot be passed from one person to another.
diagnosis : the process of identifying a disease or condition from its signs and symptoms.
bulky : very small and easy to carry around.
affordable : extremely expensive and hard to pay for.
take shape : to disappear completely without leaving a trace. 1회차 실전 모의고사
solution: ② diagnosis (진단): '징후와 증상으로 질병이나 신체 상태를 식별하는 과정'이라는 뜻으로 영영 풀이가 정확하다. ① infectious (전염성의): 타인에게 전파될 수 없는 것이 아니라, '한 사람에게서 다른 사람에게로 전염될 수 있는(able to be passed from one person to another)'이라는 뜻이다. ③ bulky (부피가 큰, 뚱뚱한): 작고 휴대하기 쉬운 것이 아니라, '크고 무거워서 다루거나 옮기기 힘든(large and difficult to carry)'이라는 뜻이다. ④ affordable (가격이 알맞은, 감당할 수 있는): 매우 비싼 것이 아니라, '가격이 적당하여 돈을 지불할 만한(reasonably priced; cheap enough for most people to afford)'이라는 뜻이다. ⑤ take shape (형체를 갖추다, 구체화되다): 완전히 사라지는 것이 아니라, '구체적인 형태를 나타내거나 발전하기 시작하다(to start to develop into a clear or definite form)'라는 뜻이다. body:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않은 것은?
Science for All Microscopes have been an essential tool for science for over 400 years. If microscopes had not been invented, we might not have discovered bacteria or the microscopic structures of living organisms. In certain areas of the world, however, even basic light microscopes are not accessible due to their cost. It was the Foldscope that Manu Prakash and Jim Cybulski presented as a solution to the problem. The Foldscope, a paper microscope they invented, achieved powerful magnification, and cost less than a dollar in parts. “The idea has been to make science accessible to everybody,” said Prakash. While researching methods for identifying infectious diseases in Thailand in 2011, Prakash came across an expensive microscope that was meant for malaria testing but was unused. Malaria takes over half a million lives annually, so early diagnosis is crucial in preventing its spread. But then, why was the microscope sitting unused? Prakash found that there were multiple reasons. The microscope was bulky and awkward to transport, required training to operate, and was difficult to maintain. As it was a delicate and expensive instrument, even trained lab workers felt nervous about using it. Prakash began wondering. A cheap, strong microscope could save thousands of lives. After he returned to Stanford University, where he was a professor, he started to reflect on the idea. It was not until he met Jim Cybulski that his idea of an affordable and accessible microscope began to take shape. A graduate student at Stanford, Cybulski was looking for ways to apply his engineering background to make a difference in the real world. After hearing Prakash’s vision, Cybulski quickly recognized its potential and was eager to contribute.
choices: Microscopes have played an important role in scientific research for more than 400 years.
The Foldscope was developed to provide an affordable alternative to conventional microscopes.
Prakash encountered an unused microscope for malaria testing while conducting research in Thailand in 2011.
The microscope Prakash found was widely used because it was inexpensive, portable, and easy to maintain.
Jim Cybulski became interested in the project because he wanted to use his engineering skills to make a positive impact on society. 1회차 실전 모의고사
solution: 본문에 따르면 Prakash가 발견한 현미경은 사용되지 않고 있었으며, 그 이유는 다음과 같다. bulky and awkward to transport (크고 운반하기 불편함) required training to operate (사용법 교육이 필요함) difficult to maintain (유지·관리가 어려움) delicate and expensive instrument (정교하고 비싼 장비) 따라서 "저렴하고, 휴대가 편리하며, 유지·관리가 쉬워 널리 사용되었다"는 ④의 내용은 본문과 일치하지 않는다.

조건 1. ⓐ는 experiment를 활용하여, 두 사람이 '다 양한 설계와 재료를 실험해 보았다'는 의미의 과거시제로 2단어로 쓸 것
2. ⓑ는 settle을 활용하여, '~로 안주했을지도 모른다'는 의미의 조동사+완료형으로 3단어로쓸 것

ⓒ _____ (4단어)
1회차 실전 모의고사
answer: ⓐ experimented with ⓑ might have settled ⓒ were determined to create
solution: ⓐ 앞뒤 문장이 모두 과거시제로 서술되며, Prakash와 Cybulski가 적절한 절충안을 찾기 위해 '다양한 설계와 재료를 실험해 보았다'는 의미이므로, 전치사 with와 결합한 동사구 experimented with가 알맞다. ⓑ 'While(반면에)'로 시작하는 양보의 부사절 안에서, 많은 제조업체들이 두 극단 사이의 중간 지점에 '안주했을지도 모른다'는 과거 사실에 대한 추측을 나타내야 하므로, 조동사 might와 현재완료 have settled가 결합한 might have settled가 알맞다. ⓒ 주절에서 Prakash와 Cybulski가 저렴하면서도 고성능인 현미경을 만들기로 '결심했다'는 의미이며, 'be determined to+동사원형(~하기로 결심하다)' 구조의 수동태이므로 were determined to create가 알맞다.

body:
다음 중 빈칸 (A)와 (B)에 공통으로 들어갈 말은?
The Foldscope provides a magnification of 140 times, making it capable of examining blood cells, bacteria, and single-celled organisms. It is incredibly portable, weighs just 8 grams, fits easily in a pocket, and requires no external power source. (A) , the Foldscope is built to last, capable of surviving a three-story fall. Its usefulness is further enhanced by its compatibility with phone cameras, allowing users to take pictures and record images of the specimen. It is also possible to project a high-resolution image on a wall using the phone light. It is no surprise that over 1.8 million Foldscopes have been distributed in over 160 countries, making it an invaluable tool for scientists worldwide. The Foldscope has been utilized for various purposes beyond malaria diagnosis. In Nigeria, it has also been instrumental in detecting fake antimalarial drugs. The drugs are responsible for over 100,000 deaths annually in sub-Saharan Africa, mostly among children under five. When crushed into powder and examined under a Foldscope, real drugs appear as uniform particles, while fake drugs appear as mere powder. (B) , over 400 scientific papers have been published using Foldscope data, and around 1,200 projects are currently in progress in India. In the United States, Foldscope programs in public libraries have introduced many children to the wonders of science. If Prakash and Cybulski had given up on their idea of the Foldscope, these achievements could not have occurred. As billions of people lack access to health care and thousands of preventable deaths occur, science is playing a crucial role in finding solutions to these challenges.Tools like the Foldscope, which make science accessible to everyone, are becoming increasingly important.
solution: (A)와 (B) 뒤의 문장은 모두 앞 문장에 새로운 장점이나 추가 정보를 덧붙이는 내용이다. (A)에서는 Foldscope의 휴대성과 가벼움을 설명한 뒤, 추가적으로 내구성이 뛰어나다는 내용을 덧붙이고 있다. (B)에서는 가짜 약 판별 사례를 설명한 뒤, 추가적으로 과학 논문과 연구 프로젝트 사례를 소개하고 있다. 따라서 두 빈칸 모두 ‘게다가, 더욱이’의 의미를 가진 첨가 표현이 들어가는 것이 자연스럽다. ② In the end : ‘결국’라는 뜻으로 결론이나 마지막 결과를 나타낼 때 사용한다. ③ As a result : ‘그 결과’라는 뜻으로 원인과 결과 관계를 나타낸다. ④ On the other hand : ‘반면에’라는 뜻으로 대조 관계를 나타낸다. ⑤ In other words : ‘즉, 다시 말해’라는 뜻으로 앞 내용을 바꾸어 설명할 때 사용한다.

다음 글을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
Whenever a new technology emerges, there are people who want to use it for the benefit of the community rather than just for themselves. When 3D printing began to be more affordable, some scientists and engineers wanted to use this technology to create artificial arms and legs for people who could not afford to buy the traditional ones. In 2014, a global community of volunteers was established for this purpose. They create artificial hands and arms for children and adults at a very low cost. They also allow anyone to access their website and download the codes for free to create hands and arms on their own using 3D printing technology. They provide resources and training, too. Scientists’ efforts to use science and technology for the benefit of people are now expanding to include animals. Recently they have used 3D printing technology to design artificial legs for animals. A global volunteer community uses 3D printing to provide (A) _____ artificial limbs to those who cannot afford traditional ones, and this mission is now (B) _____ to include animals as well.
solution: (A) 전통적인 의수족을 살 형편이 안 되는 사람들에게 '저렴한 (affordable)' 인공 팔다리를 제공한다는 내용이므로 affordable이 알맞다. (B) 이 노력이 이제 동물까지 포함하는 것으로 '확대되고 (expanding)' 있다고 했으므로 expanding이 알맞다. 따라서 ② affordable - expanding이 정답으로 가장 알맞다.

Microscopes have been an essential tool for science for over 400 years. ⓐ(현미경이 발명되지 않았다면 우리는 박테리아 를 발견하지 못했을지도 모른다 / might, if, microscopes) or the microscopic structures of living organisms. In certain areas of the world, however, even basic light microscopes are not accessible due to their cost. It was the Foldscope that Manu Prakash and Jim Cybulski presented as a solution to the problem. The Foldscope, a paper microscope they invented, achieved powerful magnification, and cost less than a dollar in parts. "The idea has been to make science accessible to everybody," said Prakash. While researching methods for identifying infectious diseases in Thailand in 2011, Prakash (A)came across an expensive microscope that was meant for malaria testing but was unused. Prakash found that there were multiple reasons. The microscope was bulky and awkward to transport, required training to operate, and was difficult to maintain.

다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
(A) It was not until he met Jim Cybulski that ⓐhis idea of an affordable and accessible microscope began to take shape. ㉠A graduate student at Stanford, Cybulski was looking for ways to apply his engineering background to make a difference in the real world. ㉡Stanford University is a prestigious one that ranks at the top in the United States. After hearing Prakash's ⓑvision, Cybulski quickly recognized ⓒits potential and was eager to contribute.
(B) For a microscope to function properly, it must meet certain minimum requirements. ㉢These include an eyepiece, a tube through which the viewer looks, and a lens for magnification. ㉣The microscope must also have a component that can hold a specimen and move from side to side to explore different areas of the specimen. Furthermore, a mechanism to bring the specimen into focus, usually accomplished by moving ⓓit closer to or farther from the lens, is necessary. Finally, a light source is required to illuminate the specimen.
(C) An ideal microscope would be made with the best performing materials and mechanisms for each component. ㉤However, such a microscope would likely be enormously expensive. On the other hand, a cheap microscope may not be able to deliver high performance. Prakash and Cybulski experimented with various designs and materials in order to find a suitable compromise. While many manufacturers might have settled for a middle ground between these two extremes, Prakash and Cybulski were determined to create ⓔa microscope that was both inexpensive and high- performing, while remaining accessible to all.

윗글 (C)의 요지로 가장 알맞은 것은?

Prakash and Cybulski tried various designs and materials to make inexpensive and high- performing microscopes.

body:
다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
ⓐAfter drawing various designs on paper, Prakash and Cybulski realized that paper could be an excellent medium for their microscope. (가)
The Foldscope provides a magnification of 140 times,
ⓑmaking it capable of examining blood cells, bacteria, and single-celled organisms. It is incredibly portable, weighs just 8 grams, fits easily in a pocket, and requires no external power source. Moreover, the Foldscope is built to last, capable of surviving a three-story fall. (나)
It was cheap, easy to cut and fold with precision, and widely available. They faced many challenges during their attempts to develop the perfect design. Ultimately, they settled on waterproof cardboard paper with a small glass ball lens and named their invention the Foldscope. (다)
Its usefulness is further enhanced by its compatibility with phone cameras, ⓒallowing users to take pictures and record images of the specimen. It is also possible to project a high-resolution image on a wall using the phone light. It is no surprise that over 1.8 million Foldscopes have been distributed in over 160 countries,
ⓓmaking it an invaluable tool for scientists worldwide. The Foldscope has been utilized for various purposes beyond malaria diagnosis. In Nigeria, it has also been instrumental in detecting fake antimalarial drugs. The drugs are responsible for over 100,000 deaths annually in sub-Saharan Africa, mostly among children under five.
ⓔWhen crushed into powder and examined under a Foldscope, real drugs appear as uniform particles, while fake drugs appear as mere powder. Furthermore, over 400 scientific papers have been published using Foldscope data, and around 1,200 projects are currently in progress in India. In the United States, Foldscope programs in public libraries have introduced many children to the wonders of science. ⒶIf Prakash and Cybulski had given up on their idea of the Foldscope, these achievements could not have occurred. As billions of people lack access to health care and thousands of preventable deaths occur, science is playing a crucial role in finding solutions to these challenges. Tools like the Foldscope, which make science accessible to everyone, are becoming increasingly important.

다음 글에 드러난 ‘I’의 심경 변화로 가장 적절한 것은?
The cart is ridiculously heavy now, and almost impossible to push. Then, a man in a business suit comes up behind us. He smiles. "Looks like you could use some help." He doesn't wait for us to answer before grabbing the cart's handle. "Thank you for helping us," I tell him. "Not a problem. We all need to help one another." He smiles again, and I return the smile. It is good to know that difficult times can bring out the best in people. I decide that one favor deserves another. "Why don't you take a bag of ice for yourself," I suggest. His smile does not fade. "I have a better idea," he says. "Why don't you take a bag of ice for yourselves, and I'll keep the rest." For a moment I think he is joking, but then realize he is serious. "Excuse me?" He is still smiling, but his eyes scare me.
solution: 도움에 감사하다가 남자의 눈빛에 두려움을 느끼는 심경 변화이므로 ③grateful(고마워하는)→afraid(두려워하는)이 정답이다.

The Foldscope, a paper microscope Manu Prakash and Jim Cybulski invented, achieved powerful magnification, and cost less than a dollar in parts. "The idea has been to make science accessible to everybody," said Prakash. While researching methods for identifying infectious diseases in Thailand in 2011, Prakash came across an expensive microscope that was meant for malaria testing but was unused. Malaria takes over half a million lives annually, so early diagnosis is crucial in preventing its spread. But then, why was the microscope sitting unused? Prakash found that there were multiple reasons. The microscope was bulky and awkward to transport, required training to operate, and was difficult to maintain. As it was a delicate and expensive instrument, even trained lab workers felt nervous about using it.
choices: Foldscope는 강력한 배율을 구현하면서도 부품 가격이 1달 러도 안 되었다.

현미경은 섬세하고 값비싼 장비였기 때문에 숙련된 직원들 만 그것을 사용했다.
solution: 고가의 현미경은 섬세하고 비싼 장비였기 때문에 숙련된 직원들조차 사용하기를 두려워했다고 했으므로, 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은 ⑤이다.

The hunger stones, found in rivers across central Europe, typically remain underwater. However, when droughts occur and water levels retreat, these stones become visible. The stones are significant because they bear records of the past severe droughts. Droughts cause reduced harvests, food shortages, and hunger, especially for the poor. The words on the hunger stones are believed to warn of these hardships and to urge people to be prepared. Considering the continuation of climate change, experts warn that the situation we face is not just a simple, occasional drought but a severe drought that could persist for decades. The United Nations has predicted that by 2050, 75 percent of the global population could suffer from the effects of drought unless significant action is taken to address climate change.
choices: 기아석에는 과거 심각한 가뭄에 대한 기록이 남아 있다.
가뭄은 특히 가난한 사람들에게 더 큰 피해를 준다고 설명하 고 있다.
전문가들은 현재의 가뭄이 일반적으로 매년 반복되는 자연 스러운 가뭄이라고 설명한다.
UN은 2050년까지 세계 인구의 75%가 가뭄의 영향을 받을 수 있다고 예측했다.
solution: 전문가들은 현재의 상황이 수십 년간 지속될 수 있는 심각한 가뭄이라고 경고하고 있으므로 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은 ④이다.

body:
다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
Microscopes have been an essential tool for science for over 400 years. If microscopes had not been invented, we might not have discovered bacteria or the microscopic structures of living organisms. In certain areas of the world, however, even basic light microscopes are not accessible due to their cost. It was the Foldscope that Manu Prakash and Jim Cybulski presented as a solution to the problem. The Foldscope, a paper microscope they invented, achieved powerful magnification, and cost less than a dollar in parts. "The idea has been to make science accessible to everybody," said Prakash. While researching methods for identifying infectious diseases in Thailand in 2011, Prakash came across an expensive microscope that was meant for malaria testing but was unused. Malaria takes over half a million lives annually, so early diagnosis is crucial in preventing its spread. But then, why was the microscope sitting unused?
choices: The Foldscope: Science for Everyone at Almost No Cost
Malaria and the Rise of Microscope Technology
Why Microscopes Have Been Unused in Laboratories
Bacteria Discovery: The History of Light Microscopes
How Thailand Changed the Way We Study Diseases
solution: ① Foldscope가 1달러 미만의 비용으로 누구나 과학을 접할 수 있게 한다는 내용이 글의 핵심이므로, 글의 제목으로 가장 적절하다. ② 말라리아와 현미경 기술의 발전은 글에서 언급되지 않았다. ③ 현미경이 실험실에서 사용되지 않는 이유는 도입부의 문제 제기일 뿐, 글 전체의 제목으로는 적절하지 않다. ④ 세균 발견과 광학 현미경의 역사는 배경 설명으로 잠깐 언급될 뿐, 글의 핵심 주제가 아니다. ⑤ 태국이 질병 연구 방식을 변화시켰다는 내용은 글에 언급되지 않았다.

Prakash found that there were multiple reasons. The microscope was bulky and awkward to transport, required training to operate, and was difficult to maintain. As it was a delicate and expensive instrument, even trained lab workers felt nervous about using it. Prakash began wondering. A cheap, strong microscope could save thousands of lives. After he returned to Stanford University, where he was a professor, he started to reflect on the idea. It was not until he met Jim Cybulski that his idea of an affordable and accessible microscope began to take shape. A graduate student at Stanford, Cybulski was looking for ways to apply his engineering background to make a difference in the real world. After hearing Prakash's vision, Cybulski quickly recognized its potential and was eager to contribute. 2회차 실전 모의고사 For a microscope to function properly, it must meet certain minimum requirements. These include an eyepiece, a tube through which the viewer looks, and a lens for magnification. The microscope must also have a component that can hold a specimen and move from side to side to explore different areas of the specimen.
Furthermore, a mechanism to bring the specimen into focus, usually accomplished by moving it closer to or farther from the lens, is necessary. Finally, 표본을 비추기 위한 광원이 필요하다.
An ideal microscope would be made with the best performing materials and mechanisms for each component. However, such a microscope would likely be enormously expensive. On the other hand, a cheap microscope may not be able to deliver high performance. Prakash and Cybulski experimented with various designs and materials in order to find a suitable compromise. While many manufacturers might have settled for a middle ground between these two extremes, Prakash and Cybulski were determined to create a microscope that was both inexpensive and high-performing, while remaining accessible to all.
조건 1. 수동태를 사용할 것
2. (a, light source, to illuminate, the specimen)을 모두 포함할 것
3. 주어진 단어를 모두 활용할 것
→
answer: A light source is required to illuminate the specimen.
solution: 수동태는 'be동사 + 과거분사' 형태로 표현한다. '광원이 필요하다'는 의미를 수동태로 나타내기 위해 'a light source'를 주어로 하고, be동사 'is'와 'require'의 과거분사형 'required'를 결합하여 'a light source is required'로 쓴다. '표본을 비추기 위한'은 목적을 나타내는 to부정사 'to illuminate'를 사용하며, '표본'은 'the specimen'으로 표현한다. 박스에 제공된 단어 'a', 'light source', 'to illuminate', 'the specimen'을 모두 활용하고, 수동태 조건에 따라 'is required'를 스스로 추가하여 'A light source is required to illuminate the specimen.'으로 완성한다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
After drawing various designs on paper, Prakash and Cybulski realized that paper could be an excellent medium for their microscope. It was cheap, easy to cut and fold with precision, and widely available. They faced many challenges during their attempts to develop the perfect design. Ultimately, they ⓐsettled on waterproof cardboard paper with a small glass ball lens and named their invention the Foldscope. The Foldscope provides a magnification of 140 times, making it capable of examining blood cells, bacteria, and single-celled organisms. It is incredibly portable, ⓑweighs just 8 grams, fits easily in a pocket, and requires no external power source. Moreover, the Foldscope is built to last, capable of surviving a three-story fall. Its usefulness is further enhanced by its compatibility with phone cameras, ⓒallowing users to take pictures and record images of the specimen. It is also possible to project a high- resolution image on a wall using the phone light. It is no surprise that over 1.8 million Foldscopes have been distributed in over 160 countries, making it an invaluable tool for scientists worldwide. 2회차 실전 모의고사 The Foldscope has been utilized for various purposes beyond malaria diagnosis. In Nigeria, it has also been instrumental in detecting fake antimalarial drugs. The drugs are responsible for over 100,000 deaths annually in sub-Saharan Africa, mostly among children under five.
ⓓWhen crushed into powder and examined under a Foldscope, real drugs appear as uniform particles, while fake drugs appear as mere powder. Furthermore, over 400 scientific papers have been published using Foldscope data, and around 1,200 projects are currently in progress in India. In the United States, Foldscope programs in public libraries have introduced many children to the wonders of science. If Prakash and Cybulski
ⓔgave up on their idea of the Foldscope, these achievements could not have occurred. As billions of people lack access to health care and thousands of preventable deaths occur, science is playing a crucial role in finding solutions to these challenges. Tools like the Foldscope, which make science accessible to everyone, are becoming increasingly important.
solution: ⑤ gave up → had given up 결과절에 "could not have occurred"(조동사 과거형 + have + 과거분사)가 쓰여 가정법 과거완료 구문임을 나타낸다. 가정법 과거완료에서 if절은 반드시 「had + 과거분사」 형태여야 하므로, gave up(단순 과거)을 had given up으로 고쳐야 한다. 문맥상 Prakash와 Cybulski가 과거에 아이디어를 포기했더라면이라는 과거 사실의 반대를 가정하는 것이므로 if절과 결과절 모두 가정법 과거완료로 일치시켜야 한다. 따라서 ⑤가 정답이다. ① settled on: '~로 결정하다'라는 뜻의 구동사 settle on이 과거 시제로 올바르게 쓰였다. ② weighs: Foldscope의 일반적 특성(무게)을 나타내는 현재 시제 단수 동사로 올바르게 쓰였다. ③ allowing: 앞 절 전체의 내용을 의미상 주어로 취하며 결과를 나타내는 현재분사 allowing이 올바르게 쓰였다. ④ When crushed: 주어인 real drugs(약품)가 분쇄되는 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 나타내는 과거분사 crushed가 접속사 When과 함께 올바르게 쓰였다. 다음 밑줄 친 우리말의 의미를 <조건>에 맞추어 영작하시오.
Microscopes have been an essential tool for science for over 400 years. 만약 현미경이 발명되지 않 았다면, 우리는 박테리아나 생물체의 미세한 구조를 발견하 지 못했을지도 모른다.

조건 1. 가정법 과거완료(if + 주어 + had + p.p. ~, 주 어 + 조동사의 과거형 + have + p.p.)를 사용할것
2. if절은 수동태로, 주절은 능동태로 쓸 것
3. <보기>의 단어를 모두 활용할 것 (형태 변형 가 능, 필요시 단어 추가 가능).
4. 19단어로 쓸 것
5. 대문자 및 마침표에 유의하여 쓸 것
보기 if / microscope / not / invent / we / might / not / discover / bacteria / or / microscopic / structure / living / organism
→ _____ .
answer: If microscopes had not been invented, we might not have discovered bacteria or the microscopic structures of living organisms.
solution: 만약 ~하지 않았다면, …했을지도 모른다'라는 과거 사실에 반대되는 가정을 나타내야 하므로 가정법 과거완료를 사용한다. if절은 'If + 주어(microscopes) + had not been + 과거분사(invented)'로 쓰는데, 현미경이 '발명되는' 수동의 대상이므로 수동태로 쓴다. 주절은 'we might not have + 과거분사(discovered)'로 쓰고, 목적어로 'bacteria or the microscopic structures of living organisms'를 연결하여 '박테리아나 생물체의 미세한 구조'라는 의미를 완성한다.

body:
다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
Whenever a new technology emerges, there are people who want to use it for the (A) [ benefit / detriment ] of the community rather than just for themselves. When 3D printing began to be more (B) [ exorbitant / affordable ], some scientists and engineers wanted to use this technology to create artificial arms and legs for people who could not afford to buy the traditional ones. In 2014, a global community of volunteers was established for this purpose. They create artificial hands and arms for children and adults at a very low cost. They also allow anyone to access their website and download the codes for free to create hands and arms on their own using 3D printing technology. They provide resources and training, too. Scientists’ efforts to use science and technology for the benefit of people are now (C) [ shrinking / expanding ] to include animals. Recently they have used 3D printing technology to design artificial legs for animals.

(B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
Rather than pursuing personal gain, a global community and scientists utilize 3D printing technology to provide (A) _____ solutions for both humans and (B) _____ .
solution: (A) 본문에서 누구나 웹사이트에서 코드를 무료로 다운로드하고 저비용으로 인공 팔다리를 만들 수 있다고 했으므로, 장벽 없이 '접근 가능한' 솔루션을 제공한다는 의미의 accessible이 적절하다. (B) 글의 마지막 부분에서 과학자들의 이러한 이타적인 노력이 이제는 '동물들'에게까지 확장되어 의족을 디자인해주고 있다고 명시되어 있으므로 'animal'이 적절하다.

solution: (A) 개인적 이익보다는 공동체 전체를 위한 기술의 긍정적인 쓰임을 다루므로 'benefit'이 적절하다. (B) 기존의 비싼 의족을 살 수 없는 사람들을 돕는 내용이 나오므로, 3D 프린팅의 가격이 '저렴해졌을 때'라는 맥락이 되어야 하므로 'affordable'이 적절하다. (C) 도움의 손길이 사람에 그치지 않고 '동물까지 포함하는 것'으로 범위가 넓어지고 있으므로 'expanding'이 적절하다.

Whenever a new technology emerges, there are people who want to use it for the (A) [ benefit / detriment ] of the community rather than just for themselves. When 3D printing began to be more (B) [ exorbitant / affordable ], some scientists and engineers wanted to use this technology to create artificial arms and legs for people who could not afford to buy the traditional ones. They also allow anyone to access their website and download the codes for free to create hands and arms on their own using 3D printing technology. They provide resources and training, too.
