다음 글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문을 모두 고르면? (정답 2 개)
Microscopes have been an essential tool for science for over 400 years. If microscopes had not been invented, we might not have discovered bacteria or the microscopic structures of living organisms. In certain areas of the world, however, even basic light microscopes are not accessible due to their cost. It was the Foldscope that Manu Prakash and Jim Cybulski presented as a solution to the problem. The Foldscope, a paper microscope they invented, achieved powerful magnification, and cost less than a dollar in parts. “The idea has been to make science accessible to everybody,” said Prakash. While researching methods for identifying infectious diseases in Thailand in 2011, Prakash came across an expensive microscope that was meant for malaria testing but was unused. Malaria takes over half a million lives annually, so early diagnosis is crucial in preventing its spread. But then, why was the microscope sitting unused?
① How long have microscopes been used as a tool in science?
② What material was primarily used to make the Foldscope?
③ In what year did Prakash come across the unused, expensive microscope?
④ How many Foldscopes were distributed in Thailand by the end of 2011?
⑤ What was the total budget allocated for the Foldscope research project?
solution: ④ 2011년 말까지 태국에 배포된 Foldscope의 개수는 본문에 전혀 언급되지 않았으므로 답할 수 없다. ⑤ Foldscope 연구 프로젝트에 배정된 총예산 규모는 본문에서 전혀 다루지 않으므로 답할 수 없다. ① 현미경이 400년 넘게 과학의 필수 도구였다고 명시되어 있으므로 답할 수 있다. ② Foldscope가 '종이(paper)' 현미경이라고 명시되어 있으므로 답할 수 있다. ③ Prakash가 방치된 현미경을 발견한 시점이 2011년이라고 명시되어 있으므로 답할 수 있다.

choices: The Foldscope was invented by Manu Prakash working entirely alone.
Basic light microscopes remain unaffordable for some regions of the world.
The Foldscope failed to achieve meaningful magnification despite its low cost.
Prakash discovered bacteria for the first time while testing the Foldscope.
The expensive microscope Prakash found was specifically designed for treating malaria.
solution: ② 특정 지역에서는 비용 때문에 기본 광학 현미경조차 접근할 수 없다고 명시했으므로 일치한다. ① Foldscope는 Prakash와 Cybulski가 함께 발명했다고 했으므로, 혼자 발명했다는 설명은 일치하지 않는다. ③ Foldscope는 '강력한 배율을 달성했다고(achieved powerful magnification)' 명시했으므로 일치하지 않는다. ④ Prakash가 Foldscope로 박테리아를 처음 발견했다는 내용은 본문에 없으며, 박테리아 발견은 현미경 발명 전반에 대한 일반적 언급일 뿐이므로 일치하지 않는다. ⑤ 그 현미경은 '치료(treating)'가 아니라 말라리아 '검사 (testing)'를 위한 것이었으므로 일치하지 않는다.

다음 밑줄 친 부분 중 글의 흐름상 어휘의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것을 모두 고르면? (정답 2개)
Microscopes have been an ⓐvital tool for science for over 400 years. If microscopes had not been invented, we might not have discovered bacteria or the microscopic structures of ⓑliving organisms. In certain areas of the world, however, even basic light microscopes are not accessible due to their cost. It was the Foldscope that Manu Prakash and Jim Cybulski presented as a solution to the problem. The Foldscope, a paper microscope they invented, achieved powerful magnification, and cost
ⓒmore than a dollar in parts. “The idea has been to make science accessible to everybody,” said Prakash. While researching methods for identifying infectious diseases in Thailand in 2011, Prakash came across an expensive microscope that was meant for malaria testing but was ⓓutilized. Malaria takes over half a million lives annually, so early diagnosis is crucial in preventing its
ⓔspread. But then, why was the microscope sitting unused?
solution: ⓒ more than → less than 바로 뒤에서 Prakash가 '과학을 모두에게 접근 가능하게 만드는 것이 목표였다'고 말하는 흐름과, Foldscope가 저비용 해결책으로 제시되었다는 문맥상, 부품 비용이 '1달러 이상'이 아니라 '1달러 미만'이어야 알맞다. ⓓ utilized → unused 바로 뒤 문장에서 '그렇다면 왜 그 현미경은 사용되지 않은 채 방치되어 있었을까?(why was the microscope sitting unused?)'라는 질문이 이어지므로, 앞 문장에서도 그 현미경이 '활용되었다(utilized)'가 아니라 '사용되지 않았다 (unused)'고 해야 문맥이 일관된다. ⓐ vital: 필수적인 ⓑ living: 살아있는 ⓔ spread: 확산

body:
다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
After drawing various designs on paper, Prakash and Cybulski realized that paper could be an excellent medium for their microscope. ⓐIt was cheap, easy to cut and fold with precision, and widely available. They faced many challenges while their attempts to develop the perfect design. Ultimately, they settled on waterproof cardboard paper with a small glass ball lens and named their invention the Foldscope. The Foldscope provides a magnification of 140 times, making ⓑit capable of examining blood cells, bacteria, and single-celled organisms. ⓒIt is incredibly portable, weighs just 8 grams, fits easily in a pocket, and requires no external power source. Moreover, the Foldscope is built to last, capable of surviving a three-story fall. Its usefulness is further enhanced by ⓓits compatibility with phone cameras, allowing users take pictures and record images of the specimen. It is also possible to project a high- resolution image on a wall using the phone light. ⓔIt is no surprise that over 1.8 million Foldscopes have been distributed in over 160 countries, making it an invaluable tool for scientists worldwide.

In certain areas of the world, (A) _____ , even basic light microscopes are not accessible due to their cost. It was the Foldscope that Manu Prakash and Jim Cybulski presented as a solution to the problem. "The idea has been to make science accessible to everybody," said Prakash. While researching methods for identifying infectious diseases in Thailand in 2011, Prakash came across an expensive microscope that was meant for malaria testing but was unused. (C) , malaria takes over half a million lives annually, so early diagnosis is crucial in preventing its spread. But then, why was the microscope sitting unused?
solution: (A) 앞 문단에서 현미경이 과학의 필수 도구였다는 긍정적 진술이 나온 뒤, 뒤에서는 일부 지역에서 기본 현미경조차 접근할 수 없다는 상반된 상황이 이어지므로, 대조를 나타내는 'Nevertheless(그럼에도 불구하고)'가 알맞다. (B) 앞 문장에서 Foldscope가 '해결책으로 제시되었다'는 일반적 진술이 나온 뒤, 뒤에서는 그것이 구체적으로 어떤 성능과 비용을 달성했는지 부연 설명하므로, 구체화를 나타내는 'In particular(구체적으로 말하면)'가 알맞다. (C) 앞 문장에서 말라리아 검사용 현미경이 방치되어 있었다는 사실이 나온 뒤, 뒤에서는 말라리아의 심각성(연간 50만 명 이상 사망)을 제시하며 그 방치가 왜 문제인지를 뒷받침하므로, 강조·부연을 나타내는 'Indeed(실제로)'가 알맞다. 따라서, ① Nevertheless - In particular - Indeed 가 정답으로 가장 알맞다.

body:
다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
For a microscope to function properly, it must meet certain minimum requirements. These include an eyepiece, a tube through which the viewer looks, and a lens for magnification. The microscope must also have a component that can hold a specimen and move from side to side to explore different areas of the specimen. Furthermore, a mechanism to bring the specimen into focus, usually accomplished by moving it closer to or farther from the lens, is necessary. Finally, a light source is required to illuminate the specimen. An ideal microscope would be made with the best performing materials and mechanisms for each component. However, such a microscope would likely be enormously expensive. On the other hand, a cheap microscope may not be able to deliver high performance. Prakash and Cybulski experimented with various designs and materials in order to find a suitable (A) [compromise / competition]. While many manufacturers might have settled for a middle ground between these two extremes, Prakash and Cybulski were determined to create a microscope that was both (B) [inexpensive / exorbitant] and high-performing, while ⓐremaining accessible to all. After drawing various designs on paper, Prakash and Cybulski realized that paper could be an excellent medium for their microscope. It was cheap, easy to cut and fold with precision, and widely available. They faced many (C) [breakthroughs / challenges] during their attempts ⓑto develop the perfect design. Ultimately, they ⓒsettled on waterproof cardboard paper with a small glass ball lens and ⓓnaming their invention the Foldscope.

( ), _____ → 이유:
answer: ⓓ naming→ named 주어 'they' 뒤에 동사 'settled on'과 'named'가 'and'를 통 해 병렬구조로 이어져 있으므로 'named'가 적절하다.

body:
다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
For a microscope to function properly, it must meet certain minimum requirements. These include an eyepiece, a tube through which the viewer looks, and a lens for magnification. The microscope must also have a component that can hold a specimen and move from side to side to explore different areas of the specimen. Furthermore, a mechanism to bring the specimen into focus, usually accomplished by moving it closer to or farther from the lens, is necessary. Finally, a light source is required to illuminate the specimen. An ideal microscope would be made with the best performing materials and mechanisms for each component. However, such a microscope would likely be enormously expensive. On the other hand, a cheap microscope may not be able to deliver high performance. Prakash and Cybulski experimented with various designs and materials in order to find a suitable (A) [compromise / competition]. While many manufacturers might have settled for a middle ground between these two extremes, Prakash and Cybulski were determined to create a microscope that was both (B) [inexpensive / exorbitant] and high-performing, while ⓐremaining accessible to all. After drawing various designs on paper, Prakash and Cybulski realized that paper could be an excellent medium for their microscope. It was cheap, easy to cut and fold with precision, and widely available. They faced many (C) [breakthroughs / challenges] during their attempts ⓑto develop the perfect design. Ultimately, they ⓒsettled on waterproof cardboard paper with a small glass ball lens and ⓓnaming their invention the Foldscope.

Whenever a new technology emerges, there are people who want to use it for the benefit of the community rather than just for themselves. When 3D printing began to be more affordable, some scientists and engineers wanted to use this technology to create artificial arms and legs for people who could not afford to buy the traditional ones. In 2014, a global community of volunteers was established for this purpose. They create artificial hands and arms for children and adults at a very low cost. Scientists’ efforts to use science and technology for the benefit of people are now expanding to include animals. Recently they have used 3D printing technology to design artificial legs for animals.

다음 글의 주제를 나타내는 문장이 되도록 <보기>의 어구 를 모두 활용하여 배열하시오. (필요시 형태 변형 가능)
Whenever a new technology emerges, there are people who want to use it for the benefit of the community rather than just for themselves. When 3D printing began to be more affordable, some scientists and engineers wanted to use this technology to create artificial arms and legs for people who could not afford to buy the traditional ones. In 2014, a global community of volunteers was established for this purpose. They create artificial hands and arms for children and adults at a very low cost. They also allow anyone to access their website and download the codes for free to create hands and arms on their own using 3D printing technology. They provide resources and training, too. Scientists’ efforts to use science and technology for the benefit of people are now expanding to include animals. Recently they have used 3D printing technology to design artificial legs for animals.
보기 volunteers / use / how / 3D printing technology / to provide / affordable artificial limbs / for both people and animals 자원봉사자들이 사람과 동물 모두를 위해 저렴한 인공 팔다리 를 제공하기 위해 3D 프린팅 기술을 어떻게 사용하는지
→ .
answer: how volunteers use 3D printing technology to provide affordable artificial limbs for both people and animals
solution: 의문사 'how(어떻게)'로 명사절을 시작하고, 주어 'volunteers'와 동사 'use'를 연결한다. 그 목적어로 '3D printing technology'를 쓴 뒤, 목적을 나타내는 to부정사구 'to provide affordable artificial limbs(저렴한 인공 팔다리를 제공하기 위해)'를 이어 쓴다. 마지막으로 그 대상을 나타내는 'for both people and animals(사람과 동물 모두를 위해)'를 배열하여 문장을 완성한다.

While researching methods for identifying infectious diseases in Thailand in 2011, Prakash came across an expensive microscope that was meant for malaria testing but was unused. Malaria takes over half a million lives annually, so early diagnosis is crucial in preventing its spread. But then, why was the microscope sitting unused? Prakash was baffled at first but he found that there were multiple reasons behind it. The microscope was bulky and awkward to transport, required training to operate, and was difficult to maintain. As it was a delicate and expensive instrument, even trained lab workers felt nervous about using it. Prakash thought that a cheap, strong microscope could save thousands of lives. After he returned to Stanford University, where he was a professor, he started to reflect on the idea. He ensured he could make it.
solution: Prakash는 고가의 현미경이 방치된 것에 당황했으나, 저렴한 현미경이 생명을 구할 수 있다는 생각에 영감을 받았으므로, 심경 변화로 가장 적절한 것은 ① ‘어리둥절한 → 영감을 받은’ 이다.

The Foldscope has been utilized for various purposes beyond malaria diagnosis. In Nigeria, it has also been instrumental in detecting fake antimalarial drugs. The drugs are responsible for over 100,000 deaths annually in sub-Saharan Africa, mostly among children under five. When crushed into powder and examined under a Foldscope, real drugs appear as uniform particles, while fake drugs appear as mere powder. Furthermore, over 400 scientific papers have been published using Foldscope data, and around 1,200 projects are currently in progress in India. In the United States, Foldscope programs in public libraries have introduced many children to the wonders of science. If Prakash and Cybulski had given up on their idea of the Foldscope, these achievements could not have occurred.

After drawing various designs on paper, Prakash and Cybulski realized that paper could be an excellent medium for their microscope. ⓐIt was cheap, easy to cut and fold with precision, and widely available. They faced many challenges during their attempts to develop the perfect design. Ultimately, they settled on waterproof cardboard paper with a small glass ball lens and named their invention the Foldscope. The Foldscope provides a magnification of 140 times, making ⓑit capable of examining blood cells, bacteria, and single-celled organisms. It is incredibly portable, weighs just 8 grams, fits easily in a pocket, and requires no external power source. Moreover, the Foldscope is built to last, capable of surviving a three-story fall. ⓒIts usefulness is further enhanced by its compatibility with phone cameras, allowing users to take pictures and record images of the specimen. It is also possible to project a high- resolution image on a wall using the phone light. It is no surprise that over 1.8 million Foldscopes have been distributed in over 160 countries, making ⓓit an invaluable tool for scientists worldwide. The Foldscope has been utilized for various purposes beyond malaria diagnosis. In Nigeria, ⓔit has also been instrumental in detecting fake antimalarial drugs.

밑줄 친 단어의 영영 풀이로 잘못된 것은?
Science for All Microscopes have been an essential tool for science for over 400 years. If microscopes had not been invented, we might not have discovered bacteria or the microscopic structures of living organisms. In certain areas of the world, however, even basic light microscopes are not accessible due to their cost. It was the Foldscope that Manu Prakash and Jim Cybulski presented as a solution to the problem. The Foldscope, a paper microscope they invented, achieved powerful magnification, and cost less than a dollar in parts. “The idea has been to make science accessible to everybody,” said Prakash.
choices: microscope : a small tool used to cut paper or fabric.
structure : the way in which parts of something are arranged or organized.
organism : a living thing, such as an animal, plant, or bacteria.
accessible : able to be reached or used easily.
magnification : the process of making an object appear larger than it really is.
solution: ① microscope (현미경): 종이나 천을 자르는 도구가 아니라, '육안으로 볼 수 없는 아주 작은 물체나 생물을 확대해서 보여주는 광학 기구(A device that uses lenses to make very small objects look larger)'를 뜻합니다. (선택지의 설명은 가위나 칼에 가깝다.) ② structure (구조): 어떤 것의 여러 부분이 배열되거나 조직되어 있는 방식으로 올바른 풀이다. ③ organism (유기체, 생물): 동물, 식물, 박테리아와 같이 살아 있는 생명체를 뜻하므로 올바른 풀이다. ④ accessible (이용 가능한, 접근하기 쉬운): 쉽게 도달하거나 사용할 수 있는 상태를 뜻하므로 올바른 풀이다. ⑤ magnification (확대): 물체를 실제보다 더 크게 보이게 만드는 과정이나 기능으로 올바른 풀이다.

(해석: 만약 현미경이 발명되지 않았다면, 우리는 박테리아나 살아 있는 생물의 미세한 구조를 발견하지 못했을 것이 다.) ⓐ In certain areas of the world, however, even basic light microscopes are not accessible due to their cost. ⓑ It was the Foldscope that Manu Prakash and Jim Cybulski presented as a solution to the problem. The Foldscope, a paper microscope they invented, achieved powerful magnification, and cost less than a dollar in parts. “The idea has been to make science accessible to everybody,” said Prakash. ⓒ While researching methods for identifying infectious diseases in Thailand in 2011, Prakash came across an expensive microscope that was meant for malaria testing but was unused. Malaria takes over half a million lives annually, so early diagnosis is crucial in preventing its spread. But then, why was the microscope sitting unused? ⓓ Prakash found that there were multiple reasons. The microscope was bulky and awkward to transport, required training to operate, and was difficult to maintain. As it was a delicate and expensive instrument, even trained lab workers felt nervous about using it. Prakash began wondering. A cheap, strong microscope could save thousands of lives.
After he returned to Stanford University, where he was a professor, he started to reflect on the idea. ⓔ It was not until he met Jim Cybulski that his idea of an affordable and accessible microscope began to take shape. A graduate student at Stanford, Cybulski was looking for ways to apply his engineering background to make a difference in the real world. After hearing Prakash’s vision, Cybulski quickly recognized its potential and was eager to contribute.

body:
다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
Whenever a new technology emerges, there are people who want to use it for the benefit of the community rather than just for themselves. When 3D printing began to be more affordable, some scientists and engineers wanted to use this technology to create artificial arms and legs for people who could not afford to buy the traditional ones.
(A) Scientists’ efforts to use science and technology for the benefit of people are now expanding to include animals. Recently they have used 3D printing technology to design artificial legs for animals.
(B) In 2014, a global community of volunteers was established for this purpose. They create artificial hands and arms for children and adults at a very low cost.
(C) (가) 그들은 또한 누구나 그들의 웹사이트에 접속해서 코드를 무 료로 다운로드할 수 있게 한다 to create hands and arms on their own using 3D printing technology. They provide resources and training, too.

이 글을 한 문장으로 요약하려 한다. 빈칸 (A)와 (B)에 들어 갈 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
As 3D printing technology became more (A) , scientists and volunteers began creating low-cost artificial arms and legs for people and even animals, while also providing free codes, resources, and (B) _____ to help others make them on their own.
(A)
(B)
solution: 본문에서는 3D 프린팅 기술이 더 affordable(저렴한) 해지면서 과학자들과 자원봉사자들이 저비용 의수·의족 제작 활동을 시작했다고 설명한다. 또한 누구나 직접 제작할 수 있도록 무료 코드와 자료뿐 아니라 training(훈련, 교육)도 제공한다고 언급한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 각각 affordable, training이 들어가는 것이 적절하다.

source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 4과 문법 정복 실전

(A), (B), (C)의 각 괄호 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
Landslides are very common in our country. Every spring we hear of landslides that have buried villages or roads. Such landslides cause great damage to property. Often there is loss of life. Some of these landslides might have been prevented if hillside vegetation (A)[were / had been] still intact. Landslides usually begin in mountains or hills. They collapse when the spring rains come and the wet season sets in. If the mountains or hills are covered with strong roots, the soil under the roots becomes bound with fibers. This dense network of roots acts as an anchor, (B)[holds / holding] the soil. In places in which the vegetation has been cleared, there are no roots to hold the soil back. So it slides down over the surface into the valleys (C)[and / if] they collapse. Thus we see there is a definite relationship between vegetation and landslides.
solution: (A)는 과거의 실제와 반대되는 상황을 가정하는 가정법 과거완료로, 주절에 'might have been prevented'가 쓰였으므로 조건절도 과거완료 'had been'이 되어야 한다. (B)는 앞에 이미 'acts'라는 정동사가 있으므로 접속사 없이 또 다른 정동사(holds)가 이어질 수 없고, 분사 'holding'이 결과를 나타내는 분사구문으로 쓰여야 한다. (C)는 흙이 흘러내리는 상황과 계곡이 무너지는 상황을 순차적으로 이어주는 것이므로 조건의 'if'가 아니라 등위접속사 'and'가 적절하다.

body:
다음 (A), (B), (C)의 각 괄호 안에서 어법상 옳은 표현으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
• If he (A)[exercised / had exercised] regularly, he would have stayed healthy.
• The flowers (B)[would / would not] have died if they had been watered properly.
• If you didn't check the weather forecast, there could (C)[be / have been] unexpected rain.
choices: had exercised - would not - have been
solution: (A)는 가정법 과거완료의 조건절이므로 'had exercised'가 적절하고, (B)는 적절히 물을 주었다면 꽃이 죽지 않았을 것이므로 'would not'이 적절하며, (C)는 가정법 과거의 주절에서 조동사 뒤에는 동사원형 'be'가 적절하므로 정답은 ④이다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 4과 문법 정복 실전

body:

• If she (A)[studied / had studied] harder, she would have passed the exam.
• The accident (B)[would / would not] have happened if the driver had followed traffic rules.

body:
다음 (A), (B), (C)의 각 괄호 안에서 어법상 옳은 표현으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
• If they (A)[saved / had saved] money regularly, they would have bought a house.
• The project (B)[would / would not] have succeeded if the team had worked together efficiently.
• If you hadn't backed up your files, there could
(C)[be / have been] data loss.
choices: had saved - would not - have been 교과서 문법 정복 실전 학습
solution: (A) had saved 주절에 '조동사 과거형 + have p.p.'가 쓰였으므로, 과거 사실의 반대를 가정하는 가정법 과거완료 문장이다. if절에는 'had + p.p.'인 had saved를 쓰는 것이 올바르다. (B) would 문맥상 팀이 효율적으로 함께 일했다면 프로젝트가 성공했을 것이라는 의미가 되어야 하므로, 긍정을 나타내는 would를 쓰는 것이 올바르다. (C) have been if절에 'hadn't backed up'이 쓰였으므로, 과거 사실의 반대를 가정하는 가정법 과거완료 문장이다. 주절에는 '조동사 과거형 + have p.p.'인 have been을 쓰는 것이 올바르다. YBM(박) 4과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 중 어법에 맞지 않는 두 문장을 찾아 각각 틀린 부분을 바르게 고쳐 쓰시오.
ⓐThe food that otherwise would have been wasted is distributed to shelters.
ⓑIf she had studied the map, she would find the shortcut.
ⓒIf the engineer had checked the bridge, it might be stable today.
ⓓI wish I practiced more during my time on the team. 틀린 문장 ( ) : _____ → 틀린 문장 ( ) : _____ →
answer: ⓑ: would find → would have found, ⓓ: practiced → had practiced
solution: b는 if절이 'had studied'로 가정법 과거완료인데, 주절에 현재 시점 부사가 없음에도 'would find'처럼 단순 형태로 쓰여 시제가 어긋난다. 주절은 'would have found'로 써야 한다. d는 wish 뒤에 'during my time on the team'이라는 특정 과거 시점에 대한 아쉬움을 나타내므로 과거완료 'had practiced'가 와야 하는데 단순과거 'practiced'가 쓰여 틀렸다. a는 실제로 일어난 일과 대조되는 가정법 과거완료 'otherwise would have been wasted'가 올바르게 쓰였고, c는 과거의 조건이 현재까지 영향을 미치는 혼합 가정법으로 'might be stable today'가 올바르게 쓰여 옳은 문장이다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 4과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 중 어법에 맞지 않는 두 문장을 찾아 각각 틀린 부분을 바르게 고쳐 쓰시오.
ⓐIf the rescue team had arrived sooner, the hikers might be safe now.
ⓑDocuments that otherwise would have been destroyed are preserved in the archive.
ⓒIf he had trained harder last month, he would win the championship.
ⓓI wish I studied harder during my last year in college. 틀린 문장 ( ) : _____ → 틀린 문장 ( ) : _____ →
answer: ⓒ: would win → would have won, ⓓ: studied → had studied
solution: c는 if절이 'had trained'로 과거 사실의 반대를 나타내는 가정법 과거완료인데, 주절에 now나 today 같은 현재 부사가 없음에도 'would win'처럼 단순 형태로 쓰여 시제가 어긋난다. 혼합 가정법이 아니므로 주절도 'would have won'으로 써야 한다. d는 wish 뒤에 'during my last year in college'라는 특정 과거 시점에 대한 아쉬움을 나타내므로 'had studied'와 같은 과거완료가 와야 하는데 단순과거 'studied'가 쓰여 틀렸다. a는 과거의 조건이 현재까지 영향을 미치는 혼합 가정법으로 'might be safe now'가 올바르게 쓰였고, b는 실제로 일어난 일과 대조되는 가정법 과거완료 'otherwise would have been destroyed'가 올바르게 쓰여 옳은 문장이다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 4과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장끼리 짝지어진 것은?
ⓐIf it had not been for his warning, they couldn't have avoided the accident.
ⓑIt is crucial that the team submitted the report by Monday.
ⓒHe speaks as if he had traveled across South America.
ⓓYou would be happier right now if you were less anxious.
ⓔThey would have finished the race if they trained harder.
ⓕIt is time that each employee took ownership of their tasks.
solution: b와 e가 어법상 틀린 문장이므로 정답은 ②이다. b에서 'It is crucial that' 뒤에는 당위성을 나타내는 동사원형이 와야 하므로 submit이 되어야 하는데 과거형 submitted를 써서 틀렸다. e에서 'would have finished'라는 과거완료 형태의 결과가 왔으므로 조건절도 과거완료인 'had trained'가 되어야 하는데 단순과거 trained를 써서 시제가 어긋난다. a는 'If it had not been for + 명사, S + couldn't have p.p.' 형태의 가정법 과거완료로 올바르다. c는 'as if + had p.p.'로 과거 사실과 다른 상황을 나타내는 올바른 표현이다. d는 'If + were, S + would + 동사원형' 형태의 가정법 과거로 올바르다. f는 'It is time that + S + 과거형'으로 당위성을 나타내는 올바른 표현이다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 4과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장끼리 짝지어진 것은?
ⓐIf it had not been for the storm, we could have arrived earlier.
ⓑIt is important that the manager attended the conference.
ⓒThey talk as if they had lived in Paris for years.
ⓓWe would be there right now if we were more prepared.
ⓔShe would have accepted the offer if she had more time.
ⓕIt is time that every citizen took part in the election.
solution: b와 e가 어법상 틀린 문장이므로 정답은 ⑤이다. b에서 'It is important that' 뒤에는 당위성을 나타내는 동사원형이 와야 하므로 attend가 되어야 하는데 과거형 attended를 써서 틀렸다. e에서 'would have accepted'라는 과거완료 형태의 결과가 왔으므로 조건절도 과거완료인 'had had'가 되어야 하는데 단순과거 had를 써서 시제가 어긋난다. a는 'If it had not been for + 명사, S + could have p.p.' 형태의 가정법 과거완료로 올바르다. c는 'as if + had p.p.'로 과거 사실과 다른 상황을 나타내는 올바른 표현이다. d는 'If + were, S + would + 동사원형' 형태의 가정법 과거로 올바르다. f는 'It is time that + S + 과거형'으로 당위성을 나타내는 올바른 표현이다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 4과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 중 어법상 맞는 문장의 개수는?
ⓐIf she practiced every day, she would improve quickly.
ⓑHe describes the plan as if it were flawless.
ⓒThey double-checked the equipment before the launch; otherwise, the mission could have failed disastrously.
ⓓIf the team had started the project earlier, it would be completed by now.
ⓔI wish I were more patient so that I could handle stressful situations calmly.
ⓕIf it had not been for her quick thinking, the patient would have died during the surgery.
solution: 여섯 문장 모두 어법상 올바르다. a는 가정법 과거(If+과거동사, would+동사원형)으로 현재 사실에 반대되는 상황을 올바르게 나타낸다. b는 'as if+가정법 과거(were)'로 실제와 다른 상황을 비유하는 올바른 표현이다. c는 실제로 일어난 과거 행동(double-checked) 뒤에 otherwise를 이용해 그렇지 않았다면 일어났을 과거의 결과를 'could have+p.p.'로 나타낸 올바른 문장이다. d는 'had started'라는 과거완료 조건과 현재를 나타내는 'by now'에 어울리게 결과절에서 'would be completed'를 사용하여 시제가 올바르게 일치한다. e는 'wish+가정법 과거(were)' 뒤에 'so that+could'로 현재 능력에 대한 소망을 나타내는 올바른 문장이다. f는 'If it had not been for'로 과거 사실에 반대되는 상황을 나타내고, 결과절에서도 'would have died'와 'during the surgery'라는 과거 시점이 일치하므로 올바르다. YBM(박) 4과 문법 정복 실전
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 4과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 중 어법상 맞는 문장의 개수는?
ⓐIf they left now, they would arrive before sunset.
ⓑHe behaves as if he were the manager of the store.
ⓒShe backed up her files regularly; otherwise, she would have lost all her data in the crash.
ⓓIf the scientists had discovered the vaccine sooner, thousands of lives would have been saved by now.
ⓔI wish I had studied harder so that I could pass the exam now.
ⓕIf it were not for the traffic jam, she would have arrived on time yesterday.
solution: 어법상 맞는 문장은 a, b, c로 총 3개다. a는 가정법 과거(If+과거동사, would+동사원형)으로 현재 사실에 반대되는 상황을 올바르게 나타낸다. b는 'as if+가정법 과거(were)'로 실제와 다른 상황을 비유하는 올바른 표현이다. c는 반복적으로 일어난 과거 행동(backed up) 뒤에 otherwise를 이용해 그렇지 않았다면 일어났을 과거의 결과를 'would have+p.p.'로 나타낸 올바른 문장이다. d는 'had discovered'라는 과거완료 조건에 대해 결과절에서 'would have been saved'(과거 완료 조동사) 를 쓰면서 'by now'라는 현재 시점 표현을 함께 써서 시제가 어긋난다. 'by now'와 어울리려면 'would be saved'로 써야 한다. e는 'wish+had studied'로 과거에 대한 후회를 나타냈는데, 결과절에서 'could pass...now'처럼 현재 시점을 나타내는 표현을 써서 시제가 맞지 않는다. 과거의 결과를 나타내려면 'could have passed the exam'으로 써야 한다. f는 'If it were not for'는 현재 사실에 반대되는 상황을 나타내는 표현인데 결과절에 'yesterday'라는 명백한 과거 시점이 나와 시제가 맞지 않는다. 과거 사실에 반대되는 상황을 나타내려면 'If it had not been for'를 써야 한다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 4과 문법 정복 실전

body: 밑줄 친 부분이 문법과 문맥상 틀린 것을 고르시오.
choices: If they had studied harder, they would have passed the exam.
Should you need any help, please let me know immediately.
The meeting would have been canceled but for the CEO's insistence.
She acts as if she knew everything about the subject.
The project would have succeeded if we hired more experienced workers.
solution: ⑤ hired → had hired 주절의 동사가 'would have p.p'인 것으로 보아 과거의 일을 가정하는 문장이므로 주절의 동사는 'had p.p' 형태여야 한다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 4과 문법 정복 실전

body:
주어진 문장과 밑줄 친 부분의 쓰임이 같은 것을 고르시오.
보기 It is at 7 o'clock that the movie starts.
choices: Please wait. It's safer in the lobby.
It was pneumonia that caused his death.
Lisa finds it easy to make new friends. 교과서 문법 정복 실전 학습
solution: 주어진 문장의 'It'은 'at 7 o'clock'를 강조하는 'it was ~ that' 구문에 쓰인 'it'이다. 선택지 중에서는 ④의 'It'이 'pneumonia'을 강조하는 강조구문이다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 4과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중 어법 또는 문맥상 틀린 것끼리 짝지 어진 것을 고르시오.
• If the fire ⓐspread to the forest, the damage would have been enormous.
• If they could afford it, they ⓑwould be able to buy a new house.
• But for modern medicine, many patients
ⓒwould have to suffer from diseases.
• If she had prepared better, she ⓓcould have more confidence today.
• If we had left earlier, we ⓔwould have missed the train.
• The project would have failed ⓕhad it not been for the team leader.
solution: ⓐ는 가정법 과거 완료 구문으로 'If 주어 과거완료 ~, 주어 조동사의 과거형 have 과거분사~'형태가 되어야 한다. 따라서 spread를 had spread로 고쳐야 한다. ⓔ더 일찍 떠났더라면 기차를 놓치지 않았을 것이라는 흐름이 문맥상 자연스럽다. 따라서 'would have missed'를 'wouldn't have missed'로 고쳐야 한다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 4과 문법 정복 실전

body:
주어진 문장과 밑줄 친 부분의 쓰임이 같은 것을 고르시오.
보기 It was Sarah that completed the project yesterday.
choices: It was cancer that took his life.
It's wonderful to see you again.
Please come in. It's warmer inside.
Jenny finds it difficult to concentrate on studies.
solution: 주어진 문장의 'It'은 'Sarah'를 강조하는 'it was ~ that' 구문에 쓰인 'it'이다. 선택지 중에서는 ①의 'It'이 'cancer'을 강조하는 강조구문이다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 4과 문법 정복 실전

body: 밑줄 친 부분이 문법과 문맥상 틀린 것을 고르시오.
choices: The accident could have been prevented if the driver had been more careful.
Were I in your position, I would make a different choice.
The concert would have been postponed but for the sponsor's support.
He talks as if he were the owner of the company.
She would have joined us if she finished her work earlier.
solution: ⑤ finished → had finished 주절의 동사가 'would have p.p'인 것으로 보아 과거의 일을 가정하는 문장이므로 주절의 동사는 'had p.p' 형태여야 한다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 4과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 중 어법에 맞지 않는 두 문장을 찾아 각각 틀린 부분을 바르게 고쳐 쓰시오.
ⓐI wish I visited more countries during my gap year.
ⓑIf the manager had noticed the error, the project might be on track now.
ⓒIf they had left earlier, they would catch the flight.
ⓓThe tickets that otherwise would have been wasted are given to volunteers. 틀린 문장 ( ) : _____ → 틀린 문장 ( ) : _____ →
answer: ⓐ: visited → had visited, ⓒ: would catch → would have caught
solution: a는 wish 뒤에 'during my gap year'라는 특정 과거 시점에 대한 아쉬움을 나타내므로 과거완료 'had visited'가 와야 하는데 단순과거 'visited'가 쓰여 틀렸다. c는 if절이 'had left'로 가정법 과거완료인데, 주절에 현재 시점 부사가 없음에도 'would catch'처럼 단순 형태로 쓰여 시제가 어긋난다. 주절은 'would have caught'로 써야 한다. b는 과거의 조건이 현재까지 영향을 미치는 혼합 가정법으로 'might be on track now'가 올바르게 쓰였고, d는 실제로 일어난 일과 대조되는 가정법 과거완료 'otherwise would have been wasted'가 올바르게 쓰여 옳은 문장이다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 4과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 적절한 것의 개수는?
Lucy Bennett, a retired elementary school teacher, ⓐused to call her grandchildren every weekend, but they rarely picked up the phone. One day, her son told her that the kids were busy with exams and rarely answered calls. Lucy said, “If I ⓑwill send them a letter, I will surely get a reply.” She wrote two cheerful letters to the grandchildren and mentioned that she could not but ⓒto feel excited to send each of them a surprise gift: a new bicycle voucher. Then she mailed the letters, but forgot to enclose the vouchers. Within a week she received warm letters from both grandchildren, who noted at the end that she had forgotten to include the voucher. If the voucher ⓓhad been included, would they
ⓔreply so quickly?
solution: 정답은 ②이다. ⓐ 'used to call'은 '~하곤 했다'라는 과거의 습관적 동작을 나타내는 'used to + 동사원형' 구조로 어법상 적절하다. ⓑ 'If I will send them a letter, I will surely get a reply.'에서 조건절(if절)에는 미래시제 will을 쓰지 않고 현재시제를 써야 하므로 'will send'는 'send'로 고쳐야 한다. ⓒ 'could not but to feel'에서 'cannot but + 동사원형'은 '~할 수밖에 없다'는 뜻의 관용표현으로 to가 필요 없으므로 'to feel'은 'feel'로 고쳐야 한다. ⓓ 'had been included'는 가정법 과거완료 조건절에 쓰이는 'had + p.p.' 형태로 어법상 적절하다. ⓔ 'would they reply'는 가정법 과거완료 주절에 쓰여야 하므로 'would have replied'로 고쳐야 한다. 따라서 어법상 적절한 것은 ⓐ, ⓓ 2개이다. YBM(박) 4과 문법 정복 실전
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 4과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
Strict dieting often results in a temporary change rather than a lifestyle shift. People follow restrictive plans for weeks, but once they reach their target weight, they stop exercising. The goal is ⓐno longer available to guide their choices. When all of your willpower ⓑis focused on a specific number on the scale, you may feel lost after hitting it. This explains why people find
ⓒthemselves regaining the weight they lost. Lasting health is not about any single diet ⓓbut about consistent healthy choices. It is your relationship with food ⓔwhat determines your long-term well-being.
solution: ⑤ what → that 'your relationship with food'을 강조하는 'It is/was ~ that ...' 강조 구문이 쓰인 문장으로, 'what'이 아니라 'that'이 필요하다. ① 부정어를 포함하는 관용표현인 'no longer'는 '더이상 ~ 않다'라는 의미로 문맥과 문법에 맞게 쓰였다. ② 'all'과 같이 부분이나 수량을 나타내는 표현은 'of' 뒤의 명사에 수를 일치시키는데, 'of' 뒤 'your willpower'라는 단수 명사가 왔으므로 단수 동사 'is'가 쓰인 것은 적절하다. ③ 'find'의 목적어인 'find'의 주어인 'people'과 같은 대상이므로 'find'의 목적어로 재귀대명사 'themselves'가 쓰였다. ④ 상관접속사 'not A but B'(A가 아니라 B인)로 'about'이 이끄는 전치사구가 연결되었다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 4과 문법 정복 실전

body:
빈칸에 가장 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
The documents wouldn't _____ ​ if the fire alarm had worked properly.
choices: have been destroyed 교과서 문법 정복 실전 학습
solution: 과거의 사건을 반대로 가정하고 있으므로 가정법 과거완료 (주어 + would + have p.p.)이며, 주어인 The documents가 동사 destroy의 동작을 당하는 것이므로 수동태를 써서 'have been destroyed'로 나타내야 한다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 4과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 밑줄 친 우리말의 의미를 <조건>에 맞추어 영작하시오.
Microscopes have been an essential tool for science for over 400 years. 만약 현미경이 발명되지 않았다면, 우리는 박테리아를 발견하지 못했을지도 모른 다.In certain areas of the world, however, even basic light microscopes are not accessible due to their cost. It was the Foldscope that Manu Prakash and Jim Cybulski presented as a solution to the problem.
조건 1. 가정법 과거완료(If+주어+had+p.p. ~, 주어 +조동사 과거형+have+p.p.)를 사용할 것
2. if절은 수동태로 쓸 것
3. <보기>의 단어를 모두 활용할 것 (형태 변형 가능).
4. 12단어로 쓸 것
보기 if / microscope / not / invent / we / might / not / discover / bacteria
→ _____ .
answer: If microscopes had not been invented, we might not have discovered bacteria.
solution: if절은 'If+주어(microscopes)+had not been+p.p. (invented)'로 수동태를 쓰고, 주절은 'we might not have discovered bacteria'로 완성한다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 4과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 옳은 것끼리만 짝지어진 것은?
Whenever a new technology emerges, there are people ⓐwanting to use it for the benefit of the community rather than just for themselves. When 3D printing began to be more affordable, some scientists and engineers wanted to use this technology to create artificial arms and legs for people who could not afford to buy the traditional
ⓑone. In 2014, a global community of volunteers was ⓒestablished for this purpose. They create artificial hands and arms for children and adults at a very low cost. They also allow anyone ⓓto access their website and download the codes
ⓔat free to create hands and arms on their own using 3D printing technology. They provide resources and training, too. Scientists’ efforts ⓕto using science and technology for the benefit of people are now expanding to include animals. Recently they have used 3D printing technology to design artificial legs for animals.
solution: ⓐ 선행사 people을 수식하는 현재분사로, '~하기를 원하는'이라는 능동의 의미이므로 적절하다. ⓒ 주어 a global community(단수)가 '설립되는' 수동의 대상이므로 수동태로 쓰인 것이 적절하다. ⓓ 'allow+목적어+to부정사(~하도록 허락하다)' 구조에 맞게 쓰였으므로 적절하다. ⓑ one → ones 앞서 언급된 artificial arms and legs(복수)를 대신해야 하므로, 단수 대명사 one이 아닌 복수 대명사 ones가 되어야 알맞지 않다. ⓔ at free → for free '무료로'라는 의미의 관용 표현은 at free가 아니라 for free이므로 알맞지 않다. ⓕ to using → to use 명사 efforts를 수식하는 to부정사의 형용사적 용법 자리이므로 동명사가 아닌 동사원형이 와야 알맞지 않다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 4과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 옳지 않은 것은?
The Foldscope provides a magnification of 140 times, ⓐmaking it capable of examining blood cells, bacteria, and single-celled organisms. It is incredibly portable, weighs just 8 grams, fits easily in a pocket, and requires no external power source. Moreover, the Foldscope is built ⓑto last, capable of surviving a three-story fall. Its usefulness is further enhanced by its compatibility with phone cameras, ⓒallowing users to take pictures and record images of the specimen. It is also possible ⓓto project a high-resolution image on a wall using the phone light. It is no surprise that over 1.8 million Foldscopes ⓔhas been distributed in over 160 countries, making it an invaluable tool for scientists worldwide.
solution: ⓔ has been distributed → have been distributed 주어가 over
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 4과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 옳지 않은 것은?
For a microscope ⓐto function properly, it must meet certain minimum requirements. These include an eyepiece, a tube ⓑthrough which the viewer looks, and a lens for magnification. 2. if절은 수동태로, 주절은 능동태로 쓸 것
3. <보기>의 단어를 모두 활용할 것 (형태 변형 가능, 필요시 단어 추가 가능).
4. 19단어로 쓸 것
5. 대문자 및 마침표에 유의하여 쓸 것
보기 if / microscope / not / invent / we / might / not / discover / bacteria / or / microscopic / structure / living / organism
→ _____ .
answer: If microscopes had not been invented, we might not have discovered bacteria or the microscopic structures of living organisms.
solution: 만약 ~하지 않았다면, …했을지도 모른다'라는 과거 사실에 반대되는 가정을 나타내야 하므로 가정법 과거완료를 사용한다. if절은 'If + 주어(microscopes) + had not been + 과거분사(invented)'로 쓰는데, 현미경이 '발명되는' 수동의 대상이므로 수동태로 쓴다. 주절은 'we might not have + 과거분사(discovered)'로 쓰고, 목적어로 'bacteria or the microscopic structures of living organisms'를 연결하여 '박테리아나 생물체의 미세한 구조'라는 의미를 완성한다.

body:
다음 밑줄 친 부분과 바꾸어 쓸 수 있는 문장으로 알맞지 않 은 것을 모두 고르면? (정답 2개)
Microscopes have been an essential tool for science for over 400 years. If microscopes had not been invented, we might not have discovered bacteria or the microscopic structures of living organisms. 실전 학습 In certain areas of the world, however, even basic light microscopes are not accessible due to their cost. It was the Foldscope that Manu Prakash and Jim Cybulski presented as a solution to the problem.
The Foldscope, a paper microscope they invented, achieved powerful magnification, and cost less than a dollar in parts. “The idea has been to make science accessible to everybody,” said Prakash. While researching methods for identifying infectious diseases in Thailand in 2011, Prakash came across an expensive microscope that was meant for malaria testing but was unused. Malaria takes over half a million lives annually, so early diagnosis is crucial in preventing its spread. But then, why was the microscope sitting unused?
① Had microscopes not been invented, we might not have discovered bacteria or the microscopic structures of living organisms.
② Had microscopes not been created, we might not have found bacteria or the microscopic structures of living organisms.
③ Had microscopes been created, we might have found bacteria or the microscopic structures of living organisms.
④ If microscopes had not been created, we could not have discovered bacteria or the microscopic structures of living organisms.
⑤ If microscopes wasn't created, we might discover bacteria or the microscopic structures of living organisms.
solution: ③ 밑줄 친 부분은 '현미경이 발명되지 않았다면 발견하지 못했을 것이다'라는 부정의 가정인데, ③은 not이 빠져 '발명되었다면 발견했을 것이다'라는 정반대의 의미가 되므로 바꾸어 쓸 수 없다. ⑤ 가정법 과거완료 문장이므로 if절에는 'had not been created'가 와야 하는데 단순과거 부정형 'wasn't created'가 쓰였고, 주절도 'might not have discovered'가 아닌 현재형 'might discover'가 쓰여 시제가 원문과 맞지 않으므로 바꾸어 쓸 수 없다. ① 가정법 과거완료의 'Had+주어+not+p.p.' 도치 구조이므로 바꾸어 쓸 수 있다. ② invented를 created로, discovered를 found로 바꾼 동의어 치환이며 구조는 원문과 동일하므로 바꾸어 쓸 수 있다. ④ if절 구조가 원문과 동일하고, 주절의 might를 could로 바꾼 것은 가정법에서 호환 가능한 조동사이므로 바꾸어 쓸 수 있다.
source: 영어플랫 · YBM(박) 공통영어2 4과 문법 정복 실전

다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 옳은 것은?
Whenever a new technology emerges, there are people ⓐwhich want to use it for the benefit of the community rather than just for themselves. When 3D printing began to be more affordable, some scientists and engineers wanted to use this technology ⓑcreating artificial arms and legs for people who could not afford to buy the traditional ones. In 2014, a global community of volunteers
ⓒwas established for this purpose. They create artificial hands and arms for children and adults at a very low cost. They also allow anyone ⓓaccess their website and download the codes for free to create hands and arms on their own using 3D printing technology. They provide resources and training, too. Scientists' efforts to use science and technology for the benefit of people are now expanding to include animals. Recently they have used 3D printing technology to design artificial legs for animals ⓔusing 3D printing technology.
solution: ③ ‘a global community of volunteers’의 핵심 주어는 단수 명사 community이다. 또한 2014년에 ‘설립되었다’는 수동의 의미이므로 과거 수동태 was established가 알맞다. 따라서 주어와 시제, 태가 모두 바르게 쓰인 ⓒ가 정답이다. ① which want → who want 선행사 'people'은 사람을 가리키므로 관계대명사 which가 아닌 who를 써야 한다. which는 사물·동물을 선행사로 받는 관계대명사로, 사람 선행사에는 쓸 수 없다. ② creating → to create 'wanted to use this technology' 뒤에서 '~하기 위하여'라는 목적의 의미를 나타내야 하므로 동명사가 아닌 부정사의 부사적 용법인 to create가 들어가야한다. ④ access → to access 'allow+목적어+to부정사' 구문에서 목적보어는 반드시 to부정사 형태여야 한다. 따라서 'allow anyone access'처럼 동사 원형을 쓰는 것은 틀렸으며, to access로 고쳐야 한다. ⑤ using → used 문장의 주어인 'they(과학자들)'가 직접 3D 프린팅 기술을 사용하는 것이므로 능동의 현재분사 using이 맞다. used는 수동의 의미를 나타내어 문맥상 어색하며, 'animals used 3D printing technology'의 뜻이 되어 틀렸다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
After drawing various designs on paper, Prakash and Cybulski realized that paper could be an excellent medium for their microscope. It was cheap, easy to cut and fold with precision, and widely available. They faced many challenges during their attempts to develop the perfect design. Ultimately, they ⓐsettled on waterproof cardboard paper with a small glass ball lens and named their invention the Foldscope. 실전 학습 The Foldscope provides a magnification of 140 times, making it capable of examining blood cells, bacteria, and single-celled organisms. It is incredibly portable, ⓑweighs just 8 grams, fits easily in a pocket, and requires no external power source. Moreover, the Foldscope is built to last, capable of surviving a three-story fall. Its usefulness is further enhanced by its compatibility with phone cameras, ⓒallowing users to take pictures and record images of the specimen. It is also possible to project a high- resolution image on a wall using the phone light.
It is no surprise that over 1.8 million Foldscopes have been distributed in over 160 countries, making it an invaluable tool for scientists worldwide. The Foldscope has been utilized for various purposes beyond malaria diagnosis. In Nigeria, it has also been instrumental in detecting fake antimalarial drugs. The drugs are responsible for over 100,000 deaths annually in sub-Saharan Africa, mostly among children under five.
ⓓWhen crushed into powder and examined under a Foldscope, real drugs appear as uniform particles, while fake drugs appear as mere powder. Furthermore, over 400 scientific papers have been published using Foldscope data, and around 1,200 projects are currently in progress in India. In the United States, Foldscope programs in public libraries have introduced many children to the wonders of science. If Prakash and Cybulski
ⓔgave up on their idea of the Foldscope, these achievements could not have occurred. As billions of people lack access to health care and thousands of preventable deaths occur, science is playing a crucial role in finding solutions to these challenges. Tools like the Foldscope, which make science accessible to everyone, are becoming increasingly important.
solution: ⑤ gave up → had given up 결과절에 "could not have occurred"(조동사 과거형 + have + 과거분사)가 쓰여 가정법 과거완료 구문임을 나타낸다. 가정법 과거완료에서 if절은 반드시 「had + 과거분사」 형태여야 하므로, gave up(단순 과거)을 had given up으로 고쳐야 한다. 문맥상 Prakash와 Cybulski가 과거에 아이디어를 포기했더라면이라는 과거 사실의 반대를 가정하는 것이므로 if절과 결과절 모두 가정법 과거완료로 일치시켜야 한다. 따라서 ⑤가 정답이다. ① settled on: '~로 결정하다'라는 뜻의 구동사 settle on이 과거 시제로 올바르게 쓰였다. ② weighs: Foldscope의 일반적 특성(무게)을 나타내는 현재 시제 단수 동사로 올바르게 쓰였다. ③ allowing: 앞 절 전체의 내용을 의미상 주어로 취하며 결과를 나타내는 현재분사 allowing이 올바르게 쓰였다. ④ When crushed: 주어인 real drugs(약품)가 분쇄되는 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 나타내는 과거분사 crushed가 접속사 When과 함께 올바르게 쓰였다.
